questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

It's very doable, and cheaper than the earnings-call run. I checked the sources and volumes just now.

**Source.** `open-index/hacker-news` on Hugging Face is a full HN archive (stories and comments, 2006 to present) stored as parquet. It's at revision `c54ced59`, last updated 2026-08-23, about 47M items. It carries the same license as the transcript source (ODC-BY), so it pins into a `MANIFEST.tsv` just like the transcripts. The archive stops in late August. HN's newest item ID today is 50,366,582, so the last ~10 weeks would be fetched from the official API by ID range and pinned the same way. Algolia's search API is useful for rough counts but can't be pinned, so it can't be the source.

**Volume.** Algolia comment hits by term (these overlap, and "claude" also catches people named Claude):

| Term | Comments |
|---|---|
| llm | 580,602 |
| openai | 198,725 |
| claude | 168,882 |
| chatgpt | 156,299 |
| anthropic | 132,000 |
| "ai safety" | 10,734 |

So the full AI set is roughly 1M comments. With the same 16-hypothesis codebook that's about 16M pairs per model: around 3 GPU-hours, about $6 per model on Modal, or about 25 minutes on 8 GPUs. An Anthropic-only subset (about 130k) would cost under $1. A topic map at this size is fine too.

**What carries over:**
- The term regex, the window unit, both witnesses, and the codebook: about_ai, risk vs opportunity, the 12 risk types, and governance.
- The denominator, which would be all comments per month.
- The risk time series and the risk ranking.

The analyst-question codebook doesn't fit HN and wouldn't be used.

**What's different:**

1. **Publishing.** This is the one decision that's yours. The earnings-call corpus republishes executives and analysts talking on the record. HN commenters are mostly private individuals. Committing a million of their comments with usernames to a public CC0 repo would be republishing them verbatim. I'd commit only item IDs, character offsets, BLAKE3 hashes and scores. Anyone can rebuild the text locally from the pinned archive, and `verify` still works. That keeps the method intact while the repo holds no one's words or handles.
2. **Witness accuracy will drop.** HN comments are sarcastic, quote each other and argue. Zero-shot NLI will agree less with itself than it did on calls, and the comments need their own small human-coded sample before any rate is cited.
3. **What it measures.** HN is a self-selected group of developers and practitioners. It isn't the public, and it isn't workers or users in general. That makes it a useful third voice next to executives (prepared remarks) and analysts (questions): what the people building and using these tools worry about. We could put all three on the same risk ranking side by side. If practitioners rank risks very differently from executives and analysts, that's a comparison we can cite. It doesn't fill the "unmeasured voices" gap in §7.

If you're good with IDs-only, I'll build it as `corpus/hacker-news/` on the same pattern as the earnings-call corpus, starting with extraction and counts before any GPU spend.

The gold-set coder for the analyst questions is still being built in the background. I'll pull it in and give you the full analyst-question summary when it finishes.

content.text:
The analyst-question gold sample is now in the main tree. The earlier window sample is unchanged (`7501ce64…`), and rebuilding the question sample gives the same file (`ffbd8d67…`). Here's the full analyst-question result.

## Do analysts ask AI companies about risk controls or about sales?

Mostly sales. In the last 12 months to 2026-11-04, analysts asked 1,645 AI questions on calls of 293 S&P 500 firms. A question can count under more than one heading.

| What the question is about | Share | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue and units sold | 21.2% | 348 |
| AI spending and its return | 8.7% | 143 |
| Efficiency gains | 4.7% | 78 |
| Security | 3.0% | 49 |
| Competitive threat | 2.9% | — |
| General risk | 2.9% | — |
| Workforce | 1.7% | — |
| **How AI risk is controlled or governed** | **0.8%** | **13** |
| Regulation | 0.3% | 5 |
| Harm to others | 0.2% | 3 |

A simple word count, which uses no models, points the same way: in 2026, 50.4% of AI questions use commercial words and 2.2% use oversight words.

Reading the flagged questions shows the gap is even wider than the table:

- **Many "oversight" questions are sales questions.** For example, F5: *"what are you seeing on the inbound interest and pipeline build specifically on F5 AI Guardrails… Are you seeing these customers specifically budget for AI agent security…?"* The CrowdStrike example is similar: its question about "AI governance" is about pipeline.
- **The real oversight questions treat risk as a threat to the firm's own earnings, not harm to others.** Chubb is asked about "coverage for AI liability", and about its "exposure" to data-center construction.
- **The closest to a direct controls question:** Ebrahim Poonawala to BNY: *"how do you protect against the headlines we read about rogue agents when you're all signs go in terms of deploying AI internal[ly]"*.

The chart is at `proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/intent-ttm.svg`. Every flagged question is listed verbatim in `report/oversight-questions.tsv` (141 rows).

**Caveats:**
- These shares are model proposals until a person codes the gold sample.
- The two models agree only moderately on the small categories. Agreement (Cohen's κ) runs from 0.32 for harm to 0.74 for security.
- Only questions that mention AI terms are counted.
- The S&P 500 list is today's, applied backwards, so firms that left the index are missing.

## Gold sets for a person to code

Each tool shows one passage at a time, with no model scores, and saves after every answer.

- **Earnings-call passages:** 240, stratified across time periods.
  `uv run scripts/ec_gold.py code --coder NAME`
- **Analyst questions:** 200: 100 that both models flagged for oversight, 30 that only one flagged, 30 commercial-only and 40 flagged for neither.
  `uv run scripts/ec_gold.py code --set questions --coder NAME`

To score either set, run `uv run scripts/ec_gold.py score` (add `--set questions` for the question set). The "controls" category gets only a handful of positives into the sample. If that becomes the headline, it will need a targeted extra sample.

## Not committed yet

The changes are:
- the question extraction and report scripts, plus their outputs
- the gold tool and both samples
- the `--units`/`--codebook` options in the classifier
- the README, method-doc and spec log updates

I'll leave out `__pycache__`, the worktrees and other sessions' files.

Want me to commit? And for Hacker News: comment IDs only, or also the comment text?

+    # analyst questions (§10)
+    uv run scripts/ec_questions.py build
+    uvx --with duckdb==2.0.0 --with blake3 modal run scripts/ec_classify_modal.py --model deberta \
+        --units corpus/earnings-calls/ai-questions.parquet \
+        --codebook corpus/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1.tsv --id-col question_id
+    # ...the same with --model modernbert, then:
+    uv run scripts/ec_question_report.py
+
+## 10. Analyst questions: selling AI or governing it?
+
+The test of investor oversight is what the people who price these companies
+ask them. `scripts/ec_questions.py` extracts every AI question asked in the Q&A
+by someone outside the company.
+
+- **Who counts as a questioner** is read from the call's structure, not the
+  §4 name heuristic, which mislabels executives whose names recur across firms.
+  - The questioner is introduced by the operator.
+  - The questioner never gave prepared remarks on any of that issuer's calls.
+  - The questioner asks at least one question (`?`) in the Q&A.
+
+  A pseudo-random check of 25 questions found 25 genuine analyst questions.
+- **Unit:** one questioner turn that contains an AI term and a `?` and is at
+  most 3,000 characters long. There are 4,288 such questions, out of 882,118
+  questioner turns on 33,314 calls with a detectable Q&A.
+- **Intent** is scored by the same two witnesses against
+  `codebook-questions-v0.1.tsv`:
+  - commercial (revenue, efficiency)
+  - capital (spending and its return)
+  - threat to the business
+  - workforce
+  - oversight (risks, controls, regulation, harm, security)
+
+  A deterministic word measure sits beside the witnesses as a cross-check.
+- **Same status as §5.** These are witness proposals until the question gold
+  set in `gold/earnings-calls/` is coded.
+
+Outputs are in `proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/`.
+`oversight-questions.tsv` lists every question flagged for oversight,
+verbatim.

UA = "anthropic-pbc earnings-call corpus research (github.com/ethicalcapital/anthropic-pbc)"

# Term families. `AI` is case-sensitive (avoids "ai" inside words and "Ai" names);
# the phrases are case-insensitive. Python `re` and DuckDB RE2 accept both forms.
TERMS = {
    "ai":        r"\bAI\b|\bA\.I\.|\bGenAI\b|\bAGI\b",
    "ai_phrase": r"(?i:artificial intelligence|generative ai|generative model|gen ai\b)",
    "ml":        r"(?i:machine learning|deep learning|neural net)",
    "llm":       r"\bLLMs?\b|(?i:large language model)",
    "vendor":    r"(?i:chatgpt|openai|anthropic|\bclaude\b|\bgemini\b|copilot)",
    "agentic":   r"(?i:agentic|ai agents?\b)",
}
ANY = "(" + "|".join(f"(?:{p})" for p in TERMS.values()) + ")"
TERM_RE = {k: re.compile(v) for k, v in TERMS.items()}
ANY_RE = re.compile(ANY)
SENT_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")
MAX_WINDOW = 1500     # chars; longer sentence windows are clipped around the match
CLIP_PAD = 600


def b3(s: str) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(s.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def manifest() -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="") as f:
        return {r["id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t")}


def source_path() -> Path:
    m = manifest()["transcripts"]
    return BULK / m["path"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fetch
def cmd_fetch() -> int:
    m = manifest()["transcripts"]
    dst = BULK / m["path"]
    BULK.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    if not dst.exists():
        req = urllib.request.Request(m["url"], headers={"User-Agent": UA})
        tmp = dst.with_suffix(".part")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r, tmp.open("wb") as f:
            while chunk := r.read(1 << 22):
                f.write(chunk)
        tmp.rename(dst)
    h = blake3.blake3(max_threads=blake3.blake3.AUTO)
    with dst.open("rb") as f:
        while chunk := f.read(1 << 24):
            h.update(chunk)
    got, size = h.hexdigest(), dst.stat().st_size
    if str(size) != m["bytes"] or got != m["blake3"]:
        print(f"FAIL: {dst.name} bytes={size} blake3={got}\n  manifest bytes={m['bytes']} blake3={m['blake3']}")
        return 1
    print(f"ok: {dst.name} {size} bytes blake3 {got}")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- constituents
def cmd_constituents() -> int:
    m = manifest()["sp500"]
    req = urllib.request.Request(m["url"], headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    page = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30))["query"]["pages"][0]
    rev = page["revisions"][0]
    text = rev["slots"]["main"]["content"]
    if b3(text) != m["blake3"]:
        print(f"FAIL: revision {rev['revid']} wikitext blake3 {b3(text)} != manifest {m['blake3']}")
        return 1
    section = text.split('id="constituents"', 1)[1].split("|}", 1)[0]
    rows = []
    for line in section.split("\n|-")[1:]:
        t = re.search(r"\{\{(?:NyseSymbol|NasdaqSymbol|BZX link|Cboe ticker)\|([A-Za-z.]+)", line, re.I)
        cik = re.search(r"\|\|\s*(\d{10})\s*\|\|", line) or re.search(r"\b(\d{10})\b", line)
        if t:
            rows.append((t.group(1).upper().replace(".", "-"), cik.group(1) if cik else ""))
    rows = sorted(set(rows))
    out = CORPUS / "sp500-constituents.tsv"
    with out.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(["symbol", "cik"])
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"ok: {len(rows)} constituents from wikipedia revid {rev['revid']} -> {out.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- build
def windows_for(content: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, list[str]]]:
    """Merged sentence windows (match sentence +/- 1) as [start, end) offsets."""
    bounds, pos = [], 0
    for m in SENT_END.finditer(content):
        bounds.append((pos, m.start()))
        pos = m.end()
    bounds.append((pos, len(content)))
    hits = sorted({i for i, (s, e) in enumerate(bounds) if ANY_RE.search(content, s, e)})
    spans: list[list[int]] = []
    for i in hits:
        lo, hi = max(i - 1, 0), min(i + 1, len(bounds) - 1)
        if spans and lo <= spans[-1][1] + 1:
            spans[-1][1] = max(spans[-1][1], hi)
        else:
            spans.append([lo, hi])
    out = []
    for lo, hi in spans:
        s, e = bounds[lo][0], bounds[hi][1]
        if e - s > MAX_WINDOW:  # one run-on "sentence": clip around matches, snap to spaces
            pieces = []
            for m in ANY_RE.finditer(content, s, e):
                a, b = max(m.start() - CLIP_PAD, s), min(m.end() + CLIP_PAD, e)
                if pieces and a <= pieces[-1][1]:
                    pieces[-1][1] = b
                else:
                    pieces.append([a, b])
            for a, b in pieces:
                if a > s:
                    a = content.find(" ", a, b) + 1 or a
                if b < e:
                    b = content.rfind(" ", a, b) if content.rfind(" ", a, b) > a else b
                out.append((a, b))
        else:
            out.append((s, e))
    res = []
    for s, e in out:
        seg = content[s:e]
        fam = sorted(k for k, r in TERM_RE.items() if r.search(seg))
        if fam:
            res.append((s, e, fam))
    return res

# Term families. `AI` is case-sensitive (avoids "ai" inside words and "Ai" names);
# the phrases are case-insensitive. Python `re` and DuckDB RE2 accept both forms.
TERMS = {
    "ai":        r"\bAI\b|\bA\.I\.|\bGenAI\b|\bAGI\b",
    "ai_phrase": r"(?i:artificial intelligence|generative ai|generative model|gen ai\b)",
    "ml":        r"(?i:machine learning|deep learning|neural net)",
    "llm":       r"\bLLMs?\b|(?i:large language model)",
    "vendor":    r"(?i:chatgpt|openai|anthropic|\bclaude\b|\bgemini\b|copilot)",
    "agentic":   r"(?i:agentic|ai agents?\b)",
}
ANY = "(" + "|".join(f"(?:{p})" for p in TERMS.values()) + ")"
TERM_RE = {k: re.compile(v) for k, v in TERMS.items()}
ANY_RE = re.compile(ANY)
SENT_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")
MAX_WINDOW = 1500     # chars; longer sentence windows are clipped around the match
CLIP_PAD = 600


def b3(s: str) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(s.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def manifest() -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="") as f:
        return {r["id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t")}


def source_path() -> Path:
    m = manifest()["transcripts"]
    return BULK / m["path"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fetch
def cmd_fetch() -> int:
    m = manifest()["transcripts"]
    dst = BULK / m["path"]
    BULK.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    if not dst.exists():
        req = urllib.request.Request(m["url"], headers={"User-Agent": UA})
        tmp = dst.with_suffix(".part")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r, tmp.open("wb") as f:
            while chunk := r.read(1 << 22):
                f.write(chunk)
        tmp.rename(dst)
    h = blake3.blake3(max_threads=blake3.blake3.AUTO)
    with dst.open("rb") as f:
        while chunk := f.read(1 << 24):
            h.update(chunk)
    got, size = h.hexdigest(), dst.stat().st_size
    if str(size) != m["bytes"] or got != m["blake3"]:
        print(f"FAIL: {dst.name} bytes={size} blake3={got}\n  manifest bytes={m['bytes']} blake3={m['blake3']}")
        return 1
    print(f"ok: {dst.name} {size} bytes blake3 {got}")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- constituents
def cmd_constituents() -> int:
    m = manifest()["sp500"]
    req = urllib.request.Request(m["url"], headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    page = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30))["query"]["pages"][0]
    rev = page["revisions"][0]
    text = rev["slots"]["main"]["content"]
    if b3(text) != m["blake3"]:
        print(f"FAIL: revision {rev['revid']} wikitext blake3 {b3(text)} != manifest {m['blake3']}")
        return 1
    section = text.split('id="constituents"', 1)[1].split("|}", 1)[0]
    rows = []
    for line in section.split("\n|-")[1:]:
        t = re.search(r"\{\{(?:NyseSymbol|NasdaqSymbol|BZX link|Cboe ticker)\|([A-Za-z.]+)", line, re.I)
        cik = re.search(r"\|\|\s*(\d{10})\s*\|\|", line) or re.search(r"\b(\d{10})\b", line)
        if t:
            rows.append((t.group(1).upper().replace(".", "-"), cik.group(1) if cik else ""))
    rows = sorted(set(rows))
    out = CORPUS / "sp500-constituents.tsv"
    with out.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(["symbol", "cik"])
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"ok: {len(rows)} constituents from wikipedia revid {rev['revid']} -> {out.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0

def windows_for(content: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, list[str]]]:
    """Merged sentence windows (match sentence +/- 1) as [start, end) offsets."""
    bounds, pos = [], 0
    for m in SENT_END.finditer(content):
        bounds.append((pos, m.start()))
        pos = m.end()
    bounds.append((pos, len(content)))
    hits = sorted({i for i, (s, e) in enumerate(bounds) if ANY_RE.search(content, s, e)})
    spans: list[list[int]] = []
    for i in hits:
        lo, hi = max(i - 1, 0), min(i + 1, len(bounds) - 1)
        if spans and lo <= spans[-1][1] + 1:
            spans[-1][1] = max(spans[-1][1], hi)
        else:
            spans.append([lo, hi])
    out = []
    for lo, hi in spans:
        s, e = bounds[lo][0], bounds[hi][1]
        if e - s > MAX_WINDOW:  # one run-on "sentence": clip around matches, snap to spaces
            pieces = []
            for m in ANY_RE.finditer(content, s, e):

        if fam:
            res.append((s, e, fam))
    return res

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.10" # dependencies = ["duckdb==2.0.0", "blake3>=1.0"] # /// """Hacker News focused AI corpus: Anthropic, and AI security incidents. IDs only. Source: open-index/hacker-news on Hugging Face (ODC-BY), monthly parquet files pinned to one dataset commit in corpus/hacker-news/MANIFEST.tsv (path, bytes, SHA-256 = the LFS oid Hugging Face publishes). Bulk bytes and comment text live in the gitignored .hncorpus/ and are never committed: HN commenters are mostly private individuals, so the repository holds item ids, character offsets and BLAKE3 hashes, and anyone can rebuild the text from the pinned source. Two focused sets, each a published regex (no model): anthropic "Anthropic" (not the anthropic principle / reasoning / argument), and "Claude" from 2023-03-01 (the model's release), minus common first-name collocations. ai_security a security term (CVE, breach, exfiltration, vulnerability, exploit, malware, zero-day, RCE, backdoor, leaked weights/keys/prompt, ...) in a window that also holds an AI term, or an AI-specific attack term (prompt injection, jailbreak) on its own. Unit: the earnings-call window (match sentence +/- 1, merged, clipped at 1,500 chars) over the comment's normalised text. Normalisation:

-> blank line, other tags dropped, HTML entities unescaped. (?:the |its |their )?(?:system prompt|weights|model weights|source code|api keys?|keys|credentials|secrets|user data|training data)\b)") AI_ATTACK = re.compile(r"(?i:\bprompt[- ]injections?\b|\bjailbr(?:eak|eaks|eaking|eaked|oken)\b)") SENT_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+") MAX_WINDOW, CLIP_PAD = 1500, 600 PRE_FILTER = (r"(?i)anthropic|claude|cve|rce|0-?day|breach|exfiltrat|vulnerab|exploit|malware" r"|supply.chain|zero.day|backdoor|security|hacked|leak|prompt.injection|jailbr") def b3(s: str) -> str: return blake3.blake3(s.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]*>") def normalise(raw: str) -> str: return html.unescape(TAG.sub("", raw.replace("

", "\n\n"))) def months() -> list[dict[str, str]]: with MANIFEST.open(newline="") as f: return list(csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t")) # ---------------------------------------------------------------- pin / fetch def cmd_pin() -> int: url = f"https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/{REPO}/tree/{REVISION}/data?recursive=true" tree = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=60)) rows = [] for x in tree: m = re.fullmatch(r"data/\d{4}/(\d{4}-\d{2})\.parquet", x["path"]) if x["type"] == "file" and m and FIRST_MONTH <= m.group(1) <= LAST_MONTH: rows.append((m.group(1), x["path"], f"https://huggingface.co/datasets/{REPO}/resolve/{REVISION}/{x['path']}", str(x["lfs"]["size"]), x["lfs"]["oid"])) rows.sort() CORPUS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with MANIFEST.open("w", newline="") as f: w = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n") w.writerow(["month", "path", "url", "bytes", "sha256"]) w.writerows(rows) print(f"ok: {len(rows)} monthly files pinned at {REPO}@{REVISION[:8]} -> {MANIFEST.relative_to(ROOT)}") return 0 def _fetch_one(r: dict[str, str]) -> str: dst = BULK / r["path"] dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if not dst.exists(): tmp = dst.with_suffix(".part") with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(r["url"], headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=120) as s, \ tmp.open("wb") as f: while chunk := s.read(1 << 22): f.write(chunk) tmp.rename(dst) h = hashlib.sha256() with dst.open("rb") as f: while chunk := f.read(1 << 24): h.update(chunk) ok = str(dst.stat().st_size) == r["bytes"] and h.hexdigest() == r["sha256"] return f"{'ok' if ok else 'FAIL'}: {r['month']}" def cmd_fetch() -> int: with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as ex: res = list(ex.map(_fetch_one, months())) bad = [x for x in res if x.startswith("FAIL")] print(f"{len(res) - len(bad)} ok, {len(bad)} failed" + ("".join("\n " + b for b in bad))) return 1 if bad else 0 # ---------------------------------------------------------------- windows def spans(content: str, hit_re: re.Pattern) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """Merged sentence windows (match sentence +/- 1) around hit_re, clipped like ec_extract.""" bounds, pos = [], 0 for m in SENT_END.finditer(content): bounds.append((pos, m.start())) pos = m.end() bounds.append((pos, len(content))) hits = sorted({i for i, (s, e) in enumerate(bounds) if hit_re.search(content, s, e)}) merged: list[list[int]] = [] for i in hits: lo, hi = max(i - 1, 0), min(i + 1, len(bounds) - 1) if merged and lo <= merged[-1][1] + 1: merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], hi) else: merged.append([lo, hi]) out = [] for lo, hi in merged: s, e = bounds[lo][0], bounds[hi][1] if e - s <= MAX_WINDOW: out.append((s, e)) continue pieces: list[list[int]] = [] for m in hit_re.finditer(content, s, e): a, b = max(m.start() - CLIP_PAD, s), min(m.end() + CLIP_PAD, e) if pieces and a <= pieces[-1][1]: pieces[-1][1] = b else: pieces.append([a, b]) for a, b in pieces: if a > s: a = content.find(" ", a, b) + 1 or a if b < e and content.rfind(" ", a, b) > a: b = content.rfind(" ", a, b) out.append((a, b)) return out def windows_for(text: str, day: str) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, str]]: """(set, start, end, families) for one normalised comment.""" res = [] anth = ANTHROPIC if day < CLAUDE_FROM else re.compile(f"{ANTHROPIC.pattern}|{CLAUDE.pattern}") for s, e in spans(text, anth): seg = text[s:e] fam = [k for k, r in (("anthropic", ANTHROPIC), ("claude", CLAUDE)) if r.search(seg) and (k == "anthropic" or day >= CLAUDE_FROM)] if fam: res.append(("anthropic", s, e, ";".join(fam))) sec = re.compile(f"{SECURITY.pattern}|{AI_ATTACK.pattern}") for s, e in spans(text, sec): seg = text[s:e] fam = ["ai_attack"] if AI_ATTACK.search(seg) else [] if SECURITY.search(seg) and AI_RE.search(seg): fam.append("security_ai") if fam: res.append(("ai_security", s, e, ";".join(fam))) return res def scan(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, path: Path): return con.execute( f"""SELECT id, strftime(time, '%Y-%m-%d') AS day, text FROM '{path}' WHERE type = 2 AND coalesce(deleted, 0) = 0 AND coalesce(dead, 0) = 0 AND text IS NOT NULL AND regexp_matches(text, ?) ORDER BY id""", [PRE_FILTER]).fetchall() def cmd_build() -> int: con = duckdb.connect() mrows, wrows, trows = [], [], [] for r in months(): path = BULK / r["path"] n_all = con.execute(f"""SELECT count(*) FROM '{path}' WHERE type = 2 AND coalesce(deleted, 0) = 0 AND coalesce(dead, 0) = 0 AND text IS NOT NULL""").fetchone()[0] last = con.execute(f"SELECT strftime(max(time), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') FROM '{path}' WHERE type = 2").fetchone()[0] per = {"anthropic": set(), "ai_security": set()} for item_id, day, raw in scan(con, path): text = normalise(raw) ws = windows_for(text, day) if not ws: continue tb = b3(text) trows.append((item_id, text)) for st, s, e, fam in ws: per[st].add(item_id) wid = b3(f"{item_id}:{st}:{s}:{e}")[:16] wrows.append((wid, st, item_id, day, s, e, e - s, fam, b3(text[s:e]), tb)) mrows.append((r["month"], n_all, len(per["anthropic"]), len(per["ai_security"]), last)) print(f"{r['month']}: {n_all:>7} comments anthropic {len(per['anthropic']):>6} ai_security {len(per['ai_security']):>5}", flush=True) with (CORPUS / "months.tsv").open("w", newline="") as f: w = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n") w.writerow(["month", "n_comments", "n_anthropic_comments", "n_ai_security_comments", "last_comment_utc"]) w.writerows(mrows) con.execute("""CREATE TABLE w (window_id VARCHAR, "set" VARCHAR, item_id UBIGINT, day DATE, start_char INTEGER, end_char INTEGER, n_chars INTEGER, families VARCHAR, window_blake3 VARCHAR, comment_blake3 VARCHAR)""") con.executemany("INSERT INTO w VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", wrows) con.execute(f"""COPY (SELECT * FROM w ORDER BY "set", item_id, start_char) TO '{CORPUS / "windows.parquet"}' (FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd)""") # #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.10" # dependencies = ["duckdb==2.0.0", "blake3>=1.0"] # /// """Hacker News focused AI corpus: Anthropic, and AI security incidents. IDs only. Source: open-index/hacker-news on Hugging Face (ODC-BY), monthly parquet files pinned to one dataset commit in corpus/hacker-news/MANIFEST.tsv (path, bytes, SHA-256 = the LFS oid Hugging Face publishes). Bulk bytes and comment text live in the gitignored .hncorpus/ and are never committed: HN commenters are mostly private individuals, so the repository holds item ids, character offsets and BLAKE3 hashes, and anyone can rebuild the text from the pinned source. Two focused sets, each a published regex (no model): anthropic "Anthropic" (not the anthropic principle / reasoning / argument), and "Claude" from 2023-03-01 (the model's release), minus common first-name collocations. ai_security a security term (CVE, breach, exfiltration, vulnerability, exploit, malware, zero-day, RCE, backdoor, leaked weights/keys/prompt, ...) in a window that also holds an AI term, or an AI-specific attack term (prompt injection, jailbreak) on its own. Unit: the earnings-call window (match sentence +/- 1, merged, clipped at 1,500 chars) over the comment's normalised text. Normalisation:

-> blank line, other tags dropped, HTML entities unescaped. Comments that are deleted or dead are excluded from numerator and denominator alike. uv run scripts/hn_extract.py pin # write MANIFEST.tsv from the pinned HF revision uv run scripts/hn_extract.py fetch # download + SHA-256 check into .hncorpus/ uv run scripts/hn_extract.py build # months.tsv, windows.parquet (+ local text) uv run scripts/hn_extract.py verify # re-normalise, re-slice, re-hash every window """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import csv import hashlib import html import json import re import sys import urllib.request from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor from pathlib import Path import blake3 import duckdb sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)) from ec_extract import ANY_RE as AI_RE # noqa: E402 (the earnings-call AI term regex) ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus" / "hacker-news" BULK = ROOT / ".hncorpus" # gitignored: source parquet + local text MANIFEST = CORPUS / "MANIFEST.tsv" REPO = "open-index/hacker-news" REVISION = "c54ced5973b95d80cd934b8921f44ec8d87c3cd1" FIRST_MONTH, LAST_MONTH = "2021-01", "2026-08" # Anthropic founded 2021; archive ends Aug 2026 CLAUDE_FROM = "2023-03-01" UA = "anthropic-pbc hacker-news corpus research (github.com/ethicalcapital/anthropic-pbc)" ANTHROPIC = re.compile( r"(?i:\banthropic(?:'s)?\b)(?!\s+(?i:principle|reasoning|argument|bias|selection|shadow|explanation))") CLAUDE = re.compile( r"\bClaude\b(?!\s+(?:Shannon|Monet|Debussy|L[eé]vi|Van\b|Elwood|Bernard|Chabrol|Rains|Lorrain|Cahun|Makelele|Steele|Frollo))") SECURITY = re.compile( r"\bCVE-\d{4}-\d{4,}|\bCVEs?\b|\bRCE\b|\b0-?days?\b" r"|(?i:\bdata breach(?:es)?\b|\bbreach(?:ed|es)?\b|\bexfiltrat\w*|\bvulnerabilit(?:y|ies)\b" r"|\bexploit(?:s|ed|able|ing)?\b|\bmalware\b|\bsupply[- ]chain attacks?\b|\bzero[- ]days?\b" r"|\bbackdoor(?:s|ed)?\b|\bsecurity (?:incident|breach|hole|flaw)s?\b|\bhacked\b" r"|\bdata leaks?\b|\bleak(?:s|ed)? (?:the |its |their )?(?:system prompt|weights|model weights|source code|api keys?|keys|credentials|secrets|user data|training data)\b)") AI_ATTACK = re.compile(r"(?i:\bprompt[- ]injections?\b|\bjailbr(?:eak|eaks|eaking|eaked|oken)\b)") SENT_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+") MAX_WINDOW, CLIP_PAD = 1500, 600 PRE_FILTER = (r"(?i)anthropic|claude|cve|rce|0-?day|breach|exfiltrat|vulnerab|exploit|malware" r"|supply.chain|zero.day|backdoor|security|hacked|leak|prompt.injection|jailbr") def b3(s: str) -> str: return blake3.blake3(s.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]*>") def normalise(raw: str) -> str: return html.unescape(TAG.sub("", raw.replace("

", "\n\n"))) def months() -> list[dict[str, str]]: with MANIFEST.open(newline="") as f: return list(csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t")) # ---------------------------------------------------------------- pin / fetch def cmd_pin() -> int: url = f"https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/{REPO}/tree/{REVISION}/data?recursive=true" tree = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=60)) rows = [] for x in tree: m = re.fullmatch(r"data/\d{4}/(\d{4}-\d{2})\.parquet", x["path"]) if x["type"] == "file" and m and FIRST_MONTH <= m.group(1) <= LAST_MONTH: rows.append((m.group(1), x["path"], f"https://huggingface.co/datasets/{REPO}/resolve/{REVISION}/{x['path']}", str(x["lfs"]["size"]), x["lfs"]["oid"])) rows.sort() CORPUS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with MANIFEST.open("w", newline="") as f: w = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n") w.writerow(["month", "path", "url", "bytes", "sha256"]) w.writerows(rows) print(f"ok: {len(rows)} monthly files pinned at {REPO}@{REVISION[:8]} -> {MANIFEST.relative_to(ROOT)}") return 0 def _fetch_one(r: dict[str, str]) -> str: dst = BULK / r["path"] dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if not dst.exists(): tmp = dst.with_suffix(".part") with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(r["url"], headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=120) as s, \ tmp.open("wb") as f: while chunk := s.read(1 << 22): f.write(chunk) tmp.rename(dst) h = hashlib.sha256() with dst.open("rb") as f: while chunk := f.read(1 << 24): h.update(chunk) ok = str(dst.stat().st_size) == r["bytes"] and h.hexdigest() == r["sha256"] return f"{'ok' if ok else 'FAIL'}: {r['month']}" def cmd_fetch() -> int: with ThreadPoolExecutor(6) as ex: res = list(ex.map(_fetch_one, months())) bad = [x for x in res if x.startswith("FAIL")] print(f"{len(res) - len(bad)} ok, {len(bad)} failed" + ("".join("\n " + b for b in bad))) return 1 if bad else 0 # ---------------------------------------------------------------- windows def spans(content: str, hit_re: re.Pattern) -> list[tuple[int, int]]: """Merged sentence windows (match sentence +/- 1) around hit_re, clipped like ec_extract.""" bounds, pos = [], 0 for m in SENT_END.finditer(content): bounds.append((pos, m.start())) pos = m.end() bounds.append((pos, len(content))) hits = sorted({i for i, (s, e) in enumerate(bounds) if hit_re.search(content, s, e)}) merged: list[list[int]] = [] for i in hits: lo, hi = max(i - 1, 0), min(i + 1, len(bounds) - 1) if merged and lo <= merged[-1][1] + 1: merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], hi) else: merged.append([lo, hi]) out = [] for lo, hi in merged: s, e = bounds[lo][0], bounds[hi][1] if e - s <= MAX_WINDOW: out.append((s, e)) continue pieces: list[list[int]] = [] for m in hit_re.finditer(content, s, e): a, b = max(m.start() - CLIP_PAD, s), min(m.end() + CLIP_PAD, e) if pieces and a <= pieces[-1][1]: pieces[-1][1] = b else: pieces.append([a, b]) for a, b in pieces: if a > s: a = content.find(" ", a, b) + 1 or a if b < e and content.rfind(" ", a, b) > a: b = content.rfind(" ", a, b) out.append((a, b)) return out def windows_for(text: str, day: str) -> list[tuple[str, int, int, str]]: """(set, start, end, families) for one normalised comment.""" res = [] anth = ANTHROPIC if day < CLAUDE_FROM else re.compile(f"{ANTHROPIC.pattern}|{CLAUDE.pattern}") for s, e in spans(text, anth): seg = text[s:e] fam = [k for k, r in (("anthropic", ANTHROPIC), ("claude", CLAUDE)) if r.search(seg) and (k == "anthropic" or day >= CLAUDE_FROM)] if fam: res.append(("anthropic", s, e, ";".join(fam))) sec = re.compile(f"{SECURITY.pattern}|{AI_ATTACK.pattern}") for s, e in spans(text, sec): seg = text[s:e] fam = ["ai_attack"] if AI_ATTACK.search(seg) else [] if SECURITY.search(seg) and AI_RE.search(seg): fam.append("security_ai") if fam: res.append(("ai_security", s, e, ";".join(fam))) return res def scan(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, path: Path): return con.execute( f"""SELECT id, strftime(time, '%Y-%m-%d') AS day, text FROM '{path}' WHERE type = 2 AND coalesce(deleted, 0) = 0 AND coalesce(dead, 0) = 0 AND text IS NOT NULL AND regexp_matches(text, ?) ORDER BY id""", [PRE_FILTER]).fetchall() def cmd_build() -> int: con = duckdb.connect() mrows, wrows, trows = [], [], [] for r in months(): path = BULK / r["path"] n_all = con.execute(f"""SELECT count(*) FROM '{path}' WHERE type = 2 AND coalesce(deleted, 0) = 0 AND coalesce(dead, 0) = 0 AND text IS NOT NULL""").fetchone()[0] last = con.execute(f"SELECT strftime(max(time), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') FROM '{path}' WHERE type = 2").fetchone()[0] per = {"anthropic": set(), "ai_security": set()} for item_id, day, raw in scan(con, path): text = normalise(raw) ws = windows_for(text, day) if not ws: continue tb = b3(text) trows.append((item_id, text)) for st, s, e, fam in ws: per[st].add(item_id) wid = b3(f"{item_id}:{st}:{s}:{e}")[:16] wrows.append((wid, st, item_id, day, s, e, e - s, fam, b3(text[s:e]), tb)) mrows.append((r["month"], n_all, len(per["anthropic"]), len(per["ai_security"]), last)) print(f"{r['month']}: {n_all:>7} comments anthropic {len(per['anthropic']):>6} ai_security {len(per['ai_security']):>5}", flush=True) with (CORPUS / "months.tsv").open("w", newline="") as f: w = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n") w.writerow(["month", "n_comments", "n_anthropic_comments", "n_ai_security_comments", "last_comment_utc"]) w.writerows(mrows) con.execute("""CREATE TABLE w (window_id VARCHAR, "set" VARCHAR, item_id UBIGINT, day DATE, start_char INTEGER, end_char INTEGER, n_chars INTEGER, families VARCHAR, window_blake3 VARCHAR, comment_blake3 VARCHAR)""") con.executemany("INSERT INTO w VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", wrows) con.execute(f"""COPY (SELECT * FROM w ORDER BY "set", item_id, start_char) TO '{CORPUS / "windows.parquet"}' (FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd)""") # input.prompt:
Build a pinned, deterministic Wikipedia corpus of AI-risk articles in the repo at /Users/srvo/dev/anthropic-pbc (you are in a git worktree of it; branch ec-ai-corpus). Purpose: Sloane wants to map the "dialogue space" of AI risk — the dimensions and theories of AI risk that have been identified — as a reference taxonomy, so that what executives say on earnings calls, what analysts ask, and what Hacker News practitioners discuss can later be placed against it. You build the corpus and a *candidate* dimension list; you do not run any model.

Read first: AGENTS.md (repo conventions), docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md §5 and §9 (models are witnesses; NO labels from an LLM — this binds you: the taxonomy must be derived structurally from Wikipedia, never written or judged by you or any LLM), docs/earnings-call-ai-corpus.md (the pattern to copy), scripts/ec_extract.py (PEP 723 header, MANIFEST pattern, window logic, `verify`), and corpus/earnings-calls/README.md (attribution style).

Deliverables:
1. `scripts/wp_extract.py`, a PEP 723 `uv run` script with exact pins, subcommands:
   - `pin --as-of 2026-11-04`: discover articles through the MediaWiki API (en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php, send a descriptive User-Agent like ec_extract's UA). Seed = a published list of categories plus seed articles, written as constants in the script. Start from things like Category:Existential risk from artificial general intelligence, Category:Ethics of artificial intelligence, Category:AI safety (check what actually exists), Category:Regulation of artificial intelligence, plus seed articles such as AI safety, AI alignment, Existential risk from artificial intelligence, Ethics of artificial intelligence, Algorithmic bias, Technological unemployment, Deepfake, Environmental impact of artificial intelligence, Regulation of artificial intelligence, Artificial intelligence (its risks sections), Instrumental convergence, AI capability control, Misinformation, AI-assisted targeting/lethal autonomous weapons, Hallucination (artificial intelligence), Prompt injection, AI takeover. Verify every title exists; drop and report any that do not. Traverse categories to depth 1 only. For each article, take the last revision at or before the as-of timestamp (rvstart/rvdir=older) and record title, pageid, revid, timestamp, and BLAKE3 of the wikitext in `corpus/wikipedia-ai-risk/MANIFEST.tsv`. Time is the recorded --as-of argument, never the clock.

content.content:
"""Run scripts/ec_classify.py's scoring on Modal GPUs, in parallel.

Same functions, same pins, same codebook; only the device differs. Shards come
back to this machine and are merged locally by ec_classify.merge(), which writes
the committed parquet and run record. Shards are tagged with the backend
(`modal-<GPU>`), so they never mix with a local MPS run.

    uvx --with duckdb==2.0.0 --with blake3 modal run scripts/ec_classify_modal.py --model deberta --limit 2048
    uvx --with duckdb==2.0.0 --with blake3 modal run scripts/ec_classify_modal.py --model deberta
    uvx --with duckdb==2.0.0 --with blake3 modal run scripts/ec_classify_modal.py --model modernbert
    # another unit file / codebook (output: proposals/earnings-calls/<codebook stem>/):
    ... --model deberta --units corpus/earnings-calls/ai-questions.parquet \
        --codebook corpus/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1.tsv --id-col question_id

GPU type: EC_GPU env var (default L40S). Containers: EC_MAX_CONTAINERS (default 8;
the Starter plan allows 10 concurrent GPUs). Cost is per second of GPU time;
--limit runs one shard on one GPU and prints throughput before any full run.
"""


import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import modal

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

GPU = os.environ.get("EC_GPU", "L40S")
MAX_CONTAINERS = int(os.environ.get("EC_MAX_CONTAINERS", "8"))

image = (
    modal.Image.debian_slim(python_version="3.12")
    .pip_install("torch==2.9.1", "transformers==4.57.3", "sentencepiece==0.2.1",
                 "protobuf==6.33.1", "duckdb==2.0.0", "blake3==1.0.8")
    .add_local_python_source("ec_classify")
)
app = modal.App("ec-classify", image=image)


@app.cls(gpu=GPU, timeout=3600, REDACTED)
class Scorer:
    model_key: str = modal.parameter()
    dtype: str = modal.parameter(default="bfloat16")
    batch: int = modal.parameter(default=128)

    @modal.enter()
    def load(self) -> None:
        import ec_classify as ec
        self.ec = ec
        self.tok, self.model, self.ent = ec.load_model(self.model_key, self.dtype, "cuda")

    @modal.method()
    def score(self, si: int, wins: list, hyps: list) -> tuple[int, list, float]:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            rows = self.ec.score_windows(self.tok, self.model, self.ent, "cuda", wins, hyps, self.batch)

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["duckdb==2.0.0"]
# ///
"""Hacker News focused sets: witness agreement, AI-risk share by month, and the
12-month risk-type ranking set beside the earnings-call ranking. IDs only.

Reads corpus/hacker-news/{months.tsv,windows.parquet} and the two witnesses'
scores in proposals/hacker-news/<set>/. Writes to proposals/hacker-news/report/.
No comment text or username is written; examples are item ids with their HN URL.
A positive is a witness proposal (both >= 0.5), not a finding: there is no gold set.

    uv run scripts/hn_report.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus" / "hacker-news"
PROP = ROOT / "proposals" / "hacker-news"
REPORT = PROP / "report"
EC_RANK = ROOT / "proposals" / "earnings-calls" / "codebook-v0.1" / "report" / "risk-ranking-ttm.tsv"
SETS = ["anthropic", "ai_security"]
TTM = ("2025-09-01", "2026-08-31")   # the archive's last 12 months (it ends 2026-08)
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
from ec_risk_series import LABELS, TYPES  # noqa: E402


def load(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
    parts = []
    for s in SETS:
        parts.append(f"""SELECT '{s}' AS "set", d.window_id, d.hypothesis_id AS h, d.p_entail AS pd, m.p_entail AS pm
            FROM '{PROP / s / 'deberta.parquet'}' d JOIN '{PROP / s / 'modernbert.parquet'}' m USING (window_id, hypothesis_id)""")
    con.execute("CREATE TABLE s AS " + " UNION ALL ".join(parts))
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE w AS SELECT * FROM '{CORPUS / 'windows.parquet'}'""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT "set", window_id, h, pd >= .5 AND pm >= .5 AS b FROM s""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE wf AS SELECT w.*, f.h, f.b FROM w JOIN f USING ("set", window_id)""")
    # comment-level: a comment carries hypothesis h if any of its windows in the set does
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE c AS SELECT "set", item_id, any_value(day) AS day, h, bool_or(b) AS b
        FROM wf GROUP BY ALL""")


def tsv(path: Path, header: str, rows) -> None:
    with path.open("w") as f:
        f.write(header + "\n")
        for r in rows:
            f.write("\t".join("" if v is None else str(v) for v in r) + "\n")


def agreement(con) -> None:
    rows = con.execute("""SELECT "set", h, count(*) n,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE pd >= .5) n_deberta, count(*) FILTER (WHERE pm >= .5) n_modernbert,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE pd >= .5 AND pm >= .5) n_both,
        avg((pd >= .5)::INT) a, avg((pm >= .5)::INT) b, avg(((pd >= .5) = (pm >= .5))::INT) po
        FROM s GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2""").fetchall()
    out = []
    for st, h, n, nd, nm, nb, a, b, po in rows:
        pe = a * b + (1 - a) * (1 - b)
        out.append((st, h, n, nd, nm, nb, f"{(po - pe) / (1 - pe):.3f}" if pe < 1 else ""))
    tsv(REPORT / "agreement.tsv", "set\thypothesis\tn_windows\tn_deberta\tn_modernbert\tn_both\tkappa", out)


def by_month(con) -> None:
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE m AS SELECT * FROM read_csv('{CORPUS / 'months.tsv'}', delim='\t', header=true)")
    rows = con.execute("""SELECT m.month, m.n_comments,
        count(DISTINCT c.item_id) FILTER (WHERE c."set" = 'anthropic') anth,
        count(DISTINCT c.item_id) FILTER (WHERE c."set" = 'anthropic' AND c.h = 'ai_risk' AND c.b) anth_risk,
        count(DISTINCT c.item_id) FILTER (WHERE c."set" = 'ai_security') sec,
        count(DISTINCT c.item_id) FILTER (WHERE c."set" = 'ai_security' AND c.h = 'ai_risk' AND c.b) sec_risk
        FROM m LEFT JOIN c ON strftime(c.day, '%Y-%m') = m.month GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall()
    out = [(mo, n, a, ar, f"{100 * a / n:.3f}", f"{100 * ar / a:.1f}" if a else "", s_, sr,
            f"{100 * s_ / n:.3f}") for mo, n, a, ar, s_, sr in rows]
    tsv(REPORT / "by-month.tsv", "month\tn_comments\tn_anthropic\tn_anthropic_ai_risk\tpct_comments_anthropic"
        "\tpct_anthropic_ai_risk\tn_ai_security\tn_ai_security_ai_risk\tpct_comments_ai_security", out)


def ranking(con) -> list[tuple]:
    """Per set: comments with ai_risk AND type (both witnesses), TTM. Share of ai_risk comments."""
    res = []
    for st in SETS:
        base = con.execute(f"""SELECT count(DISTINCT item_id) FROM c WHERE "set" = '{st}' AND h = 'ai_risk' AND b
            AND day BETWEEN '{TTM[0]}' AND '{TTM[1]}'""").fetchone()[0]
        for t in TYPES:
            n = con.execute(f"""SELECT count(DISTINCT x.item_id) FROM c x JOIN c r USING ("set", item_id)
                WHERE x."set" = '{st}' AND x.h = '{t}' AND x.b AND r.h = 'ai_risk' AND r.b
                AND x.day BETWEEN '{TTM[0]}' AND '{TTM[1]}'""").fetchone()[0]
            res.append((st, t, n, base))
    ec = {}
    with EC_RANK.open() as f:
        lines = [x.rstrip("\n").split("\t") for x in f if not x.startswith("#")]
    hdr, body = lines[0], lines[1:]
    tot = sum(int(r[hdr.index("windows")]) for r in body)
    for r in body:
        ec[r[hdr.index("risk_type")]] = (int(r[hdr.index("windows")]), tot)
    out = []
    for t in TYPES:
        row = [t, LABELS[t], ec[t][0], f"{100 * ec[t][0] / ec[t][1]:.1f}"]
        for st in SETS:
            n, base = next((n, b) for s_, t_, n, b in res if s_ == st and t_ == t)
            row += [n, f"{100 * n / base:.1f}" if base else ""]
        out.append(tuple(row))
    out.sort(key=lambda r: -float(r[5]))
    bases = {st: next(b for s_, _, _, b in res if s_ == st) for st in SETS}
    with (REPORT / "risk-ranking-ttm.tsv").open("w") as f:
        f.write(f"# {TTM[0]}..{TTM[1]}. Share of AI-risk units naming each type (a unit can name several). "
                f"Earnings calls: {ec[TYPES[0]][1]} risk windows, trailing 12 months to 2026-11-04. "
                f"HN: comments proposed ai_risk by both witnesses (anthropic {bases['anthropic']}, "
                f"ai_security {bases['ai_security']}). Witness proposals, no gold set.\n")
        f.write("risk_type\tlabel\tcalls_windows\tcalls_pct\tanthropic_comments\tanthropic_pct"
                "\tai_security_comments\tai_security_pct\n")
        for r in out:
            f.write("\t".join(str(v) for v in r) + "\n")
    return out


def examples(con) -> None:
    """Item ids (no text) of the most confidently risk-typed comments, per set and type, TTM."""
    rows = con.execute(f"""WITH x AS (
          SELECT s."set", w.item_id, s.h, least(s.pd, s.pm) AS p
          FROM s JOIN w USING ("set", window_id)
          WHERE s.h IN ({", ".join(f"'{t}'" for t in TYPES)}) AND s.pd >= .5 AND s.pm >= .5
            AND w.day BETWEEN '{TTM[0]}' AND '{TTM[1]}'
            AND (s."set", s.window_id) IN (SELECT "set", window_id FROM f WHERE h = 'ai_risk' AND b))
        SELECT "set", h, item_id, round(max(p), 4) p FROM x GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
        QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY "set", h ORDER BY max(p) DESC, item_id) <= 10
        ORDER BY 1, 2, 4 DESC, 3""").fetchall()
    tsv(REPORT / "examples-ttm.tsv", "set\trisk_type\titem_id\tmin_witness_p\turl",
        [(*r, f"https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id={r[2]}") for r in rows])


def plot(rank: list[tuple]) -> None:
    """Three panels, same row order, one bar per risk type: share of AI-risk units naming it."""
    panels = [("Earnings calls (executives)", 3), ("HN: Anthropic", 5), ("HN: AI security", 7)]
    W, rowh, top, left, pw, gap = 900, 26, 92, 190, 210, 26
    H = top + rowh * len(rank) + 56
    vmax = max(float(r[i]) for r in rank for _, i in panels if r[i] != "")
    vmax = (int(vmax // 10) + 1) * 10
    o = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,sans-serif" role="img" aria-labelledby="t d">',
         '<style>:root{--bg:#fff;--ink:#1b1b1b;--muted:#5f6368;--grid:#e3e3e3;--bar:#2a6f97}'
         '@media (prefers-color-scheme:dark){:root{--bg:#161616;--ink:#ececec;--muted:#a3a3a3;--grid:#333;--bar:#6fb3d9}}'
         'text{fill:var(--ink)}.m{fill:var(--muted)}.g{stroke:var(--grid)}.b{fill:var(--bar)}</style>',
         f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" style="fill:var(--bg)"/>',
         '<title id="t">What kind of AI risk: executives vs Hacker News</title>',
         '<desc id="d">Share of AI-risk passages naming each risk type, in three sources, trailing 12 months.</desc>',
         '<text x="16" y="30" font-size="18" font-weight="600">What kind of AI risk? Executives vs Hacker News</text>',
         f'<text x="16" y="52" font-size="13" class="m">Share of AI-risk units naming each type. Calls: 12 months to 2026-11-04. HN: {TTM[0][:7]} to {TTM[1][:7]}.</text>']
    for k, (name, idx) in enumerate(panels):
        x0 = left + k * (pw + gap)
        o.append(f'<text x="{x0}" y="{top - 12}" font-size="13" font-weight="600">{name}</text>')
        for v in (0, vmax // 2, vmax):
            gx = x0 + pw * v / vmax
            o.append(f'<line x1="{gx:.1f}" x2="{gx:.1f}" y1="{top - 4}" y2="{top + rowh * len(rank)}" class="g"/>')
            o.append(f'<text x="{gx:.1f}" y="{top + rowh * len(rank) + 16}" font-size="11" class="m" text-anchor="middle">{v}%</text>')
        for j, r in enumerate(rank):
            y = top + j * rowh
            v = float(r[idx]) if r[idx] != "" else 0.0
            bw = max(pw * v / vmax, 0.0)
            o.append(f'<g><title>{name}: {r[1]}, {v:.1f}% ({r[idx - 1]} units)</title>'
                     f'<rect x="{x0}" y="{y + 5}" width="{bw:.1f}" height="{rowh - 10}" rx="2" class="b"/>'
                     f'<text x="{x0 + bw + 4:.1f}" y="{y + rowh / 2 + 4}" font-size="11" class="m">{v:.0f}</text></g>')
    for j, r in enumerate(rank):
        o.append(f'<text x="{left - 10}" y="{top + j * rowh + rowh / 2 + 4}" font-size="12" text-anchor="end">{r[1]}</text>')
    o.append(f'<text x="16" y="{H - 12}" font-size="11" class="m">Ordered by HN: Anthropic. Two NLI witnesses must both score ≥ 0.5; a unit can name several types. Witness proposals, no gold set.</text>')
    o.append("</svg>")
    (REPORT / "risk-ranking-ttm.svg").write_text("\n".join(o) + "\n")


def main() -> int:
    REPORT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    con = duckdb.connect()
    load(con)
    agreement(con)
    by_month(con)
    plot(ranking(con))
    examples(con)
    for p in sorted(REPORT.iterdir()):
        print(p.relative_to(ROOT))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

12-month risk-type ranking set beside the earnings-call ranking. IDs only.

scores in proposals/hacker-news/<set>/. Writes to proposals/hacker-news/report/.

A positive is a witness proposal (both >= 0.5), not a finding: there is no gold set.

def load(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
    parts = []

        parts.append(f"""SELECT '{s}' AS "set", d.window_id, d.hypothesis_id AS h, d.p_entail AS pd, m.p_entail AS pm
            FROM '{PROP / s / 'deberta.parquet'}' d JOIN '{PROP / s / 'modernbert.parquet'}' m USING (window_id, hypothesis_id)""")
    con.execute("CREATE TABLE s AS " + " UNION ALL ".join(parts))
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE w AS SELECT * FROM '{CORPUS / 'windows.parquet'}'""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT "set", window_id, h, pd >= .5 AND pm >= .5 AS b FROM s""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE wf AS SELECT w.*, f.h, f.b FROM w JOIN f USING ("set", window_id)""")
    # comment-level: a comment carries hypothesis h if any of its windows in the set does
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE c AS SELECT "set", item_id, any_value(day) AS day, h, bool_or(b) AS b

# Hacker News: Anthropic and AI-security comments (IDs only)

Two focused sets of Hacker News comments, January 2021 to August 2026: those
that mention Anthropic or Claude, and those about AI security incidents (CVEs,
breaches, prompt injection, jailbreaks, leaked weights or keys). Method:
[`docs/hacker-news-corpus.md`](../../docs/hacker-news-corpus.md).

**No comment text and no usernames are stored here.** HN commenters are mostly
private individuals, so this folder holds item ids, character offsets into a
deterministic normalisation of each comment, and BLAKE3 hashes. The text is
rebuilt locally from the pinned source into the gitignored `.hncorpus/`, and
`verify` checks every hash. Any comment can be read at
`https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=<item_id>`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MANIFEST.tsv` | Pins: 68 monthly parquet files of `open-index/hacker-news` at dataset commit `c54ced59`, with bytes and SHA-256 (= the Hugging Face LFS oid). |
| `months.tsv` | **Denominator.** Per month: all live comments, and comments in each set. |
| `windows.parquet` | The unit: match sentence ±1 as `[start_char, end_char)` of the normalised comment, with set, term families, and BLAKE3 of the window and the comment. |

Rebuild and check from scratch:

    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py fetch    # 5.6 GB into .hncorpus/, SHA-256 checked
    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py build    # byte-identical on rerun; verifies on completion
    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py verify

Model output lives in `proposals/hacker-news/`, as witness proposals.

This folder is **not** covered by the repository's CC0 dedication.

- **Source:** `open-index/hacker-news`
  (https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-index/hacker-news), licensed under the
  **Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY 1.0)**. Its items mirror the
  public Hacker News API (https://github.com/HackerNewsAPI/HN-API). The comments
  belong to their authors; this folder republishes none of their words.
- "Hacker News" is operated by Y Combinator; this corpus is not affiliated with
  or endorsed by it.

### More about this dataset

### Documentation

**Data**: CVE records come from the CVE Program’s cvelistV5 repository. We process every published record from 2020 onward. The dates visualized on our explorer represent vulnerability publication dates, not discovery dates.

**Severity**: CVE severities are based on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). CVSS assigns a score between 0 and 10, according to factors like the attack complexity, required privileges, the scope of the vulnerability, and more. These numeric scores are then assigned to severity categories as follows:

* None: 0.0
* Low: 0.1 - 3.9
* Medium: 4.0 - 6.9
* High: 7.0 - 8.9
* Critical: 9.0 - 10.0

We default to using a CNA’s own assessment first, and fill in gaps with assessments from third parties (known as Authorized Data Publishers, or ADPs). If multiple CVSS versions are given, we default to v4.0, with fallback to v3.1, then v3.0. Records without one of these CVSS scores are counted as “Unknown.”

**Reporting organizations (CNAs)**: Every CVE record is assigned by a CNA (CVE Numbering Authority) — typically the vendor of the affected product or a third-party security research organization. We count CVEs across all CNAs, but to keep the underlying data manageable we only break down individual counts for notable CNAs, with non-notable CNAs grouped into an “Other” category.

We consider a CNA notable if it is a vendor of widely-deployed software or hardware, or a major open-source project or foundation, and it maintains an active CVE program (we require at least 50 CVEs published since 2020). We include the following organizations in our list of notable CNAs:

* Major vendors (17): Microsoft · Google · Apple · Adobe · Oracle · Cisco · IBM · Red Hat · Intel · AMD · NVIDIA · Qualcomm · Samsung · SAP · Amazon (AWS) · VMware (Broadcom) · GitHub (own products)
* Open source (4): Linux · Mozilla · Apache · OpenSSL

Reporting practices vary substantially across organizations, creating noise. For instance, Linux became a CNA in February 2024 and subsequently began assigning CVEs for thousands of backported bug fixes, leading to a high number of reports in 2024 and 2025.

**Individual records**: Alongside the aggregates, we surface individual High and Critical severity CVEs from notable CNAs, each linking back to its official CVE record. See the “Table” view in the explorer above, or download our data at the link below.

Our explorer visualizes the announcement date of Claude Mythos Preview (April 7, 2026), which coincided with a large jump in the number of new vulnerability reports. Anthropic claimed that Claude Mythos was capable of autonomous vulnerability discovery, and gave trusted partners access to the model in order to harden their software. Mythos Preview was used to find bugs in software before the April 7th announcement, which may have contributed to an increased number of reports in the month before the announcement. As of May 22nd, Anthropic claimed that Mythos Preview had been used to identify more than ten thousand high- or critical-severity bugs (not all of which had been publicly reported). Additionally, OpenAI has claimed that GPT-5.5 (released April 23) and GPT-5.5-cyber (May 7) are also capable of advanced cybersecurity tasks, and launched a similar trusted-partner program on May 7th, 2026.

input.prompt:
Build a pinned, deterministic monthly CVE time series in the repo at /Users/srvo/dev/anthropic-pbc (you are in a git worktree of it). Context: Sloane is folding AI-and-cybersecurity signals into a research paper on Anthropic. Epoch AI publishes a CVE explorer (https://epoch.ai/data/cve, CC BY; documentation says: built on the CVE Program's cvelistV5 repo, every published record 2020+, dated by publication date not discovery; severity = CNA's own CVSS first, then ADP; CVSS v4.0 > v3.1 > v3.0; else Unknown; buckets None 0, Low 0.1–3.9, Medium 4–6.9, High 7–8.9, Critical 9–10; "notable CNAs" = Microsoft, Google, Apple, Adobe, Oracle, Cisco, IBM, Red Hat, Intel, AMD, NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Samsung, SAP, Amazon (AWS), VMware (Broadcom), GitHub (own products), Linux, Mozilla, Apache, OpenSSL; Linux became a CNA Feb 2024 and inflates 2024–25; they mark the Claude Mythos Preview announcement on 2026-04-07, which coincided with a jump in reports). Epoch's download link could not be found, so rebuild from the primary source and reproduce Epoch's method.

Read first: AGENTS.md (conventions: deterministic, pinned, PEP 723 uv scripts with exact pins, no clock in outputs, time is a recorded --as-of argument, byte-identical rebuilds checked by hashing, bulk bytes in a gitignored dot-dir re-fetchable from a MANIFEST.tsv), and scripts/ec_extract.py + scripts/hn_extract.py as patterns.

Deliverables:
1. `scripts/cve_series.py` with `pin` (resolve a cvelistV5 snapshot as of 2026-11-04: prefer a GitHub release asset — the repo publishes daily baseline zips — or a commit SHA; record URL, bytes, SHA-256, BLAKE3 in `corpus/cve/MANIFEST.tsv`), `fetch` (into gitignored `.cvecorpus/`; add to .gitignore), `build`, `verify`.
2. `build` writes to `corpus/cve/`:
   - `monthly.tsv`: month (2020-01 .. last full month), n_published, by severity (critical/high/medium/low/none/unknown), n_notable_cna, n_linux_cna, n_excl_linux. Published, not REJECTED records only; record the rule.
   - `monthly-by-cna.tsv`: month × notable CNA (+ Other) counts.
   - `ai-related.tsv`: one row per CVE (id, published date, CNA short name, severity, which rule matched) where (a) the affected product/vendor or description matches an AI term (reuse the regex `ANY_RE` from scripts/ec_extract.py and add AI-product terms such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, Ollama, vLLM, MCP / Model Context Protocol, Hugging Face transformers, PyTorch, TensorFlow — publish the list), or (b) the credits field names an AI system or AI lab as finder (Claude, Mythos, Anthropic, OpenAI, GPT, Codex, Big Sleep, Google DeepMind, XBOW, etc. — publish the list; match only the credits array, record its `type` e.g. finder/tool). CVE records are public data (CVE terms of use) — ids, dates and short CNA names are fine to commit; do not commit full descriptions.
   - `monthly-ai.tsv`: month, n_ai_product, n_ai_credited, and n_ai_credited by credited system.
3. A cross-check: if you can locate Epoch's numbers (the page HTML or its JS bundle at https://epoch.ai/_astro/CveExplorerViz.*.js may embed them), compare a few months and report the differences; otherwise say you could not.
4. `corpus/cve/README.md` (files table, attribution: CVE Program terms of use; credit Epoch AI CC BY for the method) and `docs/cve-series.md` (short method: the rules, what it does not answer — a CVE count measures reporting, not risk; CNA onboarding and AI-assisted discovery both raise counts; AI credit is self-reported by CNAs and incomplete).

Constraints: do not run models. Do not edit docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md, index.html, README.md, frameworks/, sources/, enrich_*.py, seal.py, or the spec. Do not commit. Report: snapshot pin, record counts, monthly totals for 2025-10..last month, the AI-credited counts by system and month in 2026, the Epoch cross-check, two build hashes, and every judgment call.

Work in the repo /Users/srvo/dev/anthropic-pbc (you are in a git worktree; first run `git reset --hard ec-ai-corpus` if your worktree lacks scripts/ and corpus/ — check, and only do it if the worktree is clean). Goal: Sloane's paper on Anthropic PBC wants to examine the claim that Anthropic is involved with the health of democracy in a positive way. The first step is quantitative proxies for "health of democracy" as a public topic and as a measured condition. Your job is to build quick, citable proxy series and to assess the feasibility of the rest. Treat the claim as something to test, not to support: the proxies measure attention and conditions, and none of them measures Anthropic's effect. Say so in the doc.
