#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "matplotlib==3.10.7",
# ]
# ///
"""Charts for DECK.md that no corpus report draws yet. Reads committed tables only.

  deck/cve-ai-credit.svg     CVEs published per month, and CVEs whose CNA credits
                             name an AI system (Claude highlighted). corpus/cve/.
  deck/gdelt-attention.svg   Share of online news monitored by GDELT that says
                             "health of democracy", and that mentions Anthropic.
                             corpus/democracy/gdelt-timelines.tsv.

Two measures of different scale are drawn as two panels, never a dual axis.
Deterministic: fixed svg.hashsalt, no Date metadata.

    uv run scripts/deck_charts.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "deck"
CVE = ROOT / "corpus" / "cve" / "monthly-ai.tsv"
GDELT = ROOT / "corpus" / "democracy" / "gdelt-timelines.tsv"

# Same palette as the corpus reports (dataviz reference palette, light mode).
SURFACE, INK, INK2, GRID = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df"
S1, S2, MUTED = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#a8a69f"


def rows(p: Path) -> list[dict]:
    with p.open() as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader((l for l in f if not l.startswith("#")), delimiter="\t"))


def setup():
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("svg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    plt.rcParams.update({"svg.hashsalt": "deck", "font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 10,
                         "axes.edgecolor": INK2, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "xtick.color": INK2,
                         "ytick.color": INK2})
    return matplotlib, plt


def style(ax) -> None:
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    for s in ("top", "right", "left"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(length=0)


def cve(matplotlib, plt) -> None:
    r = [x for x in rows(CVE) if x["month"] >= "2023-01"]
    months = [x["month"] for x in r]
    xs = range(len(months))
    pub = [int(x["n_published"]) for x in r]
    ai = [int(x["n_ai_credited"]) for x in r]
    claude = [int(x["n_credit_claude"]) for x in r]
    other = [a - c for a, c in zip(ai, claude)]
    ticks = [i for i, m in enumerate(months) if m.endswith("-01")]
    labels = [months[i][:4] for i in ticks]

    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6.2), facecolor=SURFACE, sharex=True,
                                 gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.45})
    style(a1)
    a1.bar(xs, pub, color=S1, width=0.78)
    a1.annotate(f"{pub[-1]:,}", (xs[-1], pub[-1]), xytext=(0, 4), textcoords="offset points",
                ha="center", color=INK, fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
    a1.yaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:,.0f}"))
    a1.set_title("CVEs published per month", loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")

    style(a2)
    a2.bar(xs, claude, color=S2, width=0.78, label="Credit names Claude")
    a2.bar(xs, other, bottom=claude, color=MUTED, width=0.78, label="Credit names another AI system or term")
    a2.annotate(f"{ai[-1]} ({claude[-1]} Claude)", (xs[-1], ai[-1]), xytext=(-4, 4),
                textcoords="offset points", ha="right", color=INK, fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
    a2.set_title("CVEs whose credits name an AI system, per month", loc="left", color=INK,
                 fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    a2.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=False, fontsize=9, labelcolor=INK)
    a2.set_xticks(ticks, labels)
    fig.suptitle("Vulnerability disclosures, and the share credited to AI", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 color=INK, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, f"Source: CVEProject/cvelistV5 baseline 2026-11-04 (corpus/cve). Months "
             f"{months[0]} to {months[-1]}. Credit = CNA credits field only, matched to named systems; "
             "method credit Epoch AI (CC BY).", color=INK2, fontsize=7)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.08, right=0.98, top=0.88, bottom=0.1)
    fig.savefig(OUT / "cve-ai-credit.svg", facecolor=SURFACE, metadata={"Date": None, "Creator": None})
    plt.close(fig)


def gdelt(matplotlib, plt) -> None:
    by: dict[str, dict[str, list[float]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for x in rows(GDELT):
        if x["source"] == "doc" and x["mode"] == "timelinevol" and x["query_id"] in ("hod", "anthropic"):
            by[x["query_id"]][x["date"][:6]].append(float(x["value"]))
    months = sorted(set(by["hod"]) | set(by["anthropic"]))
    months = [m for m in months if "201701" <= m <= "202610"]
    xs = range(len(months))
    ticks = [i for i, m in enumerate(months) if m.endswith("01")]
    labels = [months[i][:4] for i in ticks]

    def mean(q: str) -> list[float]:
        return [sum(by[q][m]) / len(by[q][m]) if by[q].get(m) else 0.0 for m in months]

    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6.2), facecolor=SURFACE, sharex=True,
                                 gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.45})
    for ax, q, color, title in ((a1, "hod", S1, '"Health of democracy"'), (a2, "anthropic", S2, "Anthropic")):
        style(ax)
        ys = mean(q)
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=color, lw=2)
        pk = max(range(len(ys)), key=ys.__getitem__)
        ax.annotate(f"peak {months[pk][:4]}-{months[pk][4:]}", (pk, ys[pk]), xytext=(0, 5),
                    textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK, fontsize=9)
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.3f}%"))
        ax.set_ylim(0, None)
        ax.set_title(f"{title}: % of monitored online news articles (monthly mean of daily values)",
                     loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold")
    a2.set_xticks(ticks, labels)
    fig.suptitle("News attention: the health of democracy, and Anthropic", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 color=INK, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, "Source: GDELT DOC 2.0 API, timelinevol, responses saved 2026-11-04 "
             "(corpus/democracy). Attention, not effect: neither line measures anything Anthropic does "
             "to democracy.", color=INK2, fontsize=7)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.98, top=0.88, bottom=0.1)
    fig.savefig(OUT / "gdelt-attention.svg", facecolor=SURFACE, metadata={"Date": None, "Creator": None})
    plt.close(fig)


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    matplotlib, plt = setup()
    cve(matplotlib, plt)
    gdelt(matplotlib, plt)
    print("wrote deck/cve-ai-credit.svg, deck/gdelt-attention.svg")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "matplotlib==3.10.7",
# ]
# ///
"""Charts for DECK.md that no corpus report draws yet. Reads committed tables only.

  deck/cve-ai-credit.svg     CVEs published per month, and CVEs whose CNA credits
                             name an AI system (Claude highlighted). corpus/cve/.
  deck/gdelt-attention.svg   Share of online news monitored by GDELT that says
                             "health of democracy", and that mentions Anthropic.
                             corpus/democracy/gdelt-timelines.tsv.

Two measures of different scale are drawn as two panels, never a dual axis.
Deterministic: fixed svg.hashsalt, no Date metadata.

    uv run scripts/deck_charts.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "deck"
CVE = ROOT / "corpus" / "cve" / "monthly-ai.tsv"
GDELT = ROOT / "corpus" / "democracy" / "gdelt-timelines.tsv"

# Same palette as the corpus reports (dataviz reference palette, light mode).
SURFACE, INK, INK2, GRID = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df"
S1, S2, MUTED = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#a8a69f"


def rows(p: Path) -> list[dict]:
    with p.open() as f:
        return list(csv.DictReader((l for l in f if not l.startswith("#")), delimiter="\t"))


def setup():
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("svg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    plt.rcParams.update({"svg.hashsalt": "deck", "font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 10,
                         "axes.edgecolor": INK2, "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "xtick.color": INK2,
                         "ytick.color": INK2})
    return matplotlib, plt


def style(ax) -> None:
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=0.8)
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    for s in ("top", "right", "left"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(length=0)


def cve(matplotlib, plt) -> None:
    r = [x for x in rows(CVE) if x["month"] >= "2023-01"]
    months = [x["month"] for x in r]
    xs = range(len(months))
    pub = [int(x["n_published"]) for x in r]
    ai = [int(x["n_ai_credited"]) for x in r]
    claude = [int(x["n_credit_claude"]) for x in r]
    other = [a - c for a, c in zip(ai, claude)]
    ticks = [i for i, m in enumerate(months) if m.endswith("-01")]
    labels = [months[i][:4] for i in ticks]

    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6.2), facecolor=SURFACE, sharex=True,
                                 gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.45})
    style(a1)
    a1.bar(xs, pub, color=S1, width=0.78)
    a1.annotate(f"{pub[-1]:,}", (xs[-1], pub[-1]), xytext=(0, 4), textcoords="offset points",
                ha="center", color=INK, fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
    a1.yaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:,.0f}"))
    a1.set_title("CVEs published per month", loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")

    style(a2)
    a2.bar(xs, claude, color=S2, width=0.78, label="Credit names Claude")
    a2.bar(xs, other, bottom=claude, color=MUTED, width=0.78, label="Credit names another AI system or term")
    a2.annotate(f"{ai[-1]} ({claude[-1]} Claude)", (xs[-1], ai[-1]), xytext=(-4, 4),
                textcoords="offset points", ha="right", color=INK, fontsize=9, fontweight="bold")
    a2.set_title("CVEs whose credits name an AI system, per month", loc="left", color=INK,
                 fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
    a2.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=False, fontsize=9, labelcolor=INK)
    a2.set_xticks(ticks, labels)
    fig.suptitle("Vulnerability disclosures, and the share credited to AI", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 color=INK, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, f"Source: CVEProject/cvelistV5 baseline 2026-11-04 (corpus/cve). Months "
             f"{months[0]} to {months[-1]}. Credit = CNA credits field only, matched to named systems; "
             "method credit Epoch AI (CC BY).", color=INK2, fontsize=7)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.08, right=0.98, top=0.88, bottom=0.1)
    fig.savefig(OUT / "cve-ai-credit.svg", facecolor=SURFACE, metadata={"Date": None, "Creator": None})
    plt.close(fig)


def gdelt(matplotlib, plt) -> None:
    by: dict[str, dict[str, list[float]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for x in rows(GDELT):
        if x["source"] == "doc" and x["mode"] == "timelinevol" and x["query_id"] in ("hod", "anthropic"):
            by[x["query_id"]][x["date"][:6]].append(float(x["value"]))
    months = sorted(set(by["hod"]) | set(by["anthropic"]))
    months = [m for m in months if "201701" <= m <= "202610"]
    xs = range(len(months))
    ticks = [i for i, m in enumerate(months) if m.endswith("01")]
    labels = [months[i][:4] for i in ticks]

    def mean(q: str) -> list[float]:
        return [sum(by[q][m]) / len(by[q][m]) if by[q].get(m) else 0.0 for m in months]

    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6.2), facecolor=SURFACE, sharex=True,
                                 gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.45})
    for ax, q, color, title in ((a1, "hod", S1, '"Health of democracy"'), (a2, "anthropic", S2, "Anthropic")):
        style(ax)
        ys = mean(q)
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=color, lw=2)
        pk = max(range(len(ys)), key=ys.__getitem__)
        ax.annotate(f"peak {months[pk][:4]}-{months[pk][4:]}", (pk, ys[pk]), xytext=(0, 5),
                    textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK, fontsize=9)
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.3f}%"))
        ax.set_ylim(0, None)
        ax.set_title(f"{title}: % of monitored online news articles (monthly mean of daily values)",
                     loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold")
    a2.set_xticks(ticks, labels)
    fig.suptitle("News attention: the health of democracy, and Anthropic", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 color=INK, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, "Source: GDELT DOC 2.0 API, timelinevol, responses saved 2026-11-04 "
             "(corpus/democracy). Attention, not effect: neither line measures anything Anthropic does "
             "to democracy.", color=INK2, fontsize=7)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.98, top=0.88, bottom=0.1)
    fig.savefig(OUT / "gdelt-attention.svg", facecolor=SURFACE, metadata={"Date": None, "Creator": None})
    plt.close(fig)


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    matplotlib, plt = setup()
    cve(matplotlib, plt)
    gdelt(matplotlib, plt)
    print("wrote deck/cve-ai-credit.svg, deck/gdelt-attention.svg")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def gdelt(matplotlib, plt) -> None:
    by: dict[str, dict[str, list[float]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    for x in rows(GDELT):
        if x["source"] == "doc" and x["mode"] == "timelinevol" and x["query_id"] in ("hod", "anthropic"):
            by[x["query_id"]][x["date"][:6]].append(float(x["value"]))
    months = sorted(set(by["hod"]) | set(by["anthropic"]))
    months = [m for m in months if "201701" <= m <= "202610"]
    xs = range(len(months))
    ticks = [i for i, m in enumerate(months) if m.endswith("01")]
    labels = [months[i][:4] for i in ticks]

    def median(q: str) -> list[float]:  # a median: single-day spikes (e.g. 2026-09-12, -20) do not move it
        out = []
        for m in months:
            v = sorted(by[q].get(m, []))
            out.append((v[(len(v) - 1) // 2] + v[len(v) // 2]) / 2 if v else 0.0)
        return out

    fig, (a1, a2) = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(9, 6.2), facecolor=SURFACE, sharex=True,
                                 gridspec_kw={"hspace": 0.45})
    for ax, q, color, title in ((a1, "hod", S1, '"Health of democracy"'), (a2, "anthropic", S2, "Anthropic")):
        style(ax)
        ys = median(q)
        ax.plot(xs, ys, color=color, lw=2)
        pk = max(range(len(ys)), key=ys.__getitem__)
        ax.annotate(f"peak {months[pk][:4]}-{months[pk][4:]}", (pk, ys[pk]), xytext=(0, 5),
                    textcoords="offset points", ha="center", color=INK, fontsize=9)
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(matplotlib.ticker.FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: f"{v:.3f}%"))
        ax.set_ylim(0, None)
        ax.set_title(f"{title}: % of monitored online news articles (monthly median of daily values)",
                     loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=10.5, fontweight="bold")
    a2.set_xticks(ticks, labels)
    fig.suptitle("News attention: the health of democracy, and Anthropic", x=0.01, ha="left",
                 color=INK, fontsize=13, fontweight="bold")
    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, "Source: GDELT DOC 2.0 API, timelinevol, responses saved 2026-11-04 (corpus/democracy).\n"
             "Attention, not effect: neither line measures anything Anthropic does to democracy.",
             color=INK2, fontsize=7)
    fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.98, top=0.86, bottom=0.12)
    fig.savefig(OUT / "gdelt-attention.svg", facecolor=SURFACE, metadata={"Date": None, "Creator": None})
    plt.close(fig)


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    matplotlib, plt = setup()
    cve(matplotlib, plt)
    gdelt(matplotlib, plt)
    print("wrote deck/cve-ai-credit.svg, deck/gdelt-attention.svg")

---

## Verdict first

1. **Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.** The public
   benefit purpose sits in its certificate and DGCL §362 requires balancing
   stockholders, "those materially affected," and that purpose. But §365(b)
   gives directors **no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit
   interest**, and §367 limits enforcement to derivative suits by holders of
   ≥2% (or $2M, lesser, once listed). The public the charter names cannot
   enforce it. **[CONFIRMED/HIGH]**
2. **The Report grades its own homework — and its own LTBT says so.** The
   Trust: the report "largely describes inputs; in subsequent reports we will
   increasingly look for Anthropic to produce outcomes" (p.17). Flagship
   benefit counts (33,000+ critical flaws; a 129,000 program-total that is
   **not in the PBC Report** — partner-reported, caught by the loop audit) have no public
   CVE-level audit. The 80% productivity figure is *Claude estimating
   Claude*. **[UNVERIFIED counts; MISLEADING if read as verified]**
3. **Present, Anthropic-attributable harm is documented and priced; present,
   Anthropic-attributable benefit is mostly anecdote.** Priced: the $1.5B
   *Bartz* settlement over ~500,000 pirated books (~7M downloaded); an
   estimated **5–7% of 9M-2026 revenue (~$1.7–2.3B of $33.2B) from customers
   later found violating its usage policy** (S-1); four Claude models gaining
   unauthorized access to real third-party systems in testing (Report p.6).
   Benefits at the same standard of proof: protein *binding* confirmed in
   independent wet labs (17/211 constructs; no neutralization, no medicine);
   the rest is process anecdote Anthropic admits lacks outcome evidence.
   On a like-for-like evidence standard, **documented harm outweighs documented
   benefit today. [NUANCED/HIGH — a ledger asymmetry, not a welfare sum]**
4. **"Measurable harm to millions" is not documented — and saying so plainly is
   the stronger argument.** No study counts millions of individually verified
   AI-harm victims (2023–26). Millions-scale figures in circulation are
   extrapolations (2.2% NCII self-report, n>16k), relative gaps (Stanford:
   22–25-year-olds in AI-exposed hiring ~19% below trend, while Yale finds no
   macro disruption), or population-counting (4.2B "affected" by election
   deepfakes = whole populations, not affected persons) **[MISLEADING]**.
   What *is* documented at scale is **exposure**: $895.4B of compute/infrastructure
   commitments ($447.5B before 2031; $69.8B in the next 12 months; ~$213.8B
   terminable), Q3-2026 revenue of $17.0B, and Anthropic's own admission that
   decisions are concentrated in "a handful of companies, nations, and people.
higher-income, white-collar workers." Health/education: "we don't yet have
evidence that these efforts have had their intended effects." The binder
result — the strongest benefit claim in either document — survives scrutiny
narrowly: two independent labs confirmed *binding* for 17/211 constructs on
one toxin family; neutralization and any medicine remain untested. The
33,000-flaw headline does not survive as stated: partner-reported, no public
CVE-level deduplication or severity audit in sources reviewed. The Fermat
and enzyme claims enter this paper exactly as Anthropic filed them: as
claims (circle 3) awaiting the artifacts that would make them findings.

**Institutional read.** Distribution today follows ability to pay token

Paper: `docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md`. Every chart here rebuilds from committed files. Model output in these charts comes from witnesses: two NLI models whose labels are proposals, not hand-verified findings. --- ## The argument in one line **Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.** - §365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest. - §367 limits enforcement to holders of ≥2% (or $2M, lesser, once listed). - The public the charter names cannot enforce it. The Report argues from *inputs + intentions* to a discharged public duty. The paper finds that inference unearned (§3). --- ![w:1000](docs/figures/fig1-verification.svg)
51 of 60 load-bearing quotes verified byte-exact against the PBC Report and S-1 (loop audit, 2026-11-03). "129,000" is not in the Report.
--- ![w:1000](docs/figures/fig3-scorecard.svg)
Appendix A: 0 of 10 governance dimensions held as filed; 4 partial or revocable, 6 absent.
--- ![w:1000](docs/figures/fig4-leverage.svg)
§1a, Meadows leverage points: Anthropic acts at 12 and 6, declines at 5, 4 and 3, speaks at 2 and 3.
--- ![w:1000](docs/figures/fig2-risk-governance-index.svg)
Risk–Governance Index v1 on Anthropic's own disclosed risks: 0 of 8 controlled.
--- # What the public record shows The paper's evidence is Anthropic's own filings. The rest of this deck looks outward at what public data says about AI risk and Anthropic: - **S&P 500 earnings calls:** what companies and analysts say about AI. - **Hacker News:** what practitioners say about Anthropic and AI security. - **Wikipedia:** the map of AI-risk ideas. - **The CVE record:** what the vulnerability database credits to AI. --- ![w:900](proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/ai-risk-by-year.svg)
AI as a risk on S&P 500 calls: 12.3% of 2026 calls (to 11-04) by both models, up from under 1% before 2023.
--- ![h:520](proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/risk-ranking-ttm.svg)
Companies name cybersecurity, safety and overspending. Energy, bias and jobs barely register. Codebook v0.1.
--- ![h:520](proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/intent-ttm.svg)
Analysts ask how AI sells (21.2% of AI questions) far more than how it is governed (0.8%). This bears on App. E: almost nobody on a call asks about control.
--- ![w:1050](proposals/hacker-news/report/risk-ranking-ttm.svg)
Hacker News discussion of Anthropic is about safety and ethics (40%) far more than executives' calls are (12%). Codebook v0.1; HN precision on safety/ethics is weaker (method doc).
--- ![h:540](proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/dialogue-space.svg)
The dialogue space, under the DRAFT v0.2 codebook: executives and analysts talk about cyber and capex; Wikipedia covers the field. Draft wording; shares differ from v0.1.
--- ![w:950](deck/cve-ai-credit.svg)
The public CVE record credits Claude on 370 CVEs (2020-01 to 2026-10) and any AI system on 924. That cannot confirm or refute "33,000+": not every flaw becomes a CVE, and credits need not name the tool.
--- ## What this deck does not show - **No effect of Anthropic on any outcome.** Attention and counts only. - **No gold set yet.** Every model-labelled chart is a two-witness proposal; precision is unmeasured. - **Survivorship.** The earnings-call universe is today's S&P 500. - **No news-attention chart.** GDELT's daily series drops days (18 of 31 in October 2026), so it was left out. - **The paper is unsealed.** The sealed version will carry its graph-root hash. input.content:
# The report as a build product

Status: plan, 2026-11-04. Nothing below is built yet except the first deck
(`DECK.md`, hand-assembled).

## Principle

The paper is not edited; it is **built**. An edition is a deterministic function
of one source commit and a few recorded parameters:

    edition = build(source commit, codebook version)

Rerunning the build at the same commit with the same parameters gives the same
bytes. Building produces a **new commit** whose parent is the source commit, so
every edition names exactly the code, data, codebook and prose it came from.

`docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md` at `1afb042` ("v0, finalized") is **edition
v0**. It was written by hand and stays frozen as it is. Editions from v1 on are
built.

## What goes in

1. **Data**: the steps in `dag.yml`. The build refuses to run unless
   `dag.py status` is all `ok`, so every table it reads is locked by hash.
2. **One codebook version** for every model-labelled chart and number in the
   edition. Mixing versions is a build error. This is the fix for the first
   deck, which shows v0.1 charts beside a v0.2-draft chart (executives'
   cybersecurity share reads 36% on one slide and 40% on another).
3. **Charts**: scripts that turn tables into SVG, with the codebook version
   as an argument and printed on the chart.
4. **Bindings**: every number in the prose is a reference to a table cell, a
   computed value, or a Descartes claim id (`docs/descartes-spec.md`). There
   are no hand-typed numbers; a lint fails the build on a bare figure in
   bound prose.
5. **Prose templates**: the argument, written and reviewed by people
   (buzz-saw and brand-voice passes apply to the templates).

## What comes out

An edition folder holding the rendered paper, the deck, the charts it used,
and a stamp file:

- source commit;
- codebook version;
- BLAKE3 of `dag.lock.tsv` (and of the Praxis catalog pin, once the data moves
  there);
- tool versions (Python packages, Marp CLI);
- the BLAKE3 of every output file.

A human signs the stamp (the dataset attestation mechanism, applied to the
edition). Agents never sign.

## Checks the build enforces

- every `dag.yml` step `ok`;
- one codebook version across all charts and bindings;
- every binding resolves; no unbound number in bound prose;
- a rebuild at the source commit is byte-identical.

## First target

`DECK.md` becomes edition output: `deck_charts.py` and the corpus report
charts take `--codebook`, slide captions take their numbers from bindings, and
the build writes the deck with its stamp. The paper template comes later.

## Open decisions

1. **Codebook for the first built edition**: v0.1 (reviewed; analysts'
   questions were never scored against it, so the cross-source chart loses
   them) or v0.2 (all five sources; every chart says DRAFT until its wording is
   approved, OPENQUESTIONS Q2).
2. **Where editions live**: a folder per edition in this repository, git tags
   with release assets, or both.
3. **Whether the build commits by itself** or leaves a tree for a person to
   review and commit.
4. **How bindings and Descartes claims meet**: whether every binding becomes a
   Descartes claim, or only quotes from outside documents do.
5. **Where the data lives** when this runs: here, or the Praxis catalog
   (paused, pending the other session's registry work).

            count(*) FILTER (WHERE lex) AS calls_lexical, count(*) FILTER (WHERE nli) AS calls_witnesses,
            round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE lex) / count(*), 2) AS pct_lexical,
            round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE nli) / count(*), 2) AS pct_witnesses
        FROM cw WHERE year(report_date) >= {FIRST_YEAR} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall()
    head = "year\tcalls\tcalls_lexical\tcalls_witnesses\tpct_lexical\tpct_witnesses\n"
    body = "".join("\t".join(str(x) for x in r) + "\n" for r in rows)
    note = f"# calendar year of call date; {as_of[:4]} runs to {as_of}. Denominator: unique, non-stub S&P 500 calls.\n"
    (REPORT / "ai-risk-by-year.tsv").write_text(note + head + body)
    return rows


def write_ranking(con, as_of: str) -> list[tuple]:
    since = f"DATE '{as_of}' - INTERVAL 1 YEAR"
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE ttm AS SELECT * FROM w WHERE report_date > {since} AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}' AND ai_risk")
    n_firms = con.execute(f"SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol) FROM calls WHERE report_date > {since}").fetchone()[0]
    rows = []
    for t in TYPES:
        firms, wins = con.execute(f"SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol), count(*) FROM ttm WHERE {t}").fetchone()
        rows.append((t, LABELS[t], firms, wins))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-r[2], -r[3], r[0]))
    risk_firms, risk_wins = con.execute("SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol), count(*) FROM ttm").fetchone()
    note = (f"# trailing 12 months to {as_of}: {n_firms} S&P 500 firms held calls; {risk_firms} had >= 1 window "
            f"proposed as ai_risk by both witnesses ({risk_wins} windows). Witness proposals, no gold set.\n")
    (REPORT / "risk-ranking-ttm.tsv").write_text(
        note + "rank\trisk_type\tlabel\tfirms\twindows\n"
        + "".join(f"{i}\t{r[0]}\t{r[1]}\t{r[2]}\t{r[3]}\n" for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1)))
    types_expr = " || ".join(f"CASE WHEN {t} THEN '{t};' ELSE '' END" for t in TYPES)
    con.execute(f"""COPY (SELECT report_date, symbol, speaker, role, rtrim({types_expr}, ';') AS risk_types,
            window_id, replace(replace(text, chr(10), ' '), chr(9), ' ') AS quote
        FROM ttm ORDER BY report_date DESC, symbol, window_id)
        TO '{REPORT / "risk-quotes-ttm.tsv"}' (HEADER, DELIMITER '\t')""")
    return rows

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["duckdb==2.0.0"]
# ///
"""Hacker News focused sets: witness agreement, AI-risk share by month, and the
12-month risk-type ranking set beside the earnings-call ranking. IDs only.

Reads corpus/hacker-news/{months.tsv,windows.parquet} and the two witnesses'
scores in proposals/hacker-news/<set>/. Writes to proposals/hacker-news/report/.
No comment text or username is written; examples are item ids with their HN URL.
A positive is a witness proposal (both >= 0.5), not a finding: there is no gold set.

    uv run scripts/hn_report.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus" / "hacker-news"
PROP = ROOT / "proposals" / "hacker-news"
REPORT = PROP / "report"
EC_RANK = ROOT / "proposals" / "earnings-calls" / "codebook-v0.1" / "report" / "risk-ranking-ttm.tsv"
SETS = ["anthropic", "ai_security"]
TTM = ("2025-09-01", "2026-08-31")   # the archive's last 12 months (it ends 2026-08)
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
from ec_risk_series import LABELS, TYPES  # noqa: E402


def load(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> None:
    parts = []
    for s in SETS:
        parts.append(f"""SELECT '{s}' AS "set", d.window_id, d.hypothesis_id AS h, d.p_entail AS pd, m.p_entail AS pm
            FROM '{PROP / s / 'deberta.parquet'}' d JOIN '{PROP / s / 'modernbert.parquet'}' m USING (window_id, hypothesis_id)""")
    con.execute("CREATE TABLE s AS " + " UNION ALL ".join(parts))
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE w AS SELECT * FROM '{CORPUS / 'windows.parquet'}'""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE f AS SELECT "set", window_id, h, pd >= .5 AND pm >= .5 AS b FROM s""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE wf AS SELECT w.*, f.h, f.b FROM w JOIN f USING ("set", window_id)""")
    # comment-level: a comment carries hypothesis h if any of its windows in the set does
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE c AS SELECT "set", item_id, any_value(day) AS day, h, bool_or(b) AS b
        FROM wf GROUP BY ALL""")


def tsv(path: Path, header: str, rows) -> None:
    with path.open("w") as f:
        f.write(header + "\n")
        for r in rows:
            f.write("\t".join("" if v is None else str(v) for v in r) + "\n")


def agreement(con) -> None:
    rows = con.execute("""SELECT "set", h, count(*) n,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE pd >= .5) n_deberta, count(*) FILTER (WHERE pm >= .5) n_modernbert,
        count(*) FILTER (WHERE pd >= .5 AND pm >= .5) n_both,
        avg((pd >= .5)::INT) a, avg((pm >= .5)::INT) b, avg(((pd >= .5) = (pm >= .5))::INT) po
        FROM s GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2""").fetchall()
    out = []
    for st, h, n, nd, nm, nb, a, b, po in rows:
        pe = a * b + (1 - a) * (1 - b)
        out.append((st, h, n, nd, nm, nb, f"{(po - pe) / (1 - pe):.3f}" if pe < 1 else ""))
    tsv(REPORT / "agreement.tsv", "set\thypothesis\tn_windows\tn_deberta\tn_modernbert\tn_both\tkappa", out)


def by_month(con) -> None:
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE m AS SELECT * FROM read_csv('{CORPUS / 'months.tsv'}', delim='\t', header=true)")
    rows = con.execute("""SELECT m.month, m.n_comments,
        count(DISTINCT c.item_id) FILTER (WHERE c."set" = 'anthropic') anth,
        count(DISTINCT c.item_id) FILTER (WHERE c."set" = 'anthropic' AND c.h = 'ai_risk' AND c.b) anth_risk,
        count(DISTINCT c.item_id) FILTER (WHERE c."set" = 'ai_security') sec,
        count(DISTINCT c.item_id) FILTER (WHERE c."set" = 'ai_security' AND c.h = 'ai_risk' AND c.b) sec_risk
        FROM m LEFT JOIN c ON strftime(c.day, '%Y-%m') = m.month GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall()
    out = [(mo, n, a, ar, f"{100 * a / n:.3f}", f"{100 * ar / a:.1f}" if a else "", s_, sr,
            f"{100 * s_ / n:.3f}") for mo, n, a, ar, s_, sr in rows]
    tsv(REPORT / "by-month.tsv", "month\tn_comments\tn_anthropic\tn_anthropic_ai_risk\tpct_comments_anthropic"
        "\tpct_anthropic_ai_risk\tn_ai_security\tn_ai_security_ai_risk\tpct_comments_ai_security", out)


def ranking(con) -> list[tuple]:
    """Per set: comments with ai_risk AND type (both witnesses), TTM. Share of ai_risk comments."""
    res = []
    for st in SETS:
        base = con.execute(f"""SELECT count(DISTINCT item_id) FROM c WHERE "set" = '{st}' AND h = 'ai_risk' AND b
            AND day BETWEEN '{TTM[0]}' AND '{TTM[1]}'""").fetchone()[0]
        for t in TYPES:
            n = con.execute(f"""SELECT count(DISTINCT x.item_id) FROM c x JOIN c r USING ("set", item_id)
                WHERE x."set" = '{st}' AND x.h = '{t}' AND x.b AND r.h = 'ai_risk' AND r.b
                AND x.day BETWEEN '{TTM[0]}' AND '{TTM[1]}'""").fetchone()[0]
            res.append((st, t, n, base))
    ec = {}
    with EC_RANK.open() as f:
        raw = f.read().splitlines()
    tot = int(re.search(r"\((\d+) windows\)", raw[0]).group(1))   # windows proposed ai_risk
    lines = [x.split("\t") for x in raw if not x.startswith("#")]
    hdr, body = lines[0], lines[1:]
    for r in body:
        ec[r[hdr.index("risk_type")]] = (int(r[hdr.index("windows")]), tot)
    out = []
    for t in TYPES:
        row = [t, LABELS[t], ec[t][0], f"{100 * ec[t][0] / ec[t][1]:.1f}"]
        for st in SETS:
            n, base = next((n, b) for s_, t_, n, b in res if s_ == st and t_ == t)
            row += [n, f"{100 * n / base:.1f}" if base else ""]
        out.append(tuple(row))
    out.sort(key=lambda r: -float(r[5]))
    bases = {st: next(b for s_, _, _, b in res if s_ == st) for st in SETS}
    with (REPORT / "risk-ranking-ttm.tsv").open("w") as f:
        f.write(f"# {TTM[0]}..{TTM[1]}. Share of AI-risk units naming each type (a unit can name several). "
                f"Earnings calls: {ec[TYPES[0]][1]} risk windows, trailing 12 months to 2026-11-04. "
                f"HN: comments proposed ai_risk by both witnesses (anthropic {bases['anthropic']}, "
                f"ai_security {bases['ai_security']}). Witness proposals, no gold set.\n")
        f.write("risk_type\tlabel\tcalls_windows\tcalls_pct\tanthropic_comments\tanthropic_pct"
                "\tai_security_comments\tai_security_pct\n")
        for r in out:
            f.write("\t".join(str(v) for v in r) + "\n")
    return out


def examples(con) -> None:
    """Item ids (no text) of the most confidently risk-typed comments, per set and type, TTM."""
    rows = con.execute(f"""WITH x AS (
          SELECT s."set", w.item_id, s.h, least(s.pd, s.pm) AS p
          FROM s JOIN w USING ("set", window_id)
          WHERE s.h IN ({", ".join(f"'{t}'" for t in TYPES)}) AND s.pd >= .5 AND s.pm >= .5
            AND w.day BETWEEN '{TTM[0]}' AND '{TTM[1]}'
            AND (s."set", s.window_id) IN (SELECT "set", window_id FROM f WHERE h = 'ai_risk' AND b))
        SELECT "set", h, item_id, round(max(p)::DOUBLE, 4) p FROM x GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
        QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY "set", h ORDER BY max(p) DESC, item_id) <= 10
        ORDER BY 1, 2, 4 DESC, 3""").fetchall()
    tsv(REPORT / "examples-ttm.tsv", "set\trisk_type\titem_id\tmin_witness_p\turl",
        [(*r, f"https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id={r[2]}") for r in rows])


def plot(rank: list[tuple]) -> None:
    """Three panels, same row order, one bar per risk type: share of AI-risk units naming it."""
    panels = [("Earnings calls (executives)", 3), ("HN: Anthropic", 5), ("HN: AI security", 7)]
    W, rowh, top, left, pw, gap = 920, 26, 92, 190, 210, 42
    H = top + rowh * len(rank) + 56
    vmax = max(float(r[i]) for r in rank for _, i in panels if r[i] != "")
    vmax = (int(vmax // 10) + 1) * 10
    o = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,sans-serif" role="img" aria-labelledby="t d">',
         '<style>text{fill:#1b1b1b}.m{fill:#5f6368}.g{stroke:#e3e3e3}.b{fill:#2a6f97}</style>',
         f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="#fcfcfb"/>',
         '<title id="t">What kind of AI risk: executives vs Hacker News</title>',
         '<desc id="d">Share of AI-risk passages naming each risk type, in three sources, trailing 12 months.</desc>',
         '<text x="16" y="30" font-size="18" font-weight="600">What kind of AI risk? Executives vs Hacker News</text>',
         f'<text x="16" y="52" font-size="13" class="m">Share of AI-risk units naming each type. Calls: 12 months to 2026-11-04. HN: {TTM[0][:7]} to {TTM[1][:7]}.</text>']
    for k, (name, idx) in enumerate(panels):
        x0 = left + k * (pw + gap)
        o.append(f'<text x="{x0}" y="{top - 12}" font-size="13" font-weight="600">{name}</text>')
        for v in (0, vmax // 2, vmax):
            gx = x0 + pw * v / vmax
            o.append(f'<line x1="{gx:.1f}" x2="{gx:.1f}" y1="{top - 4}" y2="{top + rowh * len(rank)}" class="g"/>')
            o.append(f'<text x="{gx:.1f}" y="{top + rowh * len(rank) + 16}" font-size="11" class="m" text-anchor="middle">{v}%</text>')
        for j, r in enumerate(rank):
            y = top + j * rowh
            v = float(r[idx]) if r[idx] != "" else 0.0
            bw = max(pw * v / vmax, 0.0)
            o.append(f'<g><title>{name}: {escape(r[1])}, {v:.1f}% ({r[idx - 1]} units)</title>'
                     f'<rect x="{x0}" y="{y + 5}" width="{bw:.1f}" height="{rowh - 10}" rx="2" class="b"/>'
                     f'<text x="{x0 + bw + 4:.1f}" y="{y + rowh / 2 + 4}" font-size="11" class="m">{v:.0f}</text></g>')
    for j, r in enumerate(rank):
        o.append(f'<text x="{left - 10}" y="{top + j * rowh + rowh / 2 + 4}" font-size="12" text-anchor="end">{escape(r[1])}</text>')
    o.append(f'<text x="16" y="{H - 12}" font-size="11" class="m">Ordered by HN: Anthropic. Two NLI witnesses must both score ≥ 0.5; a unit can name several types. Witness proposals, no gold set.</text>')
    o.append("</svg>")
    (REPORT / "risk-ranking-ttm.svg").write_text("\n".join(o) + "\n")


def main() -> int:
    REPORT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    con = duckdb.connect()
    load(con)
    agreement(con)
    by_month(con)
    plot(ranking(con))
    examples(con)
    for p in sorted(REPORT.iterdir()):
        print(p.relative_to(ROOT))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "blake3==1.0.11",
#   "duckdb==2.0.0",
#   "matplotlib==3.10.7",
# ]
# ///
"""Build DECK.md as an edition of one source commit and one risk codebook.

    uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft    # write DECK.md, deck/*.svg, deck/STAMP.json
    uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft --check   # exit 1 if a rebuild would change anything

The build is the review step. It writes into the working tree and never
commits. Review `git diff`, then commit the edition yourself. The stamp names
the source commit (HEAD at build time), so the edition commit's parent is the
commit it was built from.

Rules (docs/report-build.md):
  - every dag.yml step must be `ok` (Praxis dag.py status);
  - every input the build reads must be committed and unmodified;
  - one risk codebook for every risk chart and number;
  - every number in the deck comes from a binding computed here; a digit in
    the template outside {{...}} on a caption line fails the build;
  - quotes from the paper are checked against edition v0 at PAPER_V0.
Positive = both witnesses (DeBERTa, ModernBERT) >= 0.5, everywhere.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import blake3
import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import deck_charts  # noqa: E402

TEMPLATE = ROOT / "deck" / "deck.template.md"
OUT_MD = ROOT / "DECK.md"
OUT_DIR = ROOT / "deck"
STAMP = OUT_DIR / "STAMP.json"
EC = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls"
PAPER = "docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md"
PAPER_V0 = "1afb042"
DAG_TOOL = ROOT.parent / "praxis" / "datasets" / "dag.py"
FIRST_YEAR = 2013
RISK_WORD = r"(?i)\brisk(s|y|ier|iest)?\b"

# Risk codebooks this build supports: codebook file, score folder for earnings-call windows,
# the cross-source chart for that codebook, and a status shown on every slide.
CODEBOOKS = {
    "v0.2-draft": {
        "file": "corpus/codebooks/codebook-v0.2-draft.tsv",
        "ec_scores": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.2-draft",
        "dialogue": "proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/dialogue-space.tsv",
        "status": " (DRAFT: wording awaits review)",
    },
}
# Fixed inputs read whatever the codebook (their own codebooks are recorded in the stamp).
FIXED = {
    "question_intents": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/ttm.tsv",
    "question_chart": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/intent-ttm.svg",
    "dialogue_chart": "proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/dialogue-space.svg",
    "cve_monthly_ai": "corpus/cve/monthly-ai.tsv",
}
LABELS = {"regulation": "Regulation", "cyber": "Cybersecurity", "privacy": "Data privacy",
          "accuracy": "Accuracy / hallucination", "bias": "Bias / fairness", "labor": "Jobs / labor",
          "disruption": "Disruption of the business", "capex": "Overspending / capex return",
          "energy": "Energy / power", "supply": "Chip & supply constraints", "ip": "Intellectual property",
          "safety_ethics": "Safety / ethics / misuse"}
QUOTES = {  # binding -> exact text in edition v0 (markdown emphasis and line breaks removed before matching)
    "q_toothless": "Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.",
    "q_365b": "§365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest",
}


def git(*a: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def b3(p: Path) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def label(t: str) -> str:
    return LABELS.get(t, t + " *")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- preconditions
def preflight(cb: dict, inputs: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    errs = []
    r = subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "--quiet", str(DAG_TOOL), "status"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        errs.append("dag.py status is not all ok:\n" + "\n".join(l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if not l.startswith("ok")))
    for p in inputs:
        if not git("ls-files", "--", p).strip():
            errs.append(f"input not committed: {p}")
    dirty = git("status", "--porcelain", "--", *inputs).strip()
    if dirty:
        errs.append("inputs modified since the last commit:\n" + dirty)
    return errs


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- bindings + charts
def flags_sql(scores: Path, h: str) -> str:
    return (f"SELECT d.window_id FROM '{scores / 'deberta.parquet'}' d JOIN '{scores / 'modernbert.parquet'}' m "
            f"USING (window_id, hypothesis_id) WHERE d.hypothesis_id = '{h}' AND d.p_entail >= .5 AND m.p_entail >= .5")


def earnings(cb: dict, b: dict) -> tuple[list[tuple], list[tuple]]:
    con = duckdb.connect()
    scores = ROOT / cb["ec_scores"]
    as_of = str(con.execute(f"SELECT max(report_date) FROM read_csv('{EC / 'calls.tsv'}')").fetchone()[0])
    types = [r["id"] for r in csv.DictReader((ROOT / cb["file"]).open(), delimiter="\t") if r["group"] == "risk_type"]
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE calls AS SELECT symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, report_date
        FROM read_csv('{EC / "calls.tsv"}')
        WHERE (duplicate_of IS NULL OR duplicate_of = '') AND n_paragraphs > 2 AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}'""")
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE w AS SELECT window_id, symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, report_date::DATE AS report_date,
            regexp_matches(text, '{RISK_WORD}') AS lex,
            window_id IN ({flags_sql(scores, 'ai_risk')}) AS ai_risk
        FROM '{EC / "ai-windows.parquet"}'""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE cw AS SELECT c.*, bool_or(w.lex) AS lex, bool_or(w.ai_risk) AS nli
        FROM calls c LEFT JOIN w USING (symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter) GROUP BY ALL""")
    series = con.execute(f"""SELECT year(report_date) AS year, count(*) AS calls,
            round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE lex) / count(*), 2), round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE nli) / count(*), 2)
        FROM cw WHERE year(report_date) >= {FIRST_YEAR} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall()
    since = f"DATE '{as_of}' - INTERVAL 1 YEAR"
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE ttm AS SELECT * FROM w WHERE report_date > {since} AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}' AND ai_risk")
    ranking = []

        "outputs": {k: blake3.blake3(v).hexdigest() for k, v in sorted(outs.items())},

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--codebook", required=True, choices=sorted(CODEBOOKS))
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="rebuild and compare; write nothing that differs")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    before = {p: (ROOT / p).read_bytes() for p in ("DECK.md", "deck/ai-risk-by-year.svg", "deck/risk-ranking-ttm.svg",
                                                   "deck/cve-ai-credit.svg", "deck/STAMP.json") if (ROOT / p).exists()}

          f"with risk codebook {a.codebook}. Review `git diff`, then commit.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "blake3==1.0.11",
#   "duckdb==2.0.0",
#   "matplotlib==3.10.7",
# ]
# ///
"""Build DECK.md as an edition of one source commit and one risk codebook.

    uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft    # write DECK.md, deck/*.svg, deck/STAMP.json
    uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft --check   # exit 1 if a rebuild would change anything

The build is the review step. It writes into the working tree and never
commits. Review `git diff`, then commit the edition yourself. The stamp names
the source commit (HEAD at build time), so the edition commit's parent is the
commit it was built from.

Rules (docs/report-build.md):
  - every dag.yml step must be `ok` (Praxis dag.py status);
  - every input the build reads must be committed and unmodified;
  - one risk codebook for every risk chart and number;
  - every number in the deck comes from a binding computed here; a digit in
    the template outside {{...}} on a caption line fails the build;
  - quotes from the paper are checked against edition v0 at PAPER_V0.
Positive = both witnesses (DeBERTa, ModernBERT) >= 0.5, everywhere.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import blake3
import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import deck_charts  # noqa: E402

TEMPLATE = ROOT / "deck" / "deck.template.md"
OUT_MD = ROOT / "DECK.md"
OUT_DIR = ROOT / "deck"
STAMP = OUT_DIR / "STAMP.json"
EC = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls"
PAPER = "docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md"
PAPER_V0 = "1afb042"
DAG_TOOL = ROOT.parent / "praxis" / "datasets" / "dag.py"
FIRST_YEAR = 2013
RISK_WORD = r"(?i)\brisk(s|y|ier|iest)?\b"

# Risk codebooks this build supports: codebook file, score folder for earnings-call windows,
# the cross-source chart for that codebook, and a status shown on every slide.
CODEBOOKS = {
    "v0.2-draft": {
        "file": "corpus/codebooks/codebook-v0.2-draft.tsv",
        "ec_scores": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.2-draft",
        "dialogue": "proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/dialogue-space.tsv",
        "status": " (DRAFT: wording awaits review)",
    },
}
# Fixed inputs read whatever the codebook (their own codebooks are recorded in the stamp).
FIXED = {
    "question_intents": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/ttm.tsv",
    "question_chart": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/intent-ttm.svg",
    "dialogue_chart": "proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/dialogue-space.svg",
    "cve_monthly_ai": "corpus/cve/monthly-ai.tsv",
}
LABELS = {"regulation": "Regulation", "cyber": "Cybersecurity", "privacy": "Data privacy",
          "accuracy": "Accuracy / hallucination", "bias": "Bias / fairness", "labor": "Jobs / labor",
          "disruption": "Disruption of the business", "capex": "Overspending / capex return",
          "energy": "Energy / power", "supply": "Chip & supply constraints", "ip": "Intellectual property",
          "safety_ethics": "Safety / ethics / misuse"}
QUOTES = {  # binding -> exact text in edition v0 (markdown emphasis and line breaks removed before matching)
    "q_toothless": "Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.",
    "q_365b": "§365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest",
}


def git(*a: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def b3(p: Path) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def label(t: str) -> str:
    return LABELS.get(t, t + " *")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- preconditions
def preflight(cb: dict, inputs: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    errs = []
    r = subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "--quiet", str(DAG_TOOL), "status"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.returncode != 0:
        errs.append("dag.py status is not all ok:\n" + "\n".join(l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if not l.startswith("ok")))
    for p in inputs:
        if not git("ls-files", "--", p).strip():
            errs.append(f"input not committed: {p}")

def flags_sql(scores: Path, h: str) -> str:
    return (f"SELECT d.window_id FROM '{scores / 'deberta.parquet'}' d JOIN '{scores / 'modernbert.parquet'}' m "
            f"USING (window_id, hypothesis_id) WHERE d.hypothesis_id = '{h}' AND d.p_entail >= .5 AND m.p_entail >= .5")

    con = duckdb.connect()

        FROM read_csv('{EC / "calls.tsv"}')
        WHERE (duplicate_of IS NULL OR duplicate_of = '') AND n_paragraphs > 2 AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}'""")
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE w AS SELECT window_id, symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, report_date::DATE AS report_date,
            regexp_matches(text, '{RISK_WORD}') AS lex,

        FROM '{EC / "ai-windows.parquet"}'""")
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE cw AS SELECT c.*, bool_or(w.lex) AS lex, bool_or(w.ai_risk) AS nli

            transform=ax.transAxes, color=S.INK2, fontsize=9)

content.text:
Yes, the v0.2 draft codebook was already scored on all five sources (earnings-call windows, analyst questions, both Hacker News sets and Wikipedia), so nothing needed scoring. Its wording is still the unapproved draft.

The build now works that way, and the first built deck is waiting for your review, uncommitted. Run `uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft` and it:

- **refuses to run** unless every step in the compute graph is up to date and every file it reads is committed and unmodified;
- **builds every risk chart and number from one codebook version**. The analyst-question chart uses its own question codebook, and the stamp records both;
- **fills every number in the slide captions from the tables**. A hand-typed number fails the build. It caught one on its first run ("before 2023"), and I made that a setting;
- **checks the two paper quotes** against the finalized paper at `1afb042`;
- **writes `DECK.md`, three charts and `deck/STAMP.json`** (source commit, codebook, data hashes, tool versions, every number used, every file hash). Rebuilding gives identical files, and `--check` confirms it;
- **never commits.** `git diff` is your review, and your commit is the approval.

The built deck, rendered and checked, has eight slides:
1. Title, stamped with the commit and "v0.2-draft (DRAFT)".
2. The paper's argument, in two quotes checked against the paper.
3. AI as a risk on calls: 12.2% of 2026 calls, against at most 0.6% in any year before 2023. That's under v0.2, against 12.3% under v0.1.
4. Which risks firms named: 137 firms. Cybersecurity was named by 40, safety/ethics by 31, overspending by 26. Loss of control, new in v0.2, was named by 16.
5. What analysts ask: revenue 21.2%, controls 0.8%.
6. Who talks about which risks: safety/ethics is 10% of executives' AI-risk passages, 39% on HN about Anthropic and 61% on Wikipedia.
7. CVEs: Claude is credited on 370, and AI systems on 924.
8. What the deck does not show.

Your review will show three changes from the hand-made deck:
- **The paper's four charts are gone.** `docs/figures/` was never committed (it's another session's work), and a build can't rely on uncommitted files.
- **The executives-vs-HN comparison is dropped.** The five-source chart already covers it, under the same codebook.
- **Edits now go in `deck/deck.template.md`.** `DECK.md` is generated and says so at the top.

While wiring this up I found the captions rounded Wikipedia's 60.5% to 60% while the chart showed 61%. Both now compute from the same counts.

The v0.2 wording, including `bio_chem`, which is known to fail, still needs your review before the "DRAFT" label can come off.

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "blake3==1.0.11",
#   "duckdb==2.0.0",
#   "matplotlib==3.10.7",
# ]
# ///
"""Build DECK.md as an edition of one source commit and one risk codebook.

    uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft          # write DECK.md, deck/*.svg, deck/STAMP.json
    uv run scripts/build_edition.py --codebook v0.2-draft --check  # exit 1 if a rebuild would change anything

The build is the review step: it writes into the working tree and never commits.
Review `git diff`, then commit the edition yourself.

Preconditions (fail closed):
  - every dag.yml step is `ok` (Praxis dag.py status);
  - every input is committed and unmodified.

Display controls (docs/report-build.md; every one fails the build):
  1. Exact inputs. Every number shown is computed from integer counts by
     scripts/display.py: no float, and no rounded table column, is ever shown.
  2. One rounding rule: half up, from the exact fraction.
  3. One source per number. Every chart in the deck is drawn here, from the
     same registered values as the captions, so chart and caption cannot disagree.
  4. Provenance. Every displayed value is registered with its source file,
     computation, numerator and denominator, and written to the stamp.
  5. No unbound numerals. The template may contain no digits outside {{...}}
     (front matter excepted). Every numeral in the built DECK.md, and in every
     chart's text (axis tick labels excepted), must be a registered value.
  6. Quotes. Text in double quotes in the template must be a single quote
     binding, and every quote binding must occur verbatim in edition v0.
  7. Nothing clipped. Every text element of a matplotlib chart lies inside the
     figure. Every SVG parses as XML.
  8. One codebook. Every risk chart and number uses the --codebook given.
Positive = DeBERTa and ModernBERT both >= 0.5, everywhere.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from fractions import Fraction
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

import blake3
import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import display  # noqa: E402

TEMPLATE = ROOT / "deck" / "deck.template.md"
OUT_DIR = ROOT / "deck"
EC = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls"
PAPER, PAPER_V0 = "docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md", "1afb042"
DAG_TOOL = ROOT.parent / "praxis" / "datasets" / "dag.py"
FIRST_YEAR, CUTOFF_YEAR, TTM_MONTHS = 2013, 2023, 12
RISK_WORD = r"(?i)\brisk(s|y|ier|iest)?\b"
THRESHOLD = Fraction(1, 2)

CODEBOOKS = {
    "v0.2-draft": {
        "file": "corpus/codebooks/codebook-v0.2-draft.tsv",
        "ec_scores": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.2-draft",
        "dialogue": "proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/dialogue-space.tsv",
        "status": " (DRAFT: wording awaits review)",
    },
}
QUESTIONS = {"codebook": "v0.1", "file": "corpus/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1.tsv",
             "ttm": "proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/ttm.tsv"}
CVE = "corpus/cve/monthly-ai.tsv"
QUOTES = {  # binding -> exact text in edition v0 (markdown emphasis and line breaks removed before matching)
    "q_toothless": "Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.",
    "q_365b": "§365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest",
    "q_33k": "33,000+",
}
STATIC_TOKENS = {"500"}   # "S&P 500" is a name, not a quantity
DIALOGUE_SOURCES = [("executives", "Executives (calls)"), ("analysts", "Analyst questions"),
                    ("hn_anthropic", "HN: Anthropic"), ("hn_security", "HN: AI security"), ("wikipedia", "Wikipedia")]
LABELS = {"regulation": "Regulation", "cyber": "Cybersecurity", "privacy": "Data privacy",
          "accuracy": "Accuracy / hallucination", "bias": "Bias / fairness", "labor": "Jobs / labor",
          "disruption": "Disruption of the business", "capex": "Overspending / capex return",
          "energy": "Energy / power", "supply": "Chip & supply constraints", "ip": "Intellectual property",
          "safety_ethics": "Safety / ethics / misuse"}
SURFACE, INK, INK2, GRID = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df"
S1, S2, MUTED = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#a8a69f"
META = {"Date": None, "Creator": None}

NUM = re.compile(r"\b(?=[0-9a-f]*[a-f])(?=[0-9a-f]*\d)[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b"   # commit ids
                 r"|\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|\d{4}-\d{2}"                         # dates, months
                 r"|v\d+(?:\.\d+)+(?:-draft)?"                             # versions
                 r"|§\d+\([a-z]\)"                                         # statute sections
                 r"|\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?\+?")                                # numbers


def tokens(s: str) -> set[str]:
    return {m.group(0).rstrip(",") for m in NUM.finditer(s)}


def git(*a: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *a], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def b3(p: Path) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def table(path: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[dict]]:
    with (ROOT / path).open() as f:
        lines = f.read().splitlines()
    comments = [l for l in lines if l.startswith("#")]
    return comments, list(csv.DictReader([l for l in lines if not l.startswith("#")], delimiter="\t"))


class Build:
    def __init__(self, codebook: str) -> None:
        self.codebook, self.cb = codebook, CODEBOOKS[codebook]
        self.reg = display.Registry()
        self.errs: list[str] = []
        self.outs: dict[str, bytes] = {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ preconditions
    def inputs(self) -> list[str]:
        return [self.cb["file"], self.cb["ec_scores"], self.cb["dialogue"], QUESTIONS["file"], QUESTIONS["ttm"], CVE,
                "corpus/earnings-calls/calls.tsv", "corpus/earnings-calls/ai-windows.parquet",
                "deck/deck.template.md", "scripts/build_edition.py", "scripts/display.py", "dag.lock.tsv"]

    def preflight(self) -> bool:
        r = subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "--quiet", str(DAG_TOOL), "status"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            self.errs.append("dag.py status is not all ok:\n" + "\n".join(
                l for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if not l.startswith("ok")))
        for p in self.inputs():
            if not git("ls-files", "--", p).strip():
                self.errs.append(f"input not committed: {p}")
        dirty = git("status", "--porcelain", "--", *self.inputs()).strip()
        if dirty:
            self.errs.append("inputs modified since the last commit:\n" + dirty)
        return not self.errs

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ checks
    def allowed(self) -> set[str]:
        out = set(STATIC_TOKENS)
        for t in self.reg.texts():
            out |= tokens(t)
        return out

    def check_text(self, where: str, s: str) -> None:
        bad = sorted(tokens(s) - self.allowed())
        if bad:
            self.errs.append(f"{where}: unregistered numerals {bad} in {s[:90]!r}")

    def save_fig(self, fig, name: str) -> None:
        import matplotlib
        fig.canvas.draw()
        r = fig.canvas.get_renderer()
        box = fig.bbox
        ticks = set()
        for ax in fig.axes:
            ticks |= set(ax.get_xticklabels()) | set(ax.get_yticklabels())
        for t in fig.findobj(matplotlib.text.Text):
            s = t.get_text()
            if not t.get_visible() or not s.strip():
                continue
            bb = t.get_window_extent(r)
            if bb.x0 < box.x0 - 0.5 or bb.y0 < box.y0 - 0.5 or bb.x1 > box.x1 + 0.5 or bb.y1 > box.y1 + 0.5:
                self.errs.append(f"{name}: text clipped at the figure edge: {s[:60]!r}")
            if t not in ticks:
                self.check_text(name, s)
        path = OUT_DIR / name
        fig.savefig(path, facecolor=SURFACE, metadata=META)
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        plt.close(fig)
        self.outs[f"deck/{name}"] = path.read_bytes()

    def save_svg(self, svg: str, name: str) -> None:
        root = ET.fromstring(svg)
        for el in root.iter():
            if el.tag.split("}")[-1] in ("text", "title", "desc") and el.text:
                self.check_text(name, el.text)
        path = OUT_DIR / name
        path.write_text(svg)
        self.outs[f"deck/{name}"] = path.read_bytes()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ values
    def register_static(self, head: str) -> None:
        R = self.reg
        R.put("codebook", self.codebook, source=self.cb["file"], how="--codebook")
        R.put("codebook_status", self.cb["status"], source="build_edition.CODEBOOKS", how="status of the codebook")
        R.put("question_codebook", QUESTIONS["codebook"], source=QUESTIONS["file"], how="question-intent codebook")
        R.put("source_commit", head[:12], source="git", how="HEAD at build time")
        R.put("paper_v0", PAPER_V0, source="git", how="edition v0 commit of the paper")
        R.put("threshold", display.round_half_up(THRESHOLD, 1), source="build_edition.THRESHOLD", how="both witnesses >= this")
        R.put("ttm_months", str(TTM_MONTHS), source="build_edition.TTM_MONTHS", how="trailing window, months")
        R.put("ec_cutoff_year", str(CUTOFF_YEAR), source="build_edition.CUTOFF_YEAR", how="comparison year")
        new = {r["status"].split()[0] for r in table(self.cb["file"])[1] if r["status"].startswith("v0.2")}
        for i, v in enumerate(sorted(new)):
            R.put(f"new_tag_{i}", v, source=self.cb["file"], how="status column of hypotheses new in this codebook")
        text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", git("show", f"{PAPER_V0}:{PAPER}").replace("**", "").replace("*", ""))
        for k, q in QUOTES.items():
            if q not in text:
                self.errs.append(f"quote {k} not found verbatim in {PAPER}@{PAPER_V0}: {q!r}")
            R.put(k, q, source=f"{PAPER}@{PAPER_V0}", how="verbatim quote (emphasis and line breaks removed)")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ earnings calls
    def earnings(self) -> None:
        R, cb = self.reg, self.cb
        scores = ROOT / cb["ec_scores"]
        con = duckdb.connect()
        as_of = str(con.execute(f"SELECT max(report_date) FROM read_csv('{EC / 'calls.tsv'}')").fetchone()[0])
        R.put("as_of", as_of, source="corpus/earnings-calls/calls.tsv", how="max(report_date)")

        def flags(h: str) -> str:
            return (f"SELECT d.window_id FROM '{scores / 'deberta.parquet'}' d JOIN '{scores / 'modernbert.parquet'}' m "
                    f"USING (window_id, hypothesis_id) WHERE d.hypothesis_id = '{h}' "
                    f"AND d.p_entail >= {float(THRESHOLD)} AND m.p_entail >= {float(THRESHOLD)}")
        types = [r["id"] for r in table(cb["file"])[1] if r["group"] == "risk_type"]
        new = {r["id"] for r in table(cb["file"])[1] if r["status"].startswith("v0.2")}
        con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE calls AS SELECT symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, report_date
            FROM read_csv('{EC / "calls.tsv"}')
            WHERE (duplicate_of IS NULL OR duplicate_of = '') AND n_paragraphs > 2 AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}'""")
        con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE w AS SELECT window_id, symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter,
                report_date::DATE AS report_date, regexp_matches(text, '{RISK_WORD}') AS lex,
                window_id IN ({flags('ai_risk')}) AS ai_risk
            FROM '{EC / "ai-windows.parquet"}'""")
        con.execute("""CREATE TABLE cw AS SELECT c.*, bool_or(w.lex) AS lex, bool_or(w.ai_risk) AS nli
            FROM calls c LEFT JOIN w USING (symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter) GROUP BY ALL""")
        series = con.execute(f"""SELECT year(report_date)::INT, count(*)::INT,
                (count(*) FILTER (WHERE lex))::INT, (count(*) FILTER (WHERE nli))::INT
            FROM cw WHERE year(report_date) >= {FIRST_YEAR} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall()
        src = f"corpus/earnings-calls/{{calls.tsv,ai-windows.parquet}} + {cb['ec_scores']}"
        for y, n, lex, nli in series:
            R.pct(f"ec_lex_{y}", lex, n, 1, source=src, how=f"{y}: calls with a 'risk' word in an AI window / calls")
            R.pct(f"ec_nli_{y}", nli, n, 1, source=src, how=f"{y}: calls with an ai_risk window (both witnesses) / calls")
        last = series[-1]
        R.put("ec_year_last", str(last[0]), source=src, how="last calendar year in the series")
        R.put("ec_pct_witness_last", R.values[f"ec_nli_{last[0]}"]["text"], source=src, how="= ec_nli_<last year>")
        pre = max((r for r in series if r[0] < CUTOFF_YEAR), key=lambda r: Fraction(r[3], r[1]))
        R.put("ec_pre2023_max", R.values[f"ec_nli_{pre[0]}"]["text"], source=src,
              how=f"max over years < {CUTOFF_YEAR} of ec_nli_<year> (attained {pre[0]})")

        since = f"DATE '{as_of}' - INTERVAL {TTM_MONTHS} MONTH"
        con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE ttm AS SELECT * FROM w WHERE report_date > {since} AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}' AND ai_risk")
        ranking = []
        for t in types:
            firms = con.execute(f"SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol)::INT FROM ttm WHERE window_id IN ({flags(t)})").fetchone()[0]
            lab = LABELS.get(t, t) + (" *" if t in new else "")
            ranking.append((t, lab, firms))
            R.count(f"ec_rank_{t}", firms, source=src, how=f"firms with a window both ai_risk and {t}, trailing window")
        ranking.sort(key=lambda r: (-r[2], r[0]))
        R.count("ec_ttm_risk_firms", con.execute("SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol)::INT FROM ttm").fetchone()[0],
                source=src, how="firms with >= 1 ai_risk window, trailing window")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ cross-source dialogue space
    def dialogue(self) -> None:
        R, cb = self.reg, self.cb
        comments, rows = table(cb["dialogue"])
        base = next(r for r in rows if r["risk_type"] == "ai_risk_units")
        bases = {k: int(base[f"{k}_n"]) for k, _ in DIALOGUE_SOURCES}
        types = [r for r in rows if r["risk_type"] != "ai_risk_units"]
        for k, _ in DIALOGUE_SOURCES:
            R.count(f"ds_base_{k}", bases[k], source=cb["dialogue"], how=f"{k} AI-risk units")
        for r in types:
            for k, _ in DIALOGUE_SOURCES:
                n = int(r[f"{k}_n"])
                R.pct(f"ds_{k}_{r['risk_type']}", n, bases[k], 0, source=cb["dialogue"], how=f"{k}: {r['risk_type']} / AI-risk units")
                R.pct(f"ds1_{k}_{r['risk_type']}", n, bases[k], 1, source=cb["dialogue"], how="same, one decimal (tooltip)")
                R.count(f"dsn_{k}_{r['risk_type']}", n, source=cb["dialogue"], how=f"{k}: {r['risk_type']} units")
        for key, (src, t) in {"ds_exec_safety": ("executives", "safety_ethics"), "ds_hn_safety": ("hn_anthropic", "safety_ethics"),
                              "ds_wp_safety": ("wikipedia", "safety_ethics"), "ds_sec_cyber": ("hn_security", "cyber")}.items():
            R.put(key, R.values[f"ds_{src}_{t}"]["text"], source=cb["dialogue"], how=f"= ds_{src}_{t}")
        rows_sorted = sorted(types, key=lambda r: (-max(Fraction(int(r[f'{k}_n']), bases[k]) for k, _ in DIALOGUE_SOURCES),
                                                   r["risk_type"]))
        cw, rh, left, top = 128, 24, 210, 108
        W, H = left + cw * len(DIALOGUE_SOURCES) + 24, top + rh * len(rows_sorted) + 64

        def fill(n: int, d: int) -> str:
            t = min(Fraction(100 * n, d) / 50, Fraction(1))
            lo, hi = (236, 243, 249), (16, 70, 120)
            return "#%02x%02x%02x" % tuple(int(display.round_half_up(a + (b - a) * t, 0)) for a, b in zip(lo, hi))
        o = [f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}" font-family="system-ui,-apple-system,sans-serif" role="img">',
             '<style>text{fill:#1b1b1b}.m{fill:#5f6368}</style>', f'<rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="{SURFACE}"/>',
             '<text x="16" y="30" font-size="18" font-weight="600">Who talks about which AI risks</text>',
             f'<text x="16" y="52" font-size="12" class="m">Share of each source\'s AI-risk passages naming each type. '
             f'Risk codebook {escape(self.codebook)}; * = new in {R.values["new_tag_0"]["text"]}.</text>']
        for j, (k, label) in enumerate(DIALOGUE_SOURCES):
            x = left + j * cw + cw / 2
            o.append(f'<text x="{x}" y="{top - 24}" font-size="12" font-weight="600" text-anchor="middle">{escape(label)}</text>')
            o.append(f'<text x="{x}" y="{top - 9}" font-size="11" class="m" text-anchor="middle">n = {R.values[f"ds_base_{k}"]["text"]}</text>')
        new = {r["risk_type"] for r in rows if r.get("new_in_v0.2") == "yes"}
        for i, r in enumerate(rows_sorted):
            t = r["risk_type"]
            y = top + i * rh
            o.append(f'<text x="{left - 8}" y="{y + rh / 2 + 4}" font-size="12" text-anchor="end">{escape(t)}{" *" if t in new else ""}</text>')
            for j, (k, label) in enumerate(DIALOGUE_SOURCES):
                n, d = int(r[f"{k}_n"]), bases[k]
                txt = R.values[f"ds_{k}_{t}"]["text"]
                ink = "#ffffff" if Fraction(100 * n, d) >= 25 else "#1b1b1b"
                o.append(f'<g><title>{escape(label)}: {escape(t)} {R.values[f"ds1_{k}_{t}"]["text"]}% '
                         f'({R.values[f"dsn_{k}_{t}"]["text"]} of {R.values[f"ds_base_{k}"]["text"]})</title>'
                         f'<rect x="{left + j * cw + 1}" y="{y + 1}" width="{cw - 2}" height="{rh - 2}" rx="2" fill="{fill(n, d)}"/>'
                         f'<text x="{left + j * cw + cw / 2}" y="{y + rh / 2 + 4}" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" style="fill:{ink}">{txt}</text></g>')
        o.append(f'<text x="16" y="{H - 30}" font-size="11" class="m">n = passages both NLI witnesses score ≥ '
                 f'{R.values["threshold"]["text"]} on ai_risk; a cell needs both on the type too. A passage can name several types.</text>')
        o.append(f'<text x="16" y="{H - 14}" font-size="11" class="m">Windows as in {escape(cb["dialogue"])}. '
                 'Witness proposals, no gold set.</text>')
