# HTML evidence recipe: static-v1

`html-to-text` with the single fixed argument `static-v1` is a general,
source-independent recipe implemented in `tools/html_to_text.py`. It never
accepts a quotation, selector or source-specific option. Raw originals remain
pinned; claims refer to the derived text, not to silently normalized HTML.

Run the same command for every supported input:

```sh
/usr/bin/python3 -I -B tools/html_to_text.py --recipe static-v1 sources/example.html derived/example.txt
```

Register a tab-separated row in `derived/recipes.tsv`:

```text
derived/example.txt sources/example.html html-to-text static-v1
```

The example above shows columns separated by spaces for readability; the file
requires tabs. The loop replays the recipe in its tools sandbox and compares
bytes before recording a derivation node. Its tool identity includes the recipe
version, Python version, script SHA-256 and interpreter executable SHA-256.
The inventoried script also enters the graph. The Python standard library and
platform remain assumptions; an executable digest alone does not pin all runtime
libraries. Changed output is drift, never automatic acceptance.

## Exact transformation

Decode UTF-8 strictly (an initial BOM is permitted). Parse HTML using Python's
standard HTMLParser and decode character references. Exclude head, script,
style and template content; exclude hidden elements and inline display:none or
visibility:hidden/collapse subtrees. Keep text in document order. Insert a space
at block boundaries, preserve inline adjacency, collapse Unicode whitespace to
one ASCII space, trim the ends, and append one LF. Do not deduplicate document
text: two real occurrences still fail the unique-quote check. No JavaScript runs,
network fetch occurs, sentence rewriting occurs or quotation-specific rule exists.

## Visibility boundary

This is a static document text projection, not a browser rendering or proof of
historical visual appearance. CSS stylesheets and external stylesheet links,
embedded documents, SVG/canvas and noscript fail explicitly because visibility
or content cannot be reconstructed by this recipe. Scripts are excluded as data;
script-generated text absent from the pinned document cannot be recovered.
Inline styling beyond the explicit hiding rules, layout order, generated CSS
content, animation, form state and browser state are not modeled. Such sources
need a separately pinned rendered capture and recipe; this version must not be
presented as universal HTML support. A historical URL alone cannot recover the
page's original browser state. Independent review must confirm applicability.

## Checks and observed result

`/usr/bin/python3 -I -B tests/html/test_recipe.py` covers split blocks, entities,
script duplicates, real visible duplicates, inline adjacency, hidden content,
unsupported input, deterministic CLI replay and failure without a new output.
`sh stage1/test-html-recipe.sh` repeats these inside the loop's tools sandbox
and rejects changed derived bytes.

The pinned S-1 SHA-256 is
`6297a2c2c64c7d8c65de5c481793ac4312111c85d3f6b057dac17bfe28f74dc8`.
The unchanged reported Q012, Q014, Q016 and Q017 quotations each occur exactly
once in its derived text. Counts are in `docs/bugs/html-text-probe.tsv`.
This does not settle other paper quotations, editorial judgment, or the paper's
seal. Broader rendering support remains open on Entire bug 25.
derived/papers/visser2023.txt	sources/papers/visser2023.pdf	pdftotext	-enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk
derived/witness/ai2/securities-master-context.txt	sources/witness/ai2/securities-master-context.pdf	pdftotext	-enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk
tests/html/static.txt	tests/html/static.html	html-to-text	static-v1
    name == id(content); encode(parse(content)) == content
    exact keys for its kind; every link resolves to the right kind
    artifact:    the blob's size and sha256 match
    claim:       rests on something; each evidence slice lies inside its
                 artifact and re-hashes to slice_blake3; lists strictly sorted
    attestation: the signature verifies over the subject
  fail on any cycle

loop(tracked inputs) -> root:
  env -i, allowlisted variables only
  boundary(tree)                                 -- nothing secret or stray is in the tree
  stage0 --check   == artifacts/stage0/<os>-<arch>.tsv
  build twice, sandboxed, vendored, offline      -- the two binaries must be identical
  our sha256       == stage0's sha256, for every inventoried file
  re-run derivations, sandboxed                  -- output == committed derived/*
  ingest inventoried files + claims/*.tsv
  root  = snapshot(nodes this run produced)
  verify(store); rebuild into an empty store; root' == root; verify_root(root')
  results          == artifacts/stage1/<os>-<arch>.tsv, artifacts/loss/*   -- byte for byte
```

## 4. The graph

`.descartes/` is the store: plain files you can check with `cat` and `b3sum`.
It is a projection, not committed. The loop rebuilds it from tracked inputs:
code, `sources/`, `claims/` and `attestations/`. Git holds code, vendored
crates, manifests and the human-readable inputs, never the store. Any index
added later is a disposable cache, never a source of truth.

```
.descartes/blobs/<ab>/<blake3>     raw bytes, named by their BLAKE3 hash
.descartes/objects/<ab>/<blake3>   nodes, canonical JSON, named by the hash of that encoding
```

There are five node kinds. Each has an exact key set; a missing or extra key
is an error.

| Kind | Keys | The verifier checks |
|---|---|---|
| `artifact` | `blob`, `bytes`, `media_type`, `name`, `sha256` | the blob exists and its size and SHA-256 match |
| `claim` | `statement`, `witness`, `evidence` (each: `artifact`, `start`, `end`, `slice_blake3`), `supports` | it rests on something; each range is non-empty and inside its artifact; each slice re-hashes to its digest; `supports` links are claims |
   Whitespace conversion is part of the recorded derivation, never a change
   to the quote checker. A text projection alone does not prove historical
   browser appearance.
2. **Witness.** An LLM, following `prompts/distill.md`, writes
   `proposals/<name>.tsv`. Leaves quote the text byte for byte; composites
   rest on other claims. The `witness` column names the model and the
   SHA-256 of the prompt.
3. **Check.** `descartes check FILE` reports every problem and writes
   nothing:
   - a quote that does not occur exactly once;
   - a claim with no evidence;
   - a dangling label;
   - a cycle.

   A failed claim fails every composite that rests on it.
4. **Accept.** A file with zero problems moves to `claims/`. Ingest is
   all-or-nothing per file.

The file format is six tab-separated columns:
`label rests_on witness statement path quote` (`src/claims.rs`). Evidence
paths must be relative, visible, free of symlinks and single-linked, and
inside the repo.

The verifier proves that a quote **exists**. It does not prove that the
statement **follows** from it. An LLM-witnessed claim is testimony until a
person concurs, and nothing records that concurrence yet.

Two more measures of what a step kept:
- **Fidelity** (`stage1/fidelity.sh`) colours each part of a derivation by
  the highest circle of assumption at which it is verified
  (`docs/circles.md`).

Register a tab-separated row in `derived/recipes.tsv`:

```text
derived/example.txt sources/example.html html-to-text static-v1
```

The example above shows columns separated by spaces for readability; the file
requires tabs. The loop replays the recipe in its tools sandbox and compares
bytes before recording a derivation node. Its tool identity includes the recipe
version, Python version, script SHA-256 and interpreter executable SHA-256.
The inventoried script also enters the graph. The Python standard library and
platform remain assumptions; an executable digest alone does not pin all runtime
libraries. Changed output is drift, never automatic acceptance.

## Exact transformation

Decode UTF-8 strictly (an initial BOM is permitted). Parse HTML using Python's
standard HTMLParser and decode character references. Exclude head, script,
style and template content; exclude hidden elements and inline display:none or
visibility:hidden/collapse subtrees. Keep text in document order. Insert a space
at block boundaries, preserve inline adjacency, collapse Unicode whitespace to
one ASCII space, trim the ends, and append one LF. Do not deduplicate document
text: two real occurrences still fail the unique-quote check. No JavaScript runs,
network fetch occurs, sentence rewriting occurs or quotation-specific rule exists.

## Visibility boundary

This is a static document text projection, not a browser rendering or proof of
historical visual appearance. CSS stylesheets and external stylesheet links,
embedded documents, SVG/canvas and noscript fail explicitly because visibility
or content cannot be reconstructed by this recipe. Scripts are excluded as data;
script-generated text absent from the pinned document cannot be recovered.
Inline styling beyond the explicit hiding rules, layout order, generated CSS
content, animation, form state and browser state are not modeled. Such sources
need a separately pinned rendered capture and recipe; this version must not be
presented as universal HTML support. A historical URL alone cannot recover the
page's original browser state. Independent review must confirm applicability.

## Checks and observed result

`/usr/bin/python3 -I -B tests/html/test_recipe.py` covers split blocks, entities,
script duplicates, real visible duplicates, inline adjacency, hidden content,
unsupported input, deterministic CLI replay and failure without a new output.
`sh stage1/test-html-recipe.sh` repeats these inside the loop's tools sandbox
and rejects changed derived bytes.

This does not settle other paper quotations, editorial judgment, or the paper's

## 4. The graph

`.descartes/` is the store: plain files you can check with `cat` and `b3sum`.
It is a projection, not committed. The loop rebuilds it from tracked inputs:
code, `sources/`, `claims/` and `attestations/`. Git holds code, vendored
crates, manifests and the human-readable inputs, never the store. Any index
added later is a disposable cache, never a source of truth.

```
.descartes/blobs/<ab>/<blake3>     raw bytes, named by their BLAKE3 hash
.descartes/objects/<ab>/<blake3>   nodes, canonical JSON, named by the hash of that encoding
```

There are five node kinds. Each has an exact key set; a missing or extra key
is an error.

| Kind | Keys | The verifier checks |
|---|---|---|
| `artifact` | `blob`, `bytes`, `media_type`, `name`, `sha256` | the blob exists and its size and SHA-256 match |
| `claim` | `statement`, `witness`, `evidence` (each: `artifact`, `start`, `end`, `slice_blake3`), `supports` | it rests on something; each range is non-empty and inside its artifact; each slice re-hashes to its digest; `supports` links are claims |
   Whitespace conversion is part of the recorded derivation, never a change
   to the quote checker. A text projection alone does not prove historical
   browser appearance.
2. **Witness.** An LLM, following `prompts/distill.md`, writes
   `proposals/<name>.tsv`. Leaves quote the text byte for byte; composites
   rest on other claims. The `witness` column names the model and the
   SHA-256 of the prompt.
3. **Check.** `descartes check FILE` reports every problem and writes
   nothing:
   - a quote that does not occur exactly once;
   - a claim with no evidence;
   - a dangling label;
   - a cycle.

   A failed claim fails every composite that rests on it.
4. **Accept.** A file with zero problems moves to `claims/`. Ingest is
   all-or-nothing per file.

The file format is six tab-separated columns:
`label rests_on witness statement path quote` (`src/claims.rs`). Evidence
paths must be relative, visible, free of symlinks and single-linked, and
inside the repo.

The verifier proves that a quote **exists**. It does not prove that the
statement **follows** from it. An LLM-witnessed claim is testimony until a
person concurs, and nothing records that concurrence yet.

**Separation of authority:** this repo still runs the recipes itself and only records what it did. That needs the adapter the other session said Descartes's paper registry lacks. I'd hand that to the Descartes session, with the 18 PDF line-break failures as its first test.

content.text: Trail #25 already covers HTML quotes. I'm creating a new trail for coordination between Descartes and articles, and linking it to #25:

input.content:
Intent (Sloane, 2026-11-04): articles are built from Descartes output, modularly. Nothing an article states about its own verification is written by hand, and a statement whose evidence is invalidated fixes or flags itself.

First article: anthropic-pbc `docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md` (claims `claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.tsv`, sources `sources/MANIFEST.tsv`).

## 1. One authority for source text
Descartes ingests an article's pinned sources (its MANIFEST) and claims, runs the recorded recipes and owns the derived text. The article repository holds the paper, the claims and the manifest, and runs no recipe itself. Today anthropic-pbc runs pdftotext and html-to-text locally and records the result with `descartes derive`: two places produce text. Needs the paper-registry adapter (descartes docs/public-mirror/integration-status.md).

## 2. Generated status, never hand counts
The article's "Verification status" (claims ok / failing, per cause, per claim) is emitted by Descartes as data and included in the article at build time. Found stale: §5.3 still says "51 of 60" while the check reports 72 ok / 22 failing.

## 3. Invalidation propagates
Every article statement that rests on evidence is a claim with `rests_on`, including composite and negative statements. When a leaf fails, or a pinned source contradicts it, every statement resting on it fails and the article marks it at build time, without hand edits. Case: the paper said three times that the S-1 is silent on the four-model unauthorized-access incident; the S-1 risk factors disclose it. A negative claim ("source A does not mention X") needs a checkable form, e.g. a recorded search over the derived text, which fails when a match appears. Design open.

## 4. PDF whitespace in the recipe
README §8: whitespace conversion is part of the recorded derivation, never the checker. The PDF recipe keeps printed line breaks (and the RSP's U+200B at line edges), so 18 faithful quotations fail (Constitution 11, Report 6, RSP 1). First test case for 1–3.

## 5. Rendered pages
Pages with external stylesheets are refused by html-to-text static-v1: trail #25. Blocks the Public Benefit Fund announcement, DGCL, two SEC pages, and two Anthropic pages (Q048, Q084).

Done when: one command rebuilds the article's status from pinned sources and claims, byte-identically, and changing a source flips every dependent statement without a hand edit.

The mechanism for everyone's future is owned by the few who can sue. The constituency that *can* act is the **institutional investor class** — pensions and their fiduciaries, i.e. the public's own long-term money, which sits behind Anthropic's early investors and carries both the standing and the duty. This paper is written to get them off the sidelines. #### Verification status (this draft) Run through the Descartes loop on 2026-11-03: **60 load-bearing fragments the draft attributes to the PBC Report / S-1 were checked; 51 are byte-exact in the filing** (`descartes check` exit 0 on the uniquely-anchorable set). content.text:
I fixed all three errors in the paper and opened Entire trail #26 for the coordination between Descartes and articles.

**The fixes (commit `0655261`):**
- **S-1 contradiction.** §6.3.1, Appendix A and GOV-10 no longer call the S-1 silent. §6.3.1 now quotes the S-1's risk factor: "Four of our models gained unauthorized access to real third-party systems". That is new claim Q094, and it occurs exactly once in the S-1.
- **Wrong source in §7.1.** "Pacing the frontier" is now attributed to the S-1, with its own scope: industry-wide standards, and in its words the call "does not describe our own model development".
- **Stale counts.** I took the hand-written "51 of 60" out of §5.3. The section now points to the unedited check record, which the build will replace with Descartes's own output. Figure 1 is withdrawn for the same reason: its counts were typed into `figures/build.py`.
- **Check result:** 73 claims pass and 22 fail, the same 22 as before. Q094 passes.

**Trail #26 covers what you described:**
1. **One authority for source text.** Descartes ingests an article's pinned sources and claims and owns the derived text. The article repo runs no recipes itself.
2. **Generated status.** Counts, per-claim states and charts of them come from Descartes output at build time.
3. **Invalidation propagates.** Every statement that rests on evidence becomes a claim, so when its evidence fails or a source contradicts it, the statement fails and the paper marks it automatically. Statements that a source says nothing about something (like "the S-1 is silent") need a checkable form, such as a recorded search of the source text that fails when a match appears. That design is open in the trail.
4. **Line breaks from PDFs are handled in the recipe**, with the 18 failing quotes as the first test.
5. **Rendered web pages**, linked to trail #25.

The S-1 error didn't fix itself because "the S-1 is silent" was never a claim, only prose, so nothing could invalidate it. Item 3 is for that case.

The other three charts in the gallery (figs 2–4) also take their numbers typed into `figures/build.py`, not generated from the claims. They will go stale the same way, and they belong under item 2. Pulling them now is your call.

## 2. What Anthropic says it is

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation: a company incorporated under
Delaware's corporate statute, the Delaware General Corporation Law (DGCL),
whose charter names a public purpose and whose directors must balance that
purpose against stockholders' interests and those materially affected (§4.1).
In the Report's words, Anthropic's charter *"is to responsibly develop and
maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity."* Its board has adopted five pillars, each describing a world
"where AI has gone well": the technical problems of AI safety are solved; AI
safety is a universal practice backstopped by law; AI strengthens democracy and
global stability; AI expands prosperity and human flourishing; AI's benefits are
shared by everyone (§5.2, §6.7). Anthropic reports on them in its 2026 Public
Benefit Report, a 20-page document; by statute such a report goes to
stockholders every two years, not to the public (§4.1).

input.content:
## 6. Location: say exactly where (Sloane, 2026-11-04: "it is important to be very, very precise about where we find shit")

Every claim resolves to a precise location in its source: the document (form, exhibit, filing date, accession), the section, the printed page, and the byte offsets Descartes already stores in each evidence node. Descartes emits the location; the article's citations are rendered from it, never typed.

Worked example, anthropic-pbc S-1/A No. 1 (accession 0001628280-26-068676): EDGAR prints each page number followed by a "Table of Contents" link (381 footers, page 4 has none), and the table of contents maps pages to sections. Mapped by hand, outside any committed code, so it is evidence for the design, not a record:
- Q094 "Four of our models gained unauthorized access…": p.49, Risk Factors.
- Q006: p.13, Prospectus Summary.
- Q079: p.252, Our Governance Structure and Its Goals.
- Q054: p.3, Select Defined Terms.

**Repeated passages.** The prospectus summary restates the body, so the same words occur in one filing more than once. The quote stays the source's words; the location picks the occurrence. Do not lengthen the quote to make it unique. Cases:
- Q010 occurs 7 times: cover p.i; Summary pp.6 and 13; MD&A p.135; Business pp.184, 199 and 239.
- Q013 occurs twice: Summary p.6; Business p.185.
The claims format needs a location qualifier (section and/or page) that selects one occurrence, checked as strictly as the quote.

**Why it matters (found today):** Article III of the certificate in effect (Exhibit 3.1 to S-1/A No. 1) reads "for the long term benefit of humanity"; the IPO form (Exhibit 3.3 to the original S-1, 2026-10-26) reads "long-term". The paper had quoted the Report's rendering as "the charter".

Being precise about where things are found turned up a real difference. The paper had been quoting the Report's version of the charter as "the charter". The actual certificates differ by one hyphen:
- **The certificate in force now** (Exhibit 3.1 to Amendment No. 1, filed 2026-11-02), Article III: "…advanced AI for the long term benefit of humanity."
- **The form that takes effect when the IPO completes** (Exhibit 3.3 to the original S-1, filed 2026-10-26): "long-term", with the hyphen.

§2 now quotes Article III from both certificates, each with its exhibit, filing and link. I pinned Exhibit 3.3, and both new quotes pass the check: 75 claims pass now. Committed as `4309137`.

**The summary and the body of the S-1.** As you said, they are one filing that repeats itself. I mapped every S-1 quote to its printed page and section, using EDGAR's page footers and the filing's table of contents:
- Q094, the four models, is on p. 49, Risk Factors.
- Q010 appears 7 times: the cover, the Summary (pp. 6 and 13), MD&A (p. 135) and Business (pp. 184, 199 and 239).
- Q013 appears in the Summary (p. 6) and in Business (p. 185).

The fix for repeated passages is to name which occurrence a quote comes from, by section and page, and check that as strictly as the words. Lengthening the quote until it occurs once would be fitting the check.

**Trail #26** now has a sixth item: every claim gets an exact location, generated by Descartes rather than typed in:
- the document: form, exhibit, filing date and accession number;
- the section and printed page;
- the byte offsets Descartes already stores for each quote.

The paper's citations would be built from that. The S-1 page map is in the trail as the worked example. I didn't commit it as data, because hand-made locations would go stale just like the counts did.

The other 46 "S-1" citations in the paper still don't name a section or page. I've left them until Descartes can generate locations, so we don't type in page numbers that will drift.

Intent (Sloane, 2026-11-04): monitoring around Descartes for efficiency.

## Constraint
Timings are nondeterministic, and no clock may enter a Descartes output (loop results are compared byte for byte). Measurements go to a separate side channel, keyed by run root and input digests, never into `artifacts/`, the store or the graph.

## What to measure, per run
- Each loop step (stage0 check, double build, derivations, ingest, snapshot, verify, rebuild-into-empty, verify_root): wall time, CPU time, peak memory.
- Bytes read and written per step; store size and object count; new blobs vs reused blobs (a check on "pin once": the same text pinned twice shows up here).
- `descartes check` per claims file: wall, CPU, memory, claims checked, bytes scanned.
- Host, OS/arch, binary sha256, so runs on different machines never merge silently.

## Baseline (2026-11-04, darwin-arm64, release build, warm cache)
`descartes check claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.tsv` (anthropic-pbc, 119 claim rows, 16 pinned sources): 0.43–0.46 s wall, ~0.08 s CPU, 5.5 MB peak RSS, three runs. Wall time is about 5× CPU time: the gap is unexplained (process start, file reads per quote?) and is the first thing to look at.
Local store `.descartes/` in anthropic-pbc: 19 MB, 35 files.
The loop has no timing yet.

## Done when
A loop or check run leaves one row of measurements in the side channel, a regression beyond a set threshold is reported, and nothing measured changes any byte the loop compares.

**Short IDs: yes for sources, no for the paper.** And the IDs should be computed from the text, not assigned.

- **In pinned sources, yes.** Descartes would split each source's text into blocks and give each block a short ID, such as 5 characters of its BLAKE3 hash. A quote then cites `s1a1 · p.49 · k7f3q`: readable and quotable, and anyone can recompute it from the pinned bytes. It also solves the repeated passages: the ID picks the occurrence, so Q010's seven appearances become seven distinct, citable locations without lengthening any quote. Pinned bytes never change, so the IDs never drift.
- **Computed, not assigned.** An assigned ID needs a registry that someone maintains, which is the hand-written-counts problem again. A hash-derived ID needs no registry, and Descartes already checks it is unique within the document. Five base-32 characters give about 33 million values, so a clash within one filing is unlikely, and if one happens the check fails loudly.
- **In the paper, no.** The paper changes every day, so IDs computed from its text would change on every edit. It already has stable IDs, the claim labels (Q094 and so on), and the build can print them as markers beside each quotation. The trail runs from paper marker to claim row to source block to bytes.

Readers who click through to a live web page can also get a W3C text-fragment link (`#:~:text=…`), which jumps to the passage in the browser. That's a convenience on top, not the record. I'd add the block IDs to trail #26 item 6 as the way to do location; say so and I'll put it there.

**Efficiency monitoring** is now Entire trail #27. The constraint is that timings vary from run to run, and nothing time-based may enter a Descartes output, because the loop compares its outputs byte for byte. So the measurements go to a separate log keyed by run, never into the record.
- **Measured per step of the loop:** time, CPU, memory and bytes; store growth; and new versus reused blobs, which would also show any text pinned twice.
- **Baseline:** `descartes check` on this paper (97 claim rows, 15 sources) takes about 0.45 s wall time but only 0.08 s of CPU. That fivefold gap is unexplained and is the first thing to look at. The loop records no timings yet, and I didn't run it, because the Descartes repo has another session's staged work.

Intent (Sloane, 2026-11-04): monitoring around Descartes for efficiency.

## Direction: a periodic full-corpus run
"We want to be able to run Descartes over our entire corpus every once in a while. So the direction for optimization is that." (Sloane, 2026-11-04.) Optimize for the full sweep, not for one paper.

Scale today, anthropic-pbc alone: about 11 GB of pinned bulk (`.hncorpus` 5.4 GB, `.eccorpus` 2.8 GB, `.rfcorpus` 1.5 GB, `.cvecorpus` 1.3 GB, the others ~30 MB) plus 38 MB committed under `corpus/`; the paper's sources are ~20 MB. A full run is roughly 500× the paper check. The Praxis lake adds more.

What that implies:
- **Measure throughput:** bytes per second and claims per second, per step, so a full run's cost is predictable before it starts. The time budget for a full run is Sloane's to set.
- **One pass per artifact:** check every quote against an artifact in a single scan, not one scan per quote.
- **Offsets before search:** corpus rows already carry character offsets and BLAKE3; verifying a recorded slice costs the slice, not the artifact.
- **Bounded memory:** stream artifacts; parallelize across them.
- **Skip by content:** an incremental run skips any (artifact digest, claim digest, binary digest) already verified. The periodic full run re-does everything and must reach the same root; that agreement is the check on the incremental path.
- **No second copy:** ingesting 11 GB into `.descartes/` doubles disk use; the store should reuse the pinned bytes already on disk where its integrity rules allow.

content.text:
I updated trail #27: Descartes efficiency work now aims at a periodic run over the whole corpus, not at checking one paper. The direction is also saved in the Entire brain.

**What that means for the design:**
- **Throughput comes first:** measure bytes per second and claims per second at each step, so the cost of a full run is known before it starts. How long a full run is allowed to take is your call; the trail leaves that open.
- **One pass per source:** check all the quotes in a source in a single read, not one read per quote. That fivefold gap between wall time and CPU time may be exactly this.
- **Offsets before search:** corpus rows already record character offsets and a BLAKE3 hash, so checking one costs the length of the quote, not the length of the source.
- **Skip what hasn't changed:** an incremental run skips any source, claim and Descartes build it has already verified together. The periodic full run redoes everything and must reach the same root hash, which is how we know the shortcut is honest.
- **Bounded memory and no second copy:** stream sources and spread them across cores. Copying 11 GB into the Descartes store would double disk use, so the store should reuse the pinned bytes already on disk where its integrity rules allow.

The short source IDs from before fit this too. Hashing each block once per source gives cheap, stable locations across the whole corpus.

content.content:
Exit code 1
# Circles of assumption

A derivation such as PDF → text is never simply "faithful" or "unfaithful".
Each part of the content gets a colour: the highest circle at which that part
is verified, together with the measured gap.

| Circle | What is assumed or checked | Instrument |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | The source bytes, identified by digest. This is the only thing assumed. | none |
| 1 | Conservation laws measured with one instrument: every word kept, every inked pixel accounted for | poppler (`pdftotext -bbox`, `pdftoppm`) |
| 2 | The same measurement confirmed by an independent instrument | tesseract OCR of the raster, which never sees poppler's text layer |
| 3 | An untrusted proposal (LLM) that passes circles 1–2 | an LLM witness, checked by `descartes` |
| 4 | Human discernment: what no mechanical check can settle | a person |

Rasters, text layers and OCR output are not ground truth. They are
derivations from circle 0, re-run on every check and kept only as digests in
`artifacts/fidelity/<name>.instruments.tsv`. If a re-run gives a different
digest, the instruments are not reproducible and the check fails. Because
everything can be regenerated from the source, only the source is assumed.

## First measurement: the Gemini transcript (2026-11-02)

`sh stage1/fidelity.sh` produced
`artifacts/fidelity/Secure-Alternatives-to-Iroh-P2P.tsv`:

| Component | Circle | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| source bytes | 0 | reproducible from the digest |
| text (words) | 1 | 10,898 / 10,910 (99.89%) of text-layer words are present in `pdftotext` output |
| text (words) | 2 | 10,619 / 10,910 (97.33%) confirmed by OCR at the same position |
| text position | 0 | not captured: the plain-text derivation has no coordinates |
| non-text ink | 0 | 2.41% of inked pixels lie outside every word box, in 17 regions: table grids and section rules |
| tables | 0 | not captured: row/column pairings are unverified |
| reading order | 4 | open |

The largest unaccounted region on page 3 (42.5,143 → 570,307.5 pt) is
exactly the "Comparison Across Your Requirements" table grid. The ink check
found the table without being told to look for one. Any claim that depends
on which cell sits in which row therefore rests on circle 0 until a table
proposal passes a geometric check.

The 2.67% of words OCR does not confirm are mostly code (monospace
punctuation, `::`, `->`) and the box-drawing characters in diagrams. These
are differences between instruments, and they stay visible in the per-page
rows rather than being averaged away.

## Parameters (recorded in every report)

| Parameter | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Scale | 2 px/pt (144 dpi) | Enough resolution for OCR. Coordinates are exact multiples of points. |
| Ink threshold | < 250 of 255 | Chrome draws table rules in light grey. A mid-grey threshold (128) missed every one of them, which the first run showed: 0 regions. |
| Mask margin | 1 pt | Glyph ink extends slightly past the font's box. |
| Minimum region | 40 px | Anti-aliasing specks are counted in the totals but not listed as regions. |

These are assumptions too, so they are printed at the top of every report.

## Next, in order

1. **Table proposals (circle 3).** An LLM proposes cells as page + box +
   text. The check: the glyphs inside each box spell the cell's text, the
   cells tile the table without overlap, the row and column bands are
   consistent, and the table's box covers the residual-ink region it
   explains. A table that passes moves its pairings from circle 0 to circle 3.
2. **Name the lost words.** Report the 12 words the plain-text derivation
   dropped.

A derivation such as PDF → text is never simply "faithful" or "unfaithful".
Each part of the content gets a colour: the highest circle at which that part

input.content:
Intent (Sloane, 2026-11-04): "understand how much LLM stuff we're using in there. If at all, whether and to what degree, and have the ability to do experiments on how that works. ... the goal here is to build a deterministic core that we can extend out from in concentric circles." Correctness first, always; then reliable output; then efficiency (trail #27).

The circles are already defined (descartes `docs/circles.md`): 0 the source bytes; 1–2 mechanical instruments; 3 an untrusted LLM proposal that passes 1–2; 4 human discernment.

## Inventory (2026-11-04, by hand, to be generated)
- **Core code:** no LLM call in `src/`, `stage1/` or `tools/`. LLM text enters only as (a) claim witnesses, (b) pinned sources that are LLM transcripts (`sources/llm-witness-*.md`, the Gemini export), and (c) `proposals/`, reported but never ingested.
- **Descartes claims:** 221 of 280 rows are LLM-witnessed (79%); 16 of those are `llm:unattributed`. The other 59 are witnessed by organisations or publications (`org:ai2` 54, DOI/arXiv 5).
- **anthropic-pbc paper:** 97 of 97 claim rows are `llm:claude-opus-5-5 proposed; confirm=human:sloane`. No human confirmation is recorded for any of them; the README says nothing records concurrence yet.
- **What the check covers:** the quote's existence is mechanical (circle 1). Whether the statement follows from the quote is the LLM's testimony (circle 3 at best) until a person concurs (circle 4). So 100% of the paper's statements currently rest on LLM testimony.
- **Format drift:** `src/model.rs` defines the witness as `llm:<model> prompt=sha256:<digest>`. The paper's rows carry no prompt digest, so the proposal cannot be reproduced or compared across experiments.

## Measurement (generated, never hand-counted; see trail #26)
For every claims file and every run, Descartes reports how many claims sit at each circle, by witness kind (model + prompt digest, organisation, person), and how many LLM-witnessed claims have a recorded human concurrence.

## Experiments
- Every LLM step is a recorded, replayable run: model id, prompt sha256, inputs by digest, parameters, outputs to `proposals/`. Same inputs, different model or prompt, gives comparable proposals.
- What to measure, per run: the share of proposed quotes that pass `descartes check` (circle 1); agreement between models or prompts on the same evidence; and fidelity against human verdicts.
- Gold labels come from people, never from an LLM (anthropic-pbc AGENTS.md; bert-enrichment-spec §9). Ready candidate set: the 93 atomic-review rows in `anthropic-pbc/claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.review.tsv`, LLM-reviewed and `applied`. They become gold only when Sloane, or another named coder, confirms each verdict.
- Experiment output never enters the core graph; only a claim that passes the mechanical circles and carries its recorded witness is ingested.

## Done when
Any run states, from Descartes output alone, what share of its claims rests on LLM testimony and at which circle, and an LLM experiment can be re-run from its record and compared with another.

Intent (Sloane, 2026-11-04): "understand how much LLM stuff we're using in there. If at all, whether and to what degree, and have the ability to do experiments on how that works. ... the goal here is to build a deterministic core that we can extend out from in concentric circles." Correctness first, always; then reliable output; then efficiency (trail #27).

The circles are already defined (descartes `docs/circles.md`): 0 the source bytes; 1–2 mechanical instruments; 3 an untrusted LLM proposal that passes 1–2; 4 human discernment.

## Inventory (2026-11-04, by hand, to be generated)
- **Core code:** no LLM call in `src/`, `stage1/` or `tools/`. LLM text enters only as (a) claim witnesses, (b) pinned sources that are LLM transcripts (`sources/llm-witness-*.md`, the Gemini export), and (c) `proposals/`, reported but never ingested.
- **Descartes claims:** 221 of 280 rows are LLM-witnessed (79%); 16 of those are `llm:unattributed`. The other 59 are witnessed by organisations or publications (`org:ai2` 54, DOI/arXiv 5).
- **anthropic-pbc paper:** 97 of 97 claim rows are `llm:claude-opus-5-5 proposed; confirm=human:sloane`. No human confirmation is recorded for any of them; the README says nothing records concurrence yet.
- **What the check covers:** the quote's existence is mechanical (circle 1). Whether the statement follows from the quote is the LLM's testimony (circle 3 at best) until a person concurs (circle 4). So 100% of the paper's statements currently rest on LLM testimony.
- **Format drift:** `src/model.rs` defines the witness as `llm:<model> prompt=sha256:<digest>`. The paper's rows carry no prompt digest, so the proposal cannot be reproduced or compared across experiments.

## Measurement (generated, never hand-counted; see trail #26)
For every claims file and every run, Descartes reports how many claims sit at each circle, by witness kind (model + prompt digest, organisation, person), and how many LLM-witnessed claims have a recorded human concurrence.

## Experiments
- Every LLM step is a recorded, replayable run: model id, prompt sha256, inputs by digest, parameters, outputs to `proposals/`. Same inputs, different model or prompt, gives comparable proposals.
- What to measure, per run: the share of proposed quotes that pass `descartes check` (circle 1); agreement between models or prompts on the same evidence; and fidelity against human verdicts.

Ready candidate set: the 93 atomic-review rows in `anthropic-pbc/claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.review.tsv`, LLM-reviewed and `applied`. They become gold only when Sloane, or another named coder, confirms each verdict.
- Experiment output never enters the core graph; only a claim that passes the mechanical circles and carries its recorded witness is ingested.

## Done when
Any run states, from Descartes output alone, what share of its claims rests on LLM testimony and at which circle, and an LLM experiment can be re-run from its record and compared with another.

content.content:
# Shared producer contract

Praxis owns the common emission and semantic-lake contracts for participating producers. Producer repositories retain their methods, source acquisition, authorship and independent version history. The [root README](../README.md) governs Praxis; each producer's README governs its own module. This is a shared behavior contract, not a second cross-repository roadmap.

## Before adding or changing an emitter

Reusable slide metadata is aggregated by the [central slide catalog](../catalog/SLIDES.md).
Keep one plain source manifest per library and treat old component bindings as
legacy provenance. The aggregate/native catalog must not acquire React or another
framework dependency merely to browse or combine records. Unconverted visual
layouts remain explicitly unconverted.

1. Use the [design primitive](../design/README.md) and [composable presentation contract](../design/research-presentation.md). The [research template](../design/research-template.md) is one starting composition. Keep relevant facts, claims, sources, version and limitations linked from the opening.
2. Reuse the [offline renderer](../render/README.md) and [composable HTML parts](../design/components.py) for new pages, line/bar figures, relationship views and audience-selected HTML/JSON-LD/N-Triples exports. Use the [central report writer](../report_writer/README.md) for the PDF/report path where appropriate. Add a thin producer adapter for a missing input shape; do not fork the styles or create a competing website generator.
3. Emit from pinned producer data and methods. Keep dataset, metric, unit, original locators, missingness, source version and transformation identity. One selected record set must drive the human-facing output and linked data. Do not harmonize conflicting judgments or merge authorization because byte hashes match.
4. Preserve authorship. An independently authored working paper does not become an Ethical Capital opinion because the firm hosts or aggregates it. Official firm treatment requires an explicit version and release authority; a rendering task alone is not that authority.
5. Keep export audience, publication identity, source checks, signature results and review separate. Public output must be an explicitly eligible dependency closure. Private material must never be present in hidden HTML, client bundles, source downloads, structured data or indexes of a public export.

Existing sealed publications and producer-specific emitters are not automatically migrated by a documentation pointer. Preserve their bytes, pins and signing protocols. When changing an actual emitter, prove its adapter and regenerate/check the affected output through the producer's normal revision process. The current website is not rebuilt merely by adopting this contract.

## Data belongs to one governed semantic lake

Before adding implementation code, ask whether the behavior is needed and whether
an existing component already provides it. Prefer a maintained dependency with a
small adapter over a new parser, cryptographic primitive or storage engine. Compare
total maintenance, transitive dependencies, resource use, licensing and failure
behavior; fewer lines of our code alone is not sufficient. Pin the selected tool and
test its input/output boundary. For PDF intake, inspect the existing extraction and
rendering paths before proposing another PDF parser. Record an actual missing
capability before writing custom code.

Software and capability records should join the governed catalog by stable identity,
version, owner, supported inputs/outputs, rights and reuse evidence. They point to
the authoritative repository/package; lake participation does not move source code
or deployment secrets into a data table. The referenced software repository remains
to be identified. DuckLake is a storage/query component behind this contract, not a
replacement for authorization or a reason to duplicate the software registry.

The [semantic-lake contract](semantic-lake.md) and [catalog contract](../catalog/README.md) are canonical. Praxis manages catalog identity, shared metadata and custody/placement requirements. Bulk source and derived datasets, source snapshots, claim/source records and research-question datasets participate in that one governed lake under their real owner, audience and rights scope.

Local files, caches, SQLite/vector indexes and per-repository directories can be staging, retained source pins or rebuildable projections. They must not quietly become a second authoritative private research system. A manifest saying a location exists is not evidence that bytes were stored there.

Before calling a transfer complete, obtain an actual placement/write receipt with:

- owner and audience/rights scope, dataset and immutable artifact identity;
- actual backend, bucket/container and object key or equivalent location;
- content digest, byte count and backend version where available;
- successful write plus digest/readback evidence;
- authorized reader/writer identity and allowed/denied-access evidence for private scope;
- catalog selection tied to that exact completed receipt, with retries and partial writes accounted for.

Do not guess a bucket/key from a dataset name, use a shared reference bucket as a private fallback, or promote a cached source into lake custody by renaming it. A public source can lead to private analysis. Equal bytes can have different custody and rights records. Keep source attribution and restrictions attached through derivation, search, export and delivery.

**Current boundary:** Praxis has a working local metadata catalog and offline renderer. A general lake object/manifest service, tenant authorization, transfer/recovery receipts and their runtime acceptance are not established by these tools. Existing backends must be verified for the particular dataset and scope before use. Until that succeeds, retain the current authorized bytes and pin their location as staging; report the missing placement/receipt rather than moving or publishing them. Adoption does not authorize a data migration, new bucket, credential grant or public upload.

## What producers and agents should do proactively

When work adds a dataset, emitter or off-machine copy, check this contract. Reuse central generation rather than starting another theme or generator. Register the producer's pinned metadata with the catalog; distinguish registration from storage, review and publication. Ask the coordinating owner to resolve a missing lake placement, access boundary or receipt, and preserve the existing source until resolved. Do not silently invent a private store or mark the task complete from a tool-success label.

Use the existing cross-repository coordination pointer for shared sequencing. Public producers need only the public Praxis contracts to build; do not copy private coordination plans, access details or research payloads into public repositories. No dependency on a private Dark checkout is introduced into public compilation.

<!-- praxis-producer-contract:start -->
# Praxis producer integration

Read the [shared producer contract](../../praxis/docs/producer-contract.md) before adding or changing output generation, dataset
registration or custody. The central contract owns the rules; this file is a
portable source pointer, not a second implementation or a runtime acceptance
receipt.

- [Design primitive](../../praxis/design/README.md)
- [Research presentation](../../praxis/design/research-presentation.md)
- [Offline renderer](../../praxis/render/README.md)
- [Semantic lake](../../praxis/docs/semantic-lake.md)
- [Catalog](../../praxis/catalog/README.md)

Reuse central emitters or thin producer adapters. Keep public/private exports,
publication identity, review and signatures separate. Dataset bytes belong to
the one governed lake under verified owner/audience/rights boundaries. Until
actual placement and access/readback receipts exist, preserve authorized local
staging and report the gap; do not claim the transfer completed.

The producer remains responsible for methods, source pins, attribution and
rebuildability. Existing emitters are not automatically rewired, hash pins are
not moved, and data is not uploaded by installing these references. Public
builds do not depend on private coordination plans or a private Dark checkout.
<!-- praxis-producer-contract:end -->

## Task
Write `claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.tsv`:
1. Find every quotation the paper attributes to an outside source: text in quotation marks (straight or curly) or *italic quotes* or blockquotes presented as a source's words. Skip the paper's own epigraphs/slogans and its quotations of itself.
2. One row per quotation. `label` Q001, Q002… in paper order. `witness` = `llm:claude-opus-5-5 proposed; confirm=human:sloane`. `statement` = one short plain sentence of what the quote shows, in the paper's terms, including the paper section (e.g. "§4.1: the charter purpose names the long-term benefit of humanity"). `quote` = the quoted words exactly as printed in the paper, without the surrounding quotation marks, ellipses kept as printed.

Do NOT invent derived-text paths; materialisation is a later step.

5. A quotation whose attribution is ambiguous: comment row `# AMBIGUOUS …` with the candidate sources.
6. Header comments: what the file is, that it is a draft for Sloane to confirm, that paths point at pinned sources not yet materialised, and that no check has been run.

- Touch only `claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.tsv`. Commit it once, message ending `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Never sign.

content.text:
The test is written, and the rule it checks is built and passing. It's on its own branch in Descartes, not merged, because merging would fail 72 of Descartes's own claims.

**The rule:** a claim whose witness is an LLM must name `prompt=sha256:<digest>` of a file in the repository's `prompts/` folder, or say `prompt=unrecorded`. A digest that matches no file fails, as does a malformed one or a missing one. Witnesses that aren't LLMs are unaffected.

**What I did:**
- **Tests first.** I wrote four tests before the rule existed. The two that need the rule failed, and the two that check it doesn't over-reach passed. Then I added the rule to Descartes's claims check.
- **One old test adjusted.** It used a bare `llm` witness, so the new rule now stops that row before the quote it tests is ever looked up. I gave it `prompt=unrecorded`; what it asserts is unchanged.
- **Results.** The full suite passes: 148 tests. Committed as `1a44f60` on branch `witness-prompt-digest` in a separate worktree, so the other session's staged work in Descartes is untouched.

**What it finds:**
- **This paper:** unchanged at 75 passing, with no witness errors.
- **Descartes's own claims:** 72 rows fail. They come from interactive sessions (`session=bootstrap`, `session=strictness`) and from chat transcripts you pasted (`llm:unattributed`). Each row honestly says it has no prompt file, just not in the form the rule accepts. Changing them to `prompt=unrecorded` changes their claim IDs and the loop's expected results, so that's a call for you or the Descartes session.
- **A loophole:** seven rows in the AI2 file use the witness kind `model:` instead of `llm:`, so the rule never checks them. Either `model:` is treated as another name for `llm:`, or those rows are renamed. I didn't pick, because it changes what the witness format means.

I didn't merge the branch, for the same reason. The results and both decisions are on Entire trail #28.

Locking it down means making every route by which a wrong record could pass the checks visible, then closing them one at a time. I'll take the known gaps myself:
1. **Unknown witness kinds:** make them fail rather than slip through, which closes the `model:` loophole without deciding what `model:` means.
2. **The Descartes binary:** rebuild it from a recorded commit, so every check names exactly what ran it.
3. **Sources and derived text:** re-verify every pinned source against its manifest hash, and re-run every recipe to confirm the derived text is byte-identical.

In parallel, a read-only adversarial agent will look for routes I haven't thought of.

content.content:
# A014: the sandbox denies networking, Unix sockets, the resolver, reads of
#       $HOME and writes outside the scratch dir (probed after the build,
#       with the same profile, so the proof covers the build that just ran).
# A015: a second build into a different directory is byte-identical.
# -D warnings is set here, against the pinned toolchain, not in Cargo.toml: a
# newer rustc adds lints, and old source must keep building for anyone else.
# Registry (vendored) crates are built with --cap-lints, so this binds our code.
SB_RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$ROOT=. -D warnings"
# Run the pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml) through `rustup run`, not
# whatever `cargo` is first on PATH (e.g. a build-cache shim): the
# reproducibility gate must test the bare toolchain. `rustup run` keeps the
# environment the toolchain's own tools need (rust-objcopy finds libLLVM via
# it). Everything runs under env -i (stage1/sandbox.sh), so RUSTC,
# RUSTC_WRAPPER, CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_TARGET_*_LINKER and the like
# cannot reach the build.
TOOLCHAIN=$(sed -n 's/^channel = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' rust-toolchain.toml)
[ -n "$TOOLCHAIN" ] || fail "no channel in rust-toolchain.toml"
[ "$SB_RUSTUP_BIN" != "$SB_NONE" ] || fail "rustup not found (the real binary, not a version-manager shim); the pinned toolchain needs it"
sb_phase build /usr/bin
SYSROOT=$(sb_env "$SB_RUSTUP_BIN" run "$TOOLCHAIN" rustc --print sysroot) || fail "toolchain $TOOLCHAIN not usable (not installed? the loop never installs)"
case "$SYSROOT" in /*) ;; *) fail "rustc reported a non-absolute sysroot" ;; esac
sb_phase build "$SYSROOT/bin"
RUSTC_VERSION=$(sb_env "$SB_RUSTUP_BIN" run "$TOOLCHAIN" rustc --version)
echo "stage1: toolchain  $(sb_env "$SB_RUSTUP_BIN" run "$TOOLCHAIN" cargo --version)  ($RUSTC_VERSION, env -i, no wrapper)"
cargo_sb() { sb_env "$SB_RUSTUP_BIN" run "$TOOLCHAIN" cargo "$@"; }

# Sandboxes: sandbox-exec on darwin (stage1/no-network.sb); bwrap on linux.
# Untested: no Linux run yet.
[ "$SB_KIND" != none ] || echo "stage1: SKIP network isolation (no sandbox tool for $OS); building unsandboxed"

# Both builds start from empty target directories: leftover build state (from
# another toolchain or a cache shim) is an input we have not verified, and on
# 2026-11-02 it broke stripping.
for t in a b; do
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  cargo_sb $BUILD --locked --offline --release --quiet --target-dir "$SB/build-$t" > "$TMP/build-$t.log" 2>&1 \
    || { tail -40 "$TMP/build-$t.log" >&2; fail "build $t failed (sandboxed)"; }
  # Out of sandbox-writable space as soon as the build returns.
  out="$SB/build-$t/release/descartes"
  [ -f "$out" ] && [ ! -L "$out" ] || fail "build $t produced no regular file at release/descartes"
  cp "$out" "$TMP/bin/descartes-$t"
done
cmp -s "$TMP/bin/descartes-a" "$TMP/bin/descartes-b" || fail "build not reproducible: two builds of the same source differ"
BIN="$TMP/bin/descartes"
mv "$TMP/bin/descartes-a" "$BIN"
rm -f "$TMP/bin/descartes-b"
chmod 555 "$BIN"
chmod 555 "$TMP/bin"
sha256_of() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
  else shasum -a 256 < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'; fi
}
BIN_SHA=$(sha256_of "$BIN")
# bin_check PHASE: the binary about to be used is the one that was built.
bin_check() {
  [ -f "$BIN" ] && [ ! -L "$BIN" ] || fail "verified binary missing before $1"
  [ "$(sha256_of "$BIN")" = "$BIN_SHA" ] || fail "verified binary changed before $1"
}
SB_BIN=$BIN
# No absolute home or temp path may survive the remap (assembled from pieces
# so this file passes its own boundary check).
U="/Use""rs/"; H="/ho""me/"; F="var/fol""ders"

#!/bin/sh
# article.sh ARTICLE_ROOT CLAIMS_FILE... : verify an article repository's inputs,
# then check its claims, with the same rules the loop applies to this repository.
#
#   1. sources/MANIFEST.tsv (id role fetched url path bytes blake3): every row's
#      file exists under sources/ with that size and BLAKE3, and every file in
#      sources/ (except the manifest) has a row.
#   2. derived/recipes.tsv (output input tool args): only the loop's tools, each
#      with its one argument shape; inputs are manifest sources; each recipe is
#      re-run and must reproduce its output byte for byte; every derived/*.txt
#      has a recipe.
#   3. descartes check on each claims file.
#
# Every problem is reported, not just the first; the exit status is 1 if any
# step failed. No clock or host enters the report. Unlike the loop, this runs
# no sandbox, and says so. The binary is $DESCARTES or ./descartes beside this
# repository's build; tools/html_to_text.py is this repository's recipe.
set -u
[ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "usage: article.sh ARTICLE_ROOT CLAIMS_FILE..." >&2; exit 64; }
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
ROOT=$1; shift
BIN=${DESCARTES:-}
[ -n "$BIN" ] && [ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "article: set DESCARTES to a descartes binary" >&2; exit 64; }
HTML="$HERE/tools/html_to_text.py"
tab=$(printf '\t')
bad=0
TMP=$(mktemp -d) || exit 70
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT INT TERM
note() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf 'FAIL\t%s\n' "$*"; bad=1; }
sha256_of() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
  else shasum -a 256 < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'; fi
}
safe_rel() { case "$1" in ''|/*|-*|../*|*/../*|*/..|*/./*|./*) return 1 ;; esac; return 0; }

cd "$ROOT" || exit 66
note "article: descartes sha256:$(sha256_of "$BIN")"
note "article: UNSANDBOXED (the loop sandboxes its derivations; this script does not)"

# --- 1. manifest -----------------------------------------------------------
M=sources/MANIFEST.tsv
[ -f "$M" ] || { fail "$M missing"; exit 1; }
: > "$TMP/listed"
rows=0
while IFS="$tab" read -r id role fetched url path bytes b3 rest || [ -n "${id:-}" ]; do
  case "$id" in ''|'#'*|id) continue ;; esac
  rows=$((rows + 1))
  [ -z "${rest:-}" ] || fail "$M: $id: more than 7 columns"
  safe_rel "$path" || { fail "$M: $id: path must be relative and plain: $path"; continue; }
  f="sources/$path"
  printf '%s\n' "$f" >> "$TMP/listed"
  if [ ! -f "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ]; then fail "$M: $id: $f missing or not a regular file"; continue; fi
  got_bytes=$(wc -c < "$f" | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$got_bytes" = "$bytes" ] || fail "$M: $id: $f has $got_bytes bytes, manifest says $bytes"
  got_b3=$("$BIN" hash "$f" | cut -f2)
  [ "$got_b3" = "$b3" ] || fail "$M: $id: $f BLAKE3 $got_b3, manifest says $b3"
done < "$M"
note "article: manifest  $rows rows"
find sources -type f ! -name MANIFEST.tsv | LC_ALL=C sort > "$TMP/present"
LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/listed" > "$TMP/listed.sorted"
comm -23 "$TMP/present" "$TMP/listed.sorted" | while read -r f; do printf 'FAIL\t%s is not in %s\n' "$f" "$M"; done > "$TMP/unlisted"
[ -s "$TMP/unlisted" ] && { cat "$TMP/unlisted"; bad=1; }

# --- 2. recipes ------------------------------------------------------------
R=derived/recipes.tsv
: > "$TMP/recipied"
if [ -f "$R" ]; then
  while IFS="$tab" read -r output input tool args || [ -n "${output:-}" ]; do
    case "$output" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
    printf '%s\n' "$output" >> "$TMP/recipied"
    case "$tool" in
      pdftotext) [ "$args" = "-enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk" ] || { fail "$R: $output: pdftotext takes exactly '-enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk', not '$args'"; continue; } ;;
      html-to-text) [ "$args" = "static-v1" ] || { fail "$R: $output: html-to-text takes exactly static-v1"; continue; } ;;
      *) fail "$R: $output: tool '$tool' is not allowed (allowed: pdftotext, html-to-text)"; continue ;;
    esac
    safe_rel "$input" && safe_rel "$output" || { fail "$R: $output: paths must be relative and plain"; continue; }
    grep -qxF -e "$input" "$TMP/listed" || { fail "$R: $output: input $input is not a manifest source"; continue; }
    case "$output" in derived/*) ;; *) fail "$R: $output: output must be under derived/"; continue ;; esac
    rm -f "$TMP/out"
    case "$tool" in
      pdftotext)
        command -v pdftotext >/dev/null 2>&1 || { fail "$R: $output: pdftotext absent"; continue; }
        version=$(pdftotext -v 2>&1 | sed -n '1p')
        pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk "$input" "$TMP/out" || { fail "$R: $output: pdftotext failed"; continue; }
        ;;
      html-to-text)
        [ -x /usr/bin/python3 ] || { fail "$R: $output: /usr/bin/python3 absent"; continue; }
        version="$(/usr/bin/python3 -I -B "$HTML" --version); $(/usr/bin/python3 -I -B --version 2>&1); script-sha256:$(sha256_of "$HTML")"
        /usr/bin/python3 -I -B "$HTML" --recipe static-v1 "$input" "$TMP/out" > /dev/null || { fail "$R: $output: html-to-text failed"; continue; }
        ;;
    esac
    if [ ! -f "$output" ]; then fail "$R: $output: missing (run the recipe)"; continue; fi
    cmp -s "$TMP/out" "$output" || { fail "$R: $output: not reproducible from $input with $version"; continue; }
    note "ok	re-derived $output from $input with $version: byte-identical"
  done < "$R"
fi
if [ -d derived ]; then
  find derived -type f -name '*.txt' | LC_ALL=C sort > "$TMP/dtxt"
  LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/recipied" > "$TMP/recipied.sorted"
  comm -23 "$TMP/dtxt" "$TMP/recipied.sorted" | while read -r f; do printf 'FAIL\t%s has no recipe in %s\n' "$f" "$R"; done > "$TMP/norecipe"
  [ -s "$TMP/norecipe" ] && { cat "$TMP/norecipe"; bad=1; }
fi

# --- 3. claims -------------------------------------------------------------
for c in "$@"; do
  "$BIN" check "$c" > "$TMP/check" 2>&1
  status=$?
  grep -v '^ok' "$TMP/check"
  [ $status -eq 0 ] || bad=1
done

[ $bad -eq 0 ] && note "article: PASS" || note "article: FAIL"
exit $bad

#!/bin/sh
# Negative suite for stage1/article.sh: a clean article passes, and each kind
# of tampering is refused with its own message. Usage: DESCARTES=bin test-article.sh
set -u
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd -P)
: "${DESCARTES:?set DESCARTES to a descartes binary}"
TMP=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/descartes-article-test.XXXXXX") || exit 70
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT HUP INT TERM
tab=$(printf '\t')
failures=0

# A minimal article: one HTML source, its recipe, one claim.
fixture() {
  rm -rf "$TMP/a"; mkdir -p "$TMP/a/sources" "$TMP/a/derived" "$TMP/a/claims"
  cp "$ROOT/tests/html/static.html" "$TMP/a/sources/page.html"
  b=$(wc -c < "$TMP/a/sources/page.html" | tr -d ' ')
  h=$("$DESCARTES" hash "$TMP/a/sources/page.html" | cut -f2)
  printf 'id\trole\tfetched\turl\tpath\tbytes\tblake3\npage\tcase\t2026-11-04\thttps://example.org/page\tpage.html\t%s\t%s\n' "$b" "$h" > "$TMP/a/sources/MANIFEST.tsv"
  printf 'derived/page.txt\tsources/page.html\thtml-to-text\tstatic-v1\n' > "$TMP/a/derived/recipes.tsv"
  cp "$ROOT/tests/html/static.txt" "$TMP/a/derived/page.txt"
  printf 'C1\t-\tllm:test prompt=unrecorded\tthe page says capital is substantial\tderived/page.txt\tsubstantial and increasing capital\n' > "$TMP/a/claims/c.tsv"
}
run() { DESCARTES="$DESCARTES" sh "$ROOT/stage1/article.sh" "$TMP/a" claims/c.tsv > "$TMP/out" 2>&1; }
expect_pass() {
  if run; then echo "ok    $1"; else echo "FAIL  $1: clean article refused"; cat "$TMP/out"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
}
expect_fail() { # name, message the report must contain
  if run; then echo "FAIL  $1: accepted"; failures=$((failures + 1))
  elif grep -qF -e "$2" "$TMP/out"; then echo "ok    $1"
  else echo "FAIL  $1: refused without '$2'"; cat "$TMP/out"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
}

fixture; expect_pass "clean article"
fixture; printf ' ' >> "$TMP/a/sources/page.html"; expect_fail "source bytes changed" "bytes, manifest says"
fixture; sed 's/business/bu5iness/' "$TMP/a/sources/page.html" > "$TMP/p" \&\& mv "$TMP/p" "$TMP/a/sources/page.html"; expect_fail "source changed, same size" "BLAKE3"
fixture; printf 'x' > "$TMP/a/sources/stray.pdf"; expect_fail "unlisted source" "sources/stray.pdf is not in"
fixture; rm "$TMP/a/sources/page.html"; expect_fail "listed source missing" "missing or not a regular file"
fixture; printf 'edited\n' >> "$TMP/a/derived/page.txt"; expect_fail "derived text edited" "not reproducible"
fixture; printf 'x\n' > "$TMP/a/derived/orphan.txt"; expect_fail "derived text without recipe" "has no recipe"
fixture; printf 'derived/x.txt\tsources/page.html\tcat\t-\n' >> "$TMP/a/derived/recipes.tsv"; expect_fail "disallowed tool" "is not allowed"
fixture; printf 'derived/x.txt\tsources/page.html\thtml-to-text\tstatic-v2\n' >> "$TMP/a/derived/recipes.tsv"; expect_fail "wrong recipe arguments" "takes exactly static-v1"
fixture; printf 'derived/x.txt\tsources/elsewhere.html\thtml-to-text\tstatic-v1\n' >> "$TMP/a/derived/recipes.tsv"; expect_fail "recipe input not in manifest" "is not a manifest source"
fixture; printf 'derived/x.txt\t../outside.html\thtml-to-text\tstatic-v1\n' >> "$TMP/a/derived/recipes.tsv"; expect_fail "recipe path escapes" "relative and plain"
fixture; sed "s/${tab}page.html${tab}/${tab}..\/page.html${tab}/" "$TMP/a/sources/MANIFEST.tsv" > "$TMP/m" && mv "$TMP/m" "$TMP/a/sources/MANIFEST.tsv"; expect_fail "manifest path escapes" "relative and plain"
fixture; sed 's/prompt=unrecorded//' "$TMP/a/claims/c.tsv" > "$TMP/c" && mv "$TMP/c" "$TMP/a/claims/c.tsv"; expect_fail "llm witness without prompt" "prompt=sha256"
fixture; sed 's/substantial and increasing capital$/substantial and decreasing capital/' "$TMP/a/claims/c.tsv" > "$TMP/c" && mv "$TMP/c" "$TMP/a/claims/c.tsv"; expect_fail "quote not in source" "quote not found"

[ $failures -eq 0 ] && echo "article test: all cases behaved" || echo "article test: $failures case(s) wrong"
exit $failures

- Row A3: I appended "Anthropic guarantees it will never pause development." to derived/pbc-report-2026.txt and quoted it. Result: `ok A3`.
- Row A4: I appended an HTML comment to sources/dgcl-c001-sc15.html and quoted it. Result: `ok A4`.
- `descartes derive` never runs the tool (main.rs:135-149). Recording `derive pdftotext sources/constitution.pdf derived/fake.txt`, with fake.txt holding "invented text", succeeded.
- `Derivation` has no tool-version field (model.rs:91-97), and verify only checks its shape (verify.rs:342-354).
- Three real rows quote raw `sources/*.html` and skip derivation entirely (Q007, Q048, Q084).
- Fix: check loads the manifest and recipes. Each evidence path must be a recipe output whose input's BLAKE3 matches the manifest and whose bytes equal a recorded derivation (input hash, output hash, tool and version). Raw sources are refused as evidence paths.

**3. A quote can pass without saying what the source says.** CONFIRMED.
- There is no minimum length, no word-boundary rule and no context rule. The match is a raw byte window that must occur once (store.rs:133-149).
- A1: "follow through on their commitments" (the source reads "do not follow through…") passes under the statement "companies follow through on their commitments".
- A2: "nnu" (3 bytes, from inside "annually") passes.
- A11: "an this moment calls for.\n\n10\n\nOur assessment\n\nPillar 3" passes, crossing a page number and two headings.
- A4: a match inside an HTML comment passes.
- Real case: Q022b quotes "However, we will not". The source continues "necessarily d[elay]", and the statement's point rests on that "necessarily". Q022b has no review row.
- Fix: require word boundaries at both ends and a minimum token count. Refuse spans across `\n\n` or form feeds. Store about 80 characters of context on each side in the evidence, so review sees it.

**4. The witness rule is easy to get past.** CONFIRMED, all under `ok`.
- The kind is compared exactly to `llm` (claims.rs:124). `LLM:claude` (A5), ` llm:claude` (A6), `llm-claude` (A7) and `human:Sloane` (A10) all pass with no prompt.
- Only the first `prompt=` counts (claims.rs:129). `prompt=unrecorded prompt=sha256:000…` passes (A8). `unrecorded` is a free pass in general; 3 real rows use it.
- The digest only has to match some regular file in prompts/ on disk (claims.rs:100-117). A9 names an untracked, unrelated prompts/zz-untracked.md and passes.
- Nothing ties a row to the step that produced it. The steps file says S03 (draft, eabeb…) produced the rows, yet 77 rows name S09's apply prompt (d9fd…).
- Fix:
  - Allow a closed set of witness kinds and refuse any other spelling.
  - Allow exactly one `prompt=` token.
  - Accept a prompt file only if it is tracked at HEAD.
  - Require a steps row with that digest whose outputs include the claims file.

**5. Nothing checks the review file or the steps file.** CONFIRMED.
- 24 claim labels have no review row: Q022a/b, Q026a/b, Q032a/b, Q039a/b, Q041a/b, Q069a-c, Q073a-d, Q075a/b, Q088a/b, Q094-Q096.
- 20 review labels have no claim: Q008, Q018, Q022, Q026, Q032, Q033, Q035, Q036, Q039, Q041, Q047, Q051, Q056, Q069, Q073, Q075, Q078, Q088, Q091, Q093.
- The `context` column claims to be verbatim but is never checked:
  - 16 rows' source column is not a file.
  - Of the 77 that are, only 1 context matches byte-exact. After collapsing whitespace, zero-width spaces and soft hyphens, 34 still do not match.
  - Some contexts carry editorial text: Q007 starts with an inserted "§ 362 (a): ", and Q014 contains "[...]".
- All 93 data rows are `applied` under one blanket instruction.
- The steps file is free text that no tool parses.
- Fix: a `descartes review` check. Labels must equal the claims file's set. The source must be a recipe output. Context must contain the row's quote and occur in that source under rule 3. Steps rows' hashes are re-hashed.

**6. A claim with one good row and one fabricated row still prints `ok`.** CONFIRMED.
- A12 shows it; claims.rs:255 fails a label only when every evidence row fails.
- The exit code is still 1, but the per-label `ok` lines are what gets recorded. No real label is in this state today.
- Fix: any failed row fails its label.

**7. A claim can have no evidence of its own.** PLAUSIBLE, minor.
- A row with `-`/`-` evidence and a non-empty `rests_on` passes on its parents alone (claims.rs:255). Its statement is never tied to any text.
- Fix: refuse it, or mark it as an inference so it is never presented as quoted.

Not reproducible:
- `..` paths, hidden paths, symlinks and hard links are all refused (claims.rs:52-96).
- Empty quotes are refused (store.rs:134).

Order to fix: 1 and 2 first (gate and pinned bytes), then 3 and 6 (what the quote means), then 4 and 5 (who produced it).

#!/bin/sh
# article.sh ARTICLE_ROOT CLAIMS_FILE... : verify an article repository's inputs,
# then check its claims, with the same rules the loop applies to this repository.
#
#   1. sources/MANIFEST.tsv (id role fetched url path bytes blake3): every row's
#      file exists under sources/ with that size and BLAKE3, and every file in
#      sources/ (except the manifest) has a row.
#   2. derived/recipes.tsv (output input tool args): only the loop's tools, each
#      with its one argument shape; inputs are manifest sources; each recipe is
#      re-run and must reproduce its output byte for byte; every derived/*.txt
#      has a recipe.
#   3. descartes check on each claims file.
#
# Every problem is reported, not just the first; the exit status is 1 if any
# step failed. No clock or host enters the report. Unlike the loop, this runs
# no sandbox, and says so. The binary is $DESCARTES or ./descartes beside this
# repository's build; tools/html_to_text.py is this repository's recipe.
set -u
[ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "usage: article.sh ARTICLE_ROOT CLAIMS_FILE..." >&2; exit 64; }
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
ROOT=$1; shift
BIN=${DESCARTES:-}
[ -n "$BIN" ] && [ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "article: set DESCARTES to a descartes binary" >&2; exit 64; }
HTML="$HERE/tools/html_to_text.py"
tab=$(printf '\t')
bad=0
TMP=$(mktemp -d) || exit 70
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT INT TERM
note() { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf 'FAIL\t%s\n' "$*"; bad=1; }
sha256_of() {
  if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'
  else shasum -a 256 < "$1" | awk '{print $1}'; fi
}
safe_rel() { case "$1" in ''|/*|-*|../*|*/../*|*/..|*/./*|./*) return 1 ;; esac; return 0; }

cd "$ROOT" || exit 66
note "article: descartes sha256:$(sha256_of "$BIN")"
note "article: UNSANDBOXED (the loop sandboxes its derivations; this script does not)"

# --- 1. manifest -----------------------------------------------------------
M=sources/MANIFEST.tsv
[ -f "$M" ] || { fail "$M missing"; exit 1; }
: > "$TMP/listed"
rows=0
while IFS="$tab" read -r id role fetched url path bytes b3 rest || [ -n "${id:-}" ]; do
  case "$id" in ''|'#'*|id) continue ;; esac
  rows=$((rows + 1))
  [ -z "${rest:-}" ] || fail "$M: $id: more than 7 columns"
  [ -n "$role" ] || fail "$M: $id: role is empty"
  case "$fetched" in [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-1][0-9]-[0-3][0-9]) ;; *) fail "$M: $id: fetched must be YYYY-MM-DD, not '$fetched'" ;; esac
  case "$url" in https://*|http://*) ;; *) fail "$M: $id: url must be http(s), not '$url'" ;; esac
  safe_rel "$path" || { fail "$M: $id: path must be relative and plain: $path"; continue; }
  f="sources/$path"
  printf '%s\n' "$f" >> "$TMP/listed"
  if [ ! -f "$f" ] || [ -L "$f" ]; then fail "$M: $id: $f missing or not a regular file"; continue; fi
  got_bytes=$(wc -c < "$f" | tr -d ' ')
  [ "$got_bytes" = "$bytes" ] || fail "$M: $id: $f has $got_bytes bytes, manifest says $bytes"
  got_b3=$("$BIN" hash "$f" | cut -f2)
  [ "$got_b3" = "$b3" ] || fail "$M: $id: $f BLAKE3 $got_b3, manifest says $b3"
done < "$M"
note "article: manifest  $rows rows"
find sources -type f ! -name MANIFEST.tsv | LC_ALL=C sort > "$TMP/present"
LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/listed" > "$TMP/listed.sorted"
comm -23 "$TMP/present" "$TMP/listed.sorted" | while read -r f; do printf 'FAIL\t%s is not in %s\n' "$f" "$M"; done > "$TMP/unlisted"
[ -s "$TMP/unlisted" ] && { cat "$TMP/unlisted"; bad=1; }

# --- 2. recipes ------------------------------------------------------------
R=derived/recipes.tsv
: > "$TMP/recipied"
if [ -f "$R" ]; then
  while IFS="$tab" read -r output input tool args || [ -n "${output:-}" ]; do
    case "$output" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
    printf '%s\n' "$output" >> "$TMP/recipied"
    case "$tool" in
      pdftotext) [ "$args" = "-enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk" ] || { fail "$R: $output: pdftotext takes exactly '-enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk', not '$args'"; continue; } ;;
      html-to-text) [ "$args" = "static-v1" ] || { fail "$R: $output: html-to-text takes exactly static-v1"; continue; } ;;
      *) fail "$R: $output: tool '$tool' is not allowed (allowed: pdftotext, html-to-text)"; continue ;;
    esac
    if ! safe_rel "$input" || ! safe_rel "$output"; then fail "$R: $output: paths must be relative and plain"; continue; fi
    grep -qxF -e "$input" "$TMP/listed" || { fail "$R: $output: input $input is not a manifest source"; continue; }
    case "$output" in derived/*) ;; *) fail "$R: $output: output must be under derived/"; continue ;; esac
    rm -f "$TMP/out"
    case "$tool" in
      pdftotext)
        command -v pdftotext >/dev/null 2>&1 || { fail "$R: $output: pdftotext absent"; continue; }
        version=$(pdftotext -v 2>&1 | sed -n '1p')
        pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk "$input" "$TMP/out" || { fail "$R: $output: pdftotext failed"; continue; }
        ;;
      html-to-text)
        [ -x /usr/bin/python3 ] || { fail "$R: $output: /usr/bin/python3 absent"; continue; }
        version="$(/usr/bin/python3 -I -B "$HTML" --version); $(/usr/bin/python3 -I -B --version 2>&1); script-sha256:$(sha256_of "$HTML")"
        /usr/bin/python3 -I -B "$HTML" --recipe static-v1 "$input" "$TMP/out" > /dev/null || { fail "$R: $output: html-to-text failed"; continue; }
        ;;
    esac
    if [ ! -f "$output" ]; then fail "$R: $output: missing (run the recipe)"; continue; fi
    cmp -s "$TMP/out" "$output" || { fail "$R: $output: not reproducible from $input with $version"; continue; }
    note "ok	re-derived $output from $input with $version: byte-identical"
  done < "$R"
fi
if [ -d derived ]; then
  find derived -type f -name '*.txt' | LC_ALL=C sort > "$TMP/dtxt"
  LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/recipied" > "$TMP/recipied.sorted"
  comm -23 "$TMP/dtxt" "$TMP/recipied.sorted" | while read -r f; do printf 'FAIL\t%s has no recipe in %s\n' "$f" "$R"; done > "$TMP/norecipe"
  [ -s "$TMP/norecipe" ] && { cat "$TMP/norecipe"; bad=1; }
fi

# --- 3. claims -------------------------------------------------------------
for c in "$@"; do
  "$BIN" check "$c" > "$TMP/check" 2>&1
  status=$?
  grep -v '^ok' "$TMP/check"
  [ $status -eq 0 ] || bad=1
done

if [ $bad -eq 0 ]; then note "article: PASS"; else note "article: FAIL"; fi
exit $bad

+    LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/digests" | comm -23 - "$TMP/committed" | while read -r d; do
+      printf 'FAIL\tprompt=sha256:%s: no prompt file with this digest is committed at HEAD under prompts/\n' "$d"

input.new_string:
# --- 2b. what claims may cite ----------------------------------------------
# Evidence is a recipe output, never a raw source: raw HTML keeps comments,
# scripts and markup in which a quote can match unseen. A prompt digest names
# a file committed at HEAD under prompts/, not whatever is on disk.
LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/recipied" > "$TMP/recipied.sorted"
: > "$TMP/digests"
for c in "$@"; do
  [ -f "$c" ] || { fail "$c: claims file missing"; continue; }
  awk -F'\t' 'NF >= 6 && $0 !~ /^#/ { print FNR "\t" $5 }' "$c" | while IFS="$tab" read -r n p; do
    [ "$p" = "-" ] && continue
    grep -qxF -e "$p" "$TMP/recipied.sorted" || printf 'FAIL\t%s:%s: evidence %s is not a recipe output in %s\n' "$c" "$n" "$p" "$R"
  done > "$TMP/cite"
  [ -s "$TMP/cite" ] && { cat "$TMP/cite"; bad=1; }
  awk -F'\t' 'NF >= 6 && $0 !~ /^#/ { print $3 }' "$c" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed -n 's/^prompt=sha256:\([0-9a-f]\{64\}\)$/\1/p' >> "$TMP/digests"
done
if [ -s "$TMP/digests" ]; then
  if git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- prompts/ | while read -r f; do
      git show "HEAD:$f" | { if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum; else shasum -a 256; fi; } | awk '{print $1}'
    done | LC_ALL=C sort -u > "$TMP/committed"
    LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/digests" | comm -23 - "$TMP/committed" | while read -r d; do
      printf 'FAIL\tprompt=sha256:%s: no prompt file with this digest is committed at HEAD under prompts/\n' "$d"
    done > "$TMP/untracked"
    [ -s "$TMP/untracked" ] && { cat "$TMP/untracked"; bad=1; }
    note "article: prompts  $(LC_ALL=C sort -u "$TMP/digests" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') digests named, checked against HEAD $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
  else
    fail "claims name prompt digests, but $ROOT is not a git repository with a HEAD, so committed prompts cannot be checked"
  fi
fi

# --- 3. claims -------------------------------------------------------------
