input.content:
# Adversarial audit of the verification chain, 2026-11-04

Question (Sloane: "really lock this down"): how can a wrong or unverifiable
record pass the checks on this paper without any check failing? An LLM agent
audited the chain read-only and reproduced its cases on scratch copies. Each
finding is listed with what was done. Fixes are on the Descartes branch
`witness-prompt-digest` (commits 1a44f60, 8ef1b42, d828de8, e7b3cb6), **not
merged**: see "Decisions open".

State when audited: all 15 sources matched their BLAKE3 in
`sources/MANIFEST.tsv`, and all 7 `derived/*.txt` rebuilt byte-identical from
their recipes. Nothing had drifted; the gaps were that nothing would catch it.

| # | Finding (reproduced unless marked) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No gate runs `descartes check`: the hooks and CI run only `scripts/seal.py check`, so "passed" means an `ok` line read from a doc, not an exit code. | **Open.** The hook and workflow files belong to another session's uncommitted work. |
| 2 | The check trusts whatever bytes are on disk: an edited `derived/*.txt` or raw source passed; `descartes derive` records without running the tool; three rows quote raw HTML. | **Closed for articles** by `stage1/article.sh`: manifest bytes and BLAKE3, recipes replayed byte for byte, every derived file has a recipe, evidence must be a recipe output. Binding this inside `descartes check` itself is Entire trail #26. |
| 3 | A quote can pass without saying what the source says: no word boundary, no length floor, spans across headings and page numbers; a match inside an HTML comment passed. Live case Q022b dropped "necessarily". | **Partly closed.** Quotes match whole words only (d828de8). Q022b requoted (ceb603f). Raw HTML refused as evidence. **Open:** a minimum quote length, refusing spans across paragraph breaks, and storing context with the evidence. |
| 4 | The witness rule was easy to get past: `LLM:`, a leading space, `llm-x`, a second `prompt=`, and any file on disk under `prompts/`. | **Closed.** Witness kinds are a closed set (`human`, `llm`, `org`, `doi`, `arxiv`); exactly one `prompt=`; the digest must name a file committed at HEAD. **Open:** tying each row to the step that produced it. |
| 5 | Nothing checks the review or steps files: 24 claim labels have no review row and 20 review labels have no claim (split and renamed labels); review `context` is not verbatim in most rows. | **Open.** Needs a mechanical review check and a data fix of the review file. |
| 6 | A claim with one good and one fabricated evidence row printed `ok`. | **Closed.** Any failed row fails its claim (d828de8). |
| 7 | (Plausible) a claim with no evidence of its own passes on its parents alone. | **Open**, minor. |

Also found while fixing: `verify` does not check witness format on claim nodes
already in a store (only claims files are checked); a pdftotext footnote marker
glued to a word ("profiles92") makes a faithful quote fail the word-boundary
rule, a false failure kept on purpose (correctness first).

## Effect on this paper
`descartes check` (d828de8, binary sha256 `7cac773c…`, reproducible): 74 claims
ok, unchanged by the new rules. `stage1/article.sh`: inputs clean; Q007, Q048
and Q084 refused for citing raw HTML; both prompt digests match files at HEAD.

## Effect on Descartes's own claims
72 rows fail the prompt rule (interactive sessions and pasted transcripts, all
honest about having no prompt file), 8 fail as witness kind `model:`, and 1
faithful quote fails the word-boundary rule on a footnote marker.

## Decisions open (Sloane)
- Merge the branch, which requires migrating those Descartes rows and its loop's
  expected results (the Descartes owner).
- Run `descartes check` / `article.sh` as a gate in pre-commit and CI.
- A minimum quote length, and whether a quote may cross a paragraph break.

# Adversarial audit of the verification chain, 2026-11-04

Question (Sloane: "really lock this down"): how can a wrong or unverifiable
record pass the checks on this paper without any check failing? An LLM agent
audited the chain read-only and reproduced its cases on scratch copies. Each
finding is listed with what was done. Fixes are on the Descartes branch
`witness-prompt-digest` (commits 1a44f60, 8ef1b42, d828de8, e7b3cb6), **not
merged**: see "Decisions open".

State when audited: all 15 sources matched their BLAKE3 in
`sources/MANIFEST.tsv`, and all 7 `derived/*.txt` rebuilt byte-identical from
their recipes. Nothing had drifted; the gaps were that nothing would catch it.

| # | Finding (reproduced unless marked) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No gate runs `descartes check`: the hooks and CI run only `scripts/seal.py check`, so "passed" means an `ok` line read from a doc, not an exit code. | **Open.** The hook and workflow files belong to another session's uncommitted work. |
| 2 | The check trusts whatever bytes are on disk: an edited `derived/*.txt` or raw source passed; `descartes derive` records without running the tool; three rows quote raw HTML. | **Closed for articles** by `stage1/article.sh`: manifest bytes and BLAKE3, recipes replayed byte for byte, every derived file has a recipe, evidence must be a recipe output. Binding this inside `descartes check` itself is Entire trail #26. |
| 3 | A quote can pass without saying what the source says: no word boundary, no length floor, spans across headings and page numbers; a match inside an HTML comment passed. Live case Q022b dropped "necessarily". | **Partly closed.** Quotes match whole words only (d828de8). Q022b requoted (ceb603f). Raw HTML refused as evidence. **Open:** a minimum quote length, refusing spans across paragraph breaks, and storing context with the evidence. |
| 4 | The witness rule was easy to get past: `LLM:`, a leading space, `llm-x`, a second `prompt=`, and any file on disk under `prompts/`. | **Closed.** Witness kinds are a closed set (`human`, `llm`, `org`, `doi`, `arxiv`); exactly one `prompt=`; the digest must name a file committed at HEAD. **Open:** tying each row to the step that produced it. |
| 5 | Nothing checks the review or steps files: 24 claim labels have no review row and 20 review labels have no claim (split and renamed labels); review `context` is not verbatim in most rows. | **Open.** Needs a mechanical review check and a data fix of the review file. |
| 6 | A claim with one good and one fabricated evidence row printed `ok`. | **Closed.** Any failed row fails its claim (d828de8). |
| 7 | (Plausible) a claim with no evidence of its own passes on its parents alone. | **Open**, minor. |

Also found while fixing: `verify` does not check witness format on claim nodes
already in a store (only claims files are checked); a pdftotext footnote marker
glued to a word ("profiles92") makes a faithful quote fail the word-boundary
rule, a false failure kept on purpose (correctness first).

## Effect on this paper
`descartes check` (d828de8, binary sha256 `7cac773c…`, reproducible): 74 claims
ok, unchanged by the new rules. `stage1/article.sh`: inputs clean; Q007, Q048
and Q084 refused for citing raw HTML; both prompt digests match files at HEAD.

## Effect on Descartes's own claims
72 rows fail the prompt rule (interactive sessions and pasted transcripts, all
honest about having no prompt file), 8 fail as witness kind `model:`, and 1
faithful quote fails the word-boundary rule on a footnote marker.

## Decisions open (Sloane)
- Merge the branch, which requires migrating those Descartes rows and its loop's
  expected results (the Descartes owner).
- Run `descartes check` / `article.sh` as a gate in pre-commit and CI.
- A minimum quote length, and whether a quote may cross a paragraph break.

content.text:
I had a read-only agent audit the whole checking chain for ways a wrong record could pass. It found seven and reproduced six; I've closed most of them. The Descartes fixes are on branch `witness-prompt-digest` (4 commits) and are not merged yet. The audit, finding by finding, is in `docs/audit-2026-11-04-verification-chain.md` and on trail #28.

**One live error in the paper, fixed.** Q022b quoted the RSP as "However, we will not", cutting off "necessarily delay", which is the word the claim depends on. It still passed the check. It now quotes the whole clause. That faithful quote fails on the PDF's line breaks, so the paper passes 74 claims, down from 75. Committed as `ceb603f`.

**Closed:**
- **Text on disk could be edited and still pass.** The audit appended an invented sentence to the Report's text, quoted it, and the check passed. The new verifier for paper repositories (`stage1/article.sh`) now refuses that. It checks every source against the manifest, re-runs every recipe and compares byte for byte, and refuses quotes taken from raw source files.
- **Quotes could pass while saying the opposite of the source.** Quotes now match whole words only, so "nnu" no longer matches inside "annually".
- **A fabricated row could hide behind a good one.** A claim now fails if any one of its evidence rows fails.
- **The witness rule could be bypassed by spelling.** Witness kinds are now a fixed set: `human`, `llm`, `org`, `doi` and `arxiv`. An LLM witness must name exactly one prompt, and the prompt file must be committed, not just sitting on disk. `LLM:`, a leading space, `llm-x`, `model:`, a second `prompt=` and untracked prompt files are all refused now.
- **The Descartes binary is reproducible.** Two builds from the same commit give the same binary, and the step record names the commit and digest that ran each check.

**Tests:** 153 unit tests, and 20 tampering cases for the verifier, each refused with its own message. A clean paper repository still passes all of them.

**Effect on this paper:** no passing quote was broken by the stricter rules. Three claims are now refused for quoting raw HTML: Q007 (the Delaware statute), Q048 and Q084. They need a recipe for rendered web pages before they can be cited.

**Effect on Descartes's own claims:**
- **81 rows fail.** 72 lack the prompt field, 8 use `model:`, and 1 is a faithful quote that fails because pdftotext glued a footnote number onto a word ("profiles92").
- **I kept the word rule strict anyway.** A false failure is visible; a false pass is not.

**Decisions for you:**
1. **Merge the branch.** That means migrating those 81 rows and the Descartes loop's expected results, which needs the Descartes session.
2. **Make the check a gate.** Nothing runs `descartes check` on commit or in CI. Today's hooks run only another session's `seal.py`, and those files are that session's uncommitted work, so I didn't touch them.
3. **Set two parameters:** a minimum quote length, and whether a quote may run across a paragraph break.

**Still open:**
- **The review file isn't checked.** Its labels don't line up with the claims file: 24 claims have no review row and 20 review rows have no claim, because labels were split or renamed. Most of its "verbatim" context passages don't match their source exactly.
- **Rows aren't tied to steps.** Nothing checks which step produced each claim row.
- **Stored claims bypass the witness check.** Claims already in a store, rather than in a claims file, aren't checked at all.

# Open questions

Decisions and questions waiting on someone. Each has an owner, the context
needed to answer it, and what it blocks. When one is answered, move it to
**Answered** with the answer, who gave it, and the commit that acted on it.
Never delete an entry.

New questions come from the work itself and from `PASTEBIN.md`.

## Open

### Q1 · Who signs the datasets?
- **Status:** partly answered 2026-11-04. Sloane signs with her own key;
  `scripts/attest_datasets.py` builds the records. Still open: which key, the
  first signing run, and whether to sign commits.
- **Owner:** Sloane
- **Context:** Every corpus is hash-pinned and rebuilds byte-identical, but
  nothing is signed. The attestation protocol (`docs/contrapunctus-attest.md`:
  SSH Ed25519, `ssh-keygen -Y sign`, `verify.sh`) covers only the paper.
  `docs/praxis-standard.md` PS-3.7 says release signing is open because no key
  exists. Commits are unsigned.
- **Proposal:** each corpus gets a signing record (commit plus the hash of every
  output file), signed in a separate dataset namespace and checked by
  `verify.sh`. `DATASETS.md` shows the signers.
- **Options:** Sloane's key; an Ethical Capital dataset key; either one plus a
  build key. A build key proves only that this pipeline made these bytes; it
  does not mean anyone vouches for them. Separately: whether to sign commits.
- **Blocks:** the attestation part of the white paper's method for the corpora.

### Q2 · Approve the codebook v0.2 wording

# /// script

"""Render edition/REPORT.md, on the Praxis brand, as the one version: a PDF and the web page.

    uv run scripts/render_report.py -o /abs/path/anthropic-pbc-report.pdf      # PDF only (from-md)
    uv run scripts/render_report.py --bundle /abs/path/out                       # web page + PDF (bundle)

The report has one source (edition/REPORT.md) and one version; the PDF and the web page are two
renderings of it. `--bundle DIR` runs `./praxis report bundle` into DIR, outside the repository. Emitted
files are never committed: the bundle is attached to a release (Sloane, 2026-11-04). The Praxis web writer leaves local images out for now (caption only), so this
script links each chart by its path from the repository root (edition/*.svg), with its alt text, so
nothing is copied (Praxis PRINCIPLES.md P1). A bundle shows the charts only when served from a
checkout's root; a self-contained release bundle needs the Praxis writer fixed (separate session).

The PDF runs exactly `./praxis report from-md edition/REPORT.md --template research --publisher praxis -o OUT`
from the Praxis checkout beside this repository (../praxis, as for dag.py), with one addition. from-md
compiles with Typst's root at praxis/report_writer, and Typst refuses to read any file outside its root,

# History rewrite, 2026-11-04

Branch `ec-ai-corpus` was rewritten before its first push, to keep the
repository small (Praxis `PRINCIPLES.md` P1: permacomputing, keep everything as
small as possible; decided by Sloane, 2026-11-04).

## What was removed

Every earlier version of three earnings-call tables that carried full
transcript text: `corpus/earnings-calls/ai-paragraphs.parquet`,
`ai-windows.parquet` and `ai-questions.parquet`. The text came from
Yahoo-sourced transcripts (via the defeatbeta dataset). The repository now
commits ids, character offsets and hashes for these tables, and rebuilds the
text into the gitignored `.eccorpus/` from the pinned source
(`docs/earnings-call-ai-corpus.md` §2a). Quotes stay committed.

Removed blobs (3, 33.5 MB): `7d614c9e60d7`, `a398b70c08d8`, `fd47c7a36fd6`.
Packed repository: 113 MiB before, 82 MiB after (measured on a clean clone). The rest is mostly model-output parquets, Epoch CSVs and Wikipedia article text; see the audit below.

## What did not change

- The tree at the branch tip is identical before and after (`f0b6337`).
- Commits before the first parquet commit keep their hashes. That includes
  everything on `origin/main` (tip `f3358a7`) and edition v0 of the paper
  (`1afb042`).
- Only the three tables' old versions were removed; no other file changed.

## How

`git filter-repo` 2.47.0 (`uvx git-filter-repo==2.47.0`), run in a scratch
clone with `--strip-blobs-with-ids` and `--refs c64b7f3^..ec-ai-corpus`.
Limiting the range matters: the repository's initial commit carries a GitHub
signature, which filter-repo strips, so an unlimited run rewrites every commit.
The branch was then moved with `git update-ref`, guarded on the old tip, so no
working tree or index was touched.

## Old commit hashes

Documents written before the rewrite cite old hashes (for example the review
`docs/review-2026-11-04.md` cites `a83255b`, and Praxis `OPENQUESTIONS.md` cites
`23a4bb6`). Look them up here. Commit messages that named other commits were
rewritten by filter-repo; file contents were not.

| Old | New | Subject |
|---|---|---|
| `c64b7f3` | `b175c3c` | Add S&P 500 earnings-call AI corpus and BERT witness tooling |
| `71db655` | `0abdd1b` | Score earnings-call AI windows with two NLI witnesses on Modal |
| `05b5a9b` | `7646104` | Add exploratory BERTopic map of earnings-call AI windows |
| `04f7dc7` | `78c3cd4` | Document loss-evidence corpus: 13,570 events, 6,187 companies |
| `2df66c7` | `e98613a` | Add AI-as-risk time series, 12-month risk ranking, and verbatim quotes |
| `8ccfaa4` | `48e8ce5` | Add analyst-question intent analysis and human gold-set coder |
| `eb52f4c` | `5f67689` | Add Hacker News Anthropic and AI-security corpus (ids only), scored |
| `c2d8317` | `3cebe58` | Add Wikipedia AI-risk corpus and codebook coverage report |
| `5defccf` | `ac4e145` | Add pinned monthly CVE series with AI-credited counts |
| `e121992` | `34dc07e` | Add corpus roadmap: source policy, codebook v0.2 plan, open-web sources |
| `5005f7c` | `609fb04` | Add pinned snapshot of Epoch AI datasets as of 2026-11-04 |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Praxis report front door. Local rendering never grants publication authority."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys

import cli
from doc_inline import plain_text
from doc_model import iter_headings
from doc_parse import parse_document
from md_convert import parse_frontmatter

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SECTIONS = (
    'Bottom line', 'Decision-relevant facts', 'What could change the conclusion',
    'Analysis', 'Methods and limitations', 'Claims index', 'Sources index',
    'Revision and review record',
)


def check_report(path: Path) -> None:
    text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    md = parse_frontmatter(text)
    if md.template != 'research' or md.extra.get('presentation') != 'praxis':
        raise ValueError('New research needs template: research and presentation: praxis; use init or --legacy-layout for historical documents')
    doc = parse_document(text, slug=path.stem)
    from publisher_config import profile
    profile(doc.meta.publisher)
    headings = [plain_text(h.children).strip().casefold() for h in iter_headings(doc.blocks) if h.level == 2]
    required = [s.casefold() for s in SECTIONS]
    if headings != required:
        raise ValueError('Research sections must follow the Praxis standard: ' + ' → '.join(SECTIONS) + '. Use level-three headings for findings within them.')
    if not doc.meta.title or not doc.meta.author or not doc.meta.date:
        raise ValueError('Research needs title, author and date metadata')


def main(argv=None):
    argv = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
    try:
        if argv and argv[0] == 'slides':
            from slides import main as slides_main
            return slides_main(argv[1:])
        if argv and argv[0] == 'init':
            if len(argv) != 2:
                raise ValueError('Usage: praxis report init report.md')
            with Path(argv[1]).open('x', encoding='utf-8') as out:
                out.write((ROOT / 'design/research-template.md').read_text())
            return 0
        if argv and argv[0] == 'check':
            if len(argv) != 2:
                raise ValueError('Usage: praxis report check report.md')
            check_report(Path(argv[1]))
            print('PASS: research structure and metadata; evidence support and release authority require separate review')
            return 0
        legacy = '--legacy-layout' in argv
        if legacy:
            argv.remove('--legacy-layout')
        if not argv or argv == ['--help']:
            print('Praxis reports: init FILE | check FILE | compile | from-md | register | bundle | slides\n'
                  'Research uses the shared presentation standard. --legacy-layout retains historical ordering.\n'
                  'Bundles are local private review artifacts, not audience-filtered public exports.\n')

input.content: #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script # /// script # requires-python = ">=3.14" # dependencies = [] # /// """Render the working paper, on the Praxis brand, as the one version: a PDF and the web page. uv run scripts/render_report.py --descartes BIN -o /abs/path/anthropic-pbc.pdf # PDF only (from-md) uv run scripts/render_report.py --descartes BIN --bundle /abs/path/out # web page + PDF (bundle) The paper (docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md) has one source and one version; the PDF and the web page are two renderings of it. Emitted files are never committed: they are written outside the repository and attached to a release (Sloane, 2026-11-04). Every rendering ends with a generated appendix, "Verification chain", so the document carries its own evidence trail (Sloane, 2026-11-04). It is built when the document is built, never typed: - the result of running Descartes's article verifier (stage1/article.sh) on this repository now: manifest, recipe replay, and `descartes check` on the claims file, with failing claims by cause; - the steps that produced the claims (claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.steps.tsv); - the status of the verification-chain audit (the table in docs/audit-2026-11-04-verification-chain.md); - the Entire trails the repository cites (docs/trails.tsv, refreshed by docs/trails-refresh.sh). It names the paper's commit, whether the inputs had uncommitted changes, the Descartes checkout's commit and the binary's SHA-256. Nothing in it reads a clock: the document date is the date of the paper's last commit. The paper is ordered by its question, not by the Praxis research standard's eight sections, so it is rendered with Praxis's --legacy-layout. The front matter is added here, outside the repository, in a temporary copy; the paper itself carries none. from-md compiles with Typst's root at praxis/report_writer, and Typst refuses to read any file outside its root, so this script hands Typst each chart's bytes instead of its path, and passes the image's alt text to Typst's `alt`. The Praxis web writer leaves local images out for now (caption only), so the web page links each chart by its path from the repository root. No file in Praxis is changed. """ from __future__ import annotations import argparse import hashlib import html import os import re import subprocess import sys import tempfile from pathlib import Path ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent PAPER = ROOT / "docs" / "anthropic-contrapunctus.md" CLAIMS = "claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.tsv" STEPS = ROOT / "claims" / "anthropic-contrapunctus.steps.tsv" AUDIT = ROOT / "docs" / "audit-2026-11-04-verification-chain.md" TRAILS = ROOT / "docs" / "trails.tsv" INPUTS = ["docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md", CLAIMS, "claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.steps.tsv", "sources/MANIFEST.tsv", "derived/recipes.tsv", "prompts"] FIGURE = re.compile(r'#figure\(image\("([^"\\]+)"\)') IMAGE_MD = re.compile(r"^!\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)\s]+)\)\s*$", re.M) CHECK_LINE = re.compile(r"^FAIL\t([^:\t]+\.tsv):(\d+): (.*)$") def typst_str(s: str) -> str: return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"').replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\r", "\\r").replace("\t", "\\t") + '"' def chart(base: Path, src: str) -> Path: path = (base.parent / src).resolve() if path.suffix != ".svg" or not path.is_relative_to(ROOT) or not path.is_file(): raise ValueError(f"image {src!r}: need an SVG inside {ROOT}") return path def git(*args: str, cwd: Path = ROOT) -> str: return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip() def tsv_rows(path: Path) -> list[list[str]]: """Data rows of a TSV, comments and the header row dropped.""" rows = [line.split("\t") for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line and not line.startswith("#")] return rows[1:] def cell(s: str) -> str: return s.replace("|", "\\|").replace("\n", " ") def table(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str: out = ["| " + " | ".join(header) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(header)] out += ["| " + " | ".join(cell(c) for c in r) + " |" for r in rows] return "\n".join(out) def short(s: str) -> str: """Shorten every 64-hex digest to 12 characters for the page; full values stay in the records.""" return re.sub(r"\b([0-9a-f]{12})[0-9a-f]{52}\b", r"\1…", s) def labels_by_line(path: Path) -> dict[int, str]: return {n: line.split("\t", 1)[0] for n, line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1) if line and not line.startswith("#")} def verification_appendix(descartes: Path, descartes_root: Path) -> str: article = descartes_root / "stage1" / "article.sh" if not article.is_file(): raise SystemExit(f"{article} not found: the appendix needs Descartes's article verifier") env = {**os.environ, "DESCARTES": str(descartes)} run = subprocess.run(["sh", str(article), str(ROOT), CLAIMS], cwd=ROOT, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True) lines = run.stdout.splitlines() rederived = [l for l in lines if l.startswith("ok\tre-derived")] summary = next((l.split("\t")[2:] for l in lines if l.startswith("summary\t")), ["no summary"]) manifest = next((l.removeprefix("article: manifest").strip() for l in lines if l.startswith("article: manifest")), "?") prompts = next((l.removeprefix("article: prompts").strip() for l in lines if l.startswith("article: prompts")), "none named") labels = labels_by_line(ROOT / CLAIMS) causes: dict[str, list[str]] = {} other: list[str] = [] for l in lines: if not l.startswith("FAIL\t"): continue m = CHECK_LINE.match(l) if m and m.group(1) == CLAIMS: msg = m.group(3) if msg.endswith("has no surviving evidence"): continue # the consequence of the row failure already listed cause = re.sub(r'^(evidence \S+ is not a recipe output).*', r"\1", msg.split(': "')[0]) causes.setdefault(cause, []).append(labels.get(int(m.group(2)), f"line {m.group(2)}")) else: other.append(l.removeprefix("FAIL\t")) dirty = git("status", "--porcelain", "--", *INPUTS) head = git("rev-parse", "--short=12", "HEAD") d_head = git("rev-parse", "--short=12", "HEAD", cwd=descartes_root) d_dirty = git("status", "--porcelain", "--", "stage1", "src", "tools", cwd=descartes_root) sha = hashlib.sha256(descartes.read_bytes()).hexdigest() steps = [[r[0], r[1], short(r[3]) if len(r) > 3 else "", short(r[5]) if len(r) > 5 else "", r[6] if len(r) > 6 else ""] for r in tsv_rows(STEPS)] audit = [l for l in AUDIT.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l.startswith("| ")] trails = tsv_rows(TRAILS) parts = [ "### Appendix F. Verification chain (generated at build)", "", "*Built with the document from the records in the repository; nothing in this appendix is typed by hand. " f"Paper commit `{head}`{' with uncommitted changes to its inputs' if dirty else ''}; " f"Descartes checkout `{d_head}`{' with uncommitted changes' if d_dirty else ''}; " f"Descartes binary SHA-256 `{short(sha)}`. Digests are shortened here; full values are in the records.*", "", f"**Result: {'PASS' if run.returncode == 0 else 'FAIL'}.** The article verifier ran unsandboxed. " f"Manifest: {manifest}. Recipes: {len(rederived)} re-derived, byte-identical to the text the checks use. " f"Prompts: {prompts}. Claims: {', '.join(summary)}.", "", ] if causes: parts += ["**Failing claims, by cause.** A failure is a finding, never fitted to pass (AGENTS.md).", "", table(["Cause", "Claims"], [[c, ", ".join(ls)] for c, ls in causes.items()]), ""] if other: parts += ["**Other problems.**", ""] + [f"- {cell(o)}" for o in other] + [""] parts += [ "**Steps that produced the claims** (`claims/anthropic-contrapunctus.steps.tsv`).", "", table(["Step", "Kind", "Prompt", "Outputs", "Commit"], steps), "", "**Audit of the verification chain** (`docs/audit-2026-11-04-verification-chain.md`).", "", *audit, "", "**Trails** (Entire project et/ec1c; snapshot `docs/trails.tsv`).", "", table(["Trail", "Status", "Intent"], [[f"#{r[0]}", r[1], r[2]] for r in trails]), "", "Corrections to this paper are in §9, Errata.", "", ] return "\n".join(parts) def compose(paper: Path, appendix: str) -> str: text = paper.read_text(encoding="utf-8") lines = text.splitlines() if not lines or not lines[0].startswith("# "): raise ValueError("the paper must start with its '# ' title") title = lines[0][2:].strip() date = git("log", "-1", "--format=%cs", "--", paper.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()) front = "\n".join([ "---", f"title: {typst_str(title)}", 'author: "Sloane Ortel"', f'date: "{date}"', 'classification: "Working paper"', "template: research", "presentation: praxis", "publisher: praxis", "toc_depth: 0", "---", ""]) return front + "\n".join(lines[1:]) + "\n\n" + appendix + "\n" def main() -> int: ap = # The report as a build product

Status, 2026-11-04: the edition is one Praxis research report,
`edition/REPORT.md`, built by `scripts/build_edition.py` from
`edition/report.template.md` and rendered to PDF by the Praxis report writer.
The Marp deck (`DECK.md`, `deck/`) is retired: Marp needed Node and a headless
browser, and its styling was generic rather than the Praxis brand. The paper
template (edition v1 of the argument itself) is not built yet.

## Principle

The paper is not edited; it is **built**. An edition is a deterministic function
of one source commit and a few recorded parameters:

    edition = build(source commit, codebook version)

Rerunning the build at the same commit with the same parameters gives the same
bytes. The edition is then committed on top, so every edition names exactly the
code, data, codebook and prose it came from.

The **source commit** is the last commit that touched any build input (the
template, the build scripts, the codebook, `dag.lock.tsv` and every table the
build reads; `Build.inputs()` lists them), not HEAD. Committing the edition's
own outputs moves HEAD but changes no input, so the stamp and the generated
notice stay the same and `build_edition.py --check` passes on the edition
commit, in CI or anywhere else. The build already refuses to run when an input
is uncommitted or modified, so the source commit always describes the bytes the
build read. Any commit that changes an input (including a relock of unrelated
data, since `dag.lock.tsv` is an input) makes a new source commit, and
`--check` then fails until the edition is rebuilt.

# The report as a build product

Status, 2026-11-04: the edition is one Praxis research report,
`edition/REPORT.md`, built by `scripts/build_edition.py` from
`edition/report.template.md` and rendered to PDF by the Praxis report writer.
The Marp deck (`DECK.md`, `deck/`) is retired: Marp needed Node and a headless
browser, and its styling was generic rather than the Praxis brand. The paper
template (edition v1 of the argument itself) is not built yet.

## Principle

The paper is not edited; it is **built**. An edition is a deterministic function
of one source commit and a few recorded parameters:

    edition = build(source commit, codebook version)

Rerunning the build at the same commit with the same parameters gives the same
bytes. The edition is then committed on top, so every edition names exactly the
code, data, codebook and prose it came from.

The **source commit** is the last commit that touched any build input (the
template, the build scripts, the codebook, `dag.lock.tsv` and every table the
build reads; `Build.inputs()` lists them), not HEAD. Committing the edition's
own outputs moves HEAD but changes no input, so the stamp and the generated
notice stay the same and `build_edition.py --check` passes on the edition
commit, in CI or anywhere else. The build already refuses to run when an input
is uncommitted or modified, so the source commit always describes the bytes the
build read. Any commit that changes an input (including a relock of unrelated
data, since `dag.lock.tsv` is an input) makes a new source commit, and
`--check` then fails until the edition is rebuilt.

content.text:
The PDF is built, and it ends with a generated "Verification chain" appendix, Appendix F. Everything is committed and pushed. The appendix's headline result is **FAIL**: 74 claims pass and 22 still fail, every one of them listed with its cause.

**The PDF:** `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-srvo-dev-anthropic-pbc/c1e11076-829e-4b02-9641-6b48b095d475/scratchpad/render/anthropic-pbc-working-paper-5f76702.pdf`
- 28 pages, built from pushed commit `5f76702`. Two renders came out byte-identical.
- The document date is the paper's last commit date, not today's clock.

**What the appendix contains**, all produced at render time:
- **What built it:** the paper commit, the Descartes commit, and the SHA-256 of the binary that checked the claims.
- **A live verifier run:** 15 sources checked against the manifest, and 7 derived texts re-made and byte-identical.
- **The failing claims, grouped by cause:** three claims cite raw web pages (Q007, Q048, Q084), 19 quotes broken by PDF line breaks, and 4 quotes that occur twice in their source.
- **The step record:** which brief, by digest, produced which claims, at which commit.
- **The audit table:** each finding marked closed, partly closed or open.
- **The trails:** #25, #26 and #28. The appendix reads them from a committed snapshot, `docs/trails.tsv`, so rebuilding needs no Entire login. The snapshot holds only trails this repo cites, because the project's other trails have private titles.

**Every rendering does this now.** The render script (`scripts/render_report.py`) adds the appendix to any PDF or web page it builds from the paper, and AGENTS.md has a new rule saying so. The rule belongs in Praxis's producer contract too, so it covers every report. That file has another session's uncommitted edits, so I left it alone; it can go in once those land.

**Pushed:**
- **anthropic-pbc:** `ec-ai-corpus` is now on GitHub, 156 commits on top of `main`. Before pushing I confirmed that none of the blobs removed by the history rewrite is reachable, that no file is over 20 MB, and that the commits contain no credential patterns. Pull request link: https://github.com/srvo/anthropic-pbc/pull/new/ec-ai-corpus
- **Descartes:** `witness-prompt-digest` is pushed as a branch, not merged. The render needs that branch's `stage1/article.sh`.
- **Praxis:** the `ERRATA.md` commit is local only, because Praxis has no remote.

**Two loose ends:**
- **Page 1 caption.** The web-only figure gallery is left out of the PDF, but the paper's italic line "Figures are generated deterministically…" still prints with nothing under it. That's the paper's own text, so cutting it or keeping it is your call.
- **Release.** Emitted files go to a release rather than into the repo. I haven't created one; say so and I'll attach this PDF to a release on GitHub.

# Bug: quotes from HTML sources cannot be checked as published

**For:** Descartes (file in Forgejo, `EthicalCapital/monocloud` tracker, when a
Forgejo tool is available). **Found:** 2026-11-04, quote check of
`docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md` (`docs/quote-check-2026-11-04.md`).
**Reported by:** Sloane Ortel (via Claude). **Tracked:** Entire trail #25 (HTML recipe; descartes c8c8fa7 fixed static HTML) and trail #26 (PDF line breaks in the recipe).

## What happens

`descartes check` looks for a quotation in the pinned bytes. For a PDF there is
a recorded recipe (`pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk`), so the check runs against
the text. For HTML there is none, so the check runs against raw markup, and a
quotation that a reader sees as one sentence fails:

- **Markup splits sentences.** The SEC's S-1 HTML puts each printed line in its
  own positioned `<div>`, so any sentence longer than a line is split by tags.
  Correct, faithful quotations fail (review rows Q012, Q014, Q016, Q017).
- **Entities.** Curly apostrophes and dashes are written as `’` and the
  like, so the published characters are not the bytes.
- **Embedded duplicates.** Anthropic's web pages (Next.js) carry the body text
  twice, once rendered and once in an embedded JSON payload, so every sentence
  "occurs more than once" (Q048, Q084). The Constitution page had the same
  defect; it was fixed by pinning its PDF instead (`70a8866`), which is not
  available for every page.

### Same defect in PDF-derived text (added after the re-run, merge e36f74e)

The PDF recipe (`pdftotext -enc UTF-8 -nopgbrk`) keeps the printed line
breaks, so a quotation that runs across a printed line fails, although its
words are the source's: 18 claims (Constitution 11, Public Benefit Report 6,
RSP 1). The RSP's text also carries a zero-width space (U+200B) at each line
edge (982 in `derived/rsp-v3.4.txt`). A reader sees one sentence; the check
sees a newline. Whether a layout line break or a zero-width space matches a
space is a general rule for Descartes to decide once, for every source, not
something to settle quote by quote.

## What should happen

A quotation should be checked against what was published, as a reader saw it
on the date it was pinned. Requirement (Sloane): match what is published at
the time it is published.

## Proposed fix

A recorded, general recipe for HTML, in Descartes, exactly like `pdftotext` for
PDF: one standard HTML-to-text tool, the same arguments for every HTML source,
recorded with `descartes derive` and re-run by the loop byte-identically. It
must render only the visible document (not scripts or embedded data) and decode
entities. It must not be tuned to any source or quotation (AGENTS.md, "Checks
are not beaten"). Candidate tools to evaluate: `pandoc -t plain`, `w3m -dump`,
`lynx -dump`; choose by determinism across versions and by handling of
positioned blocks.

Until it is fixed, quotations from HTML sources stay `requote` or fail the
check, and that failure is reported, not worked around.

# Adversarial audit of the verification chain, 2026-11-04

Question (Sloane: "really lock this down"): how can a wrong or unverifiable
record pass the checks on this paper without any check failing? An LLM agent
audited the chain read-only and reproduced its cases on scratch copies. Each
finding is listed with what was done. Fixes are on the Descartes branch
`witness-prompt-digest` (commits 1a44f60, 8ef1b42, d828de8, e7b3cb6), **not
merged**: see "Decisions open".

State when audited: all 15 sources matched their BLAKE3 in
`sources/MANIFEST.tsv`, and all 7 `derived/*.txt` rebuilt byte-identical from
their recipes. Nothing had drifted; the gaps were that nothing would catch it.

| # | Finding (reproduced unless marked) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No gate runs `descartes check`: the hooks and CI run only `scripts/seal.py check`, so "passed" means an `ok` line read from a doc, not an exit code. | **Open.** The hook and workflow files belong to another session's uncommitted work. |
| 2 | The check trusts whatever bytes are on disk: an edited `derived/*.txt` or raw source passed; `descartes derive` records without running the tool; three rows quote raw HTML. | **Closed for articles** by `stage1/article.sh`: manifest bytes and BLAKE3, recipes replayed byte for byte, every derived file has a recipe, evidence must be a recipe output. Binding this inside `descartes check` itself is Entire trail #26. |
| 3 | A quote can pass without saying what the source says: no word boundary, no length floor, spans across headings and page numbers; a match inside an HTML comment passed. Live case Q022b dropped "necessarily". | **Partly closed.** Quotes match whole words only (d828de8). Q022b requoted (ceb603f). Raw HTML refused as evidence. **Open:** a minimum quote length, refusing spans across paragraph breaks, and storing context with the evidence. |
| 4 | The witness rule was easy to get past: `LLM:`, a leading space, `llm-x`, a second `prompt=`, and any file on disk under `prompts/`. | **Closed.** Witness kinds are a closed set (`human`, `llm`, `org`, `doi`, `arxiv`); exactly one `prompt=`; the digest must name a file committed at HEAD. **Open:** tying each row to the step that produced it. |
| 5 | Nothing checks the review or steps files: 24 claim labels have no review row and 20 review labels have no claim (split and renamed labels); review `context` is not verbatim in most rows. | **Open.** Needs a mechanical review check and a data fix of the review file. |
| 6 | A claim with one good and one fabricated evidence row printed `ok`. | **Closed.** Any failed row fails its claim (d828de8). |
| 7 | (Plausible) a claim with no evidence of its own passes on its parents alone. | **Open**, minor. |

Also found while fixing: `verify` does not check witness format on claim nodes
already in a store (only claims files are checked); a pdftotext footnote marker
glued to a word ("profiles92") makes a faithful quote fail the word-boundary
rule, a false failure kept on purpose (correctness first).

## Effect on this paper
`descartes check` (d828de8, binary sha256 `7cac773c…`, reproducible): 74 claims
ok, unchanged by the new rules. `stage1/article.sh`: inputs clean; Q007, Q048
and Q084 refused for citing raw HTML; both prompt digests match files at HEAD.

## Effect on Descartes's own claims
72 rows fail the prompt rule (interactive sessions and pasted transcripts, all
honest about having no prompt file), 8 fail as witness kind `model:`, and 1
faithful quote fails the word-boundary rule on a footnote marker.

## Decisions open (Sloane)
- Merge the branch, which requires migrating those Descartes rows and its loop's
  expected results (the Descartes owner).
- Run `descartes check` / `article.sh` as a gate in pre-commit and CI.
- A minimum quote length, and whether a quote may cross a paragraph break.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/srvo/.claude/skills/buzz-saw-editor

# Buzz Saw Editor

The best arguments are buzz saws: flat, sharp, and moving fast enough to cut through
previously solid thinking. Your job is to produce that. Not a nicer version of what
exists. A sharper version, or an honest accounting of why the argument cannot be made
sharp.

## The Standard

A buzz-saw argument has three properties:

1. **Logical chain.** Each premise follows from the prior one with no gaps assumed.
   If A → B → C → D, every arrow must be earned. Unstated premises are a liability.
2. **No needless words.** Every sentence carries weight or it gets cut. Hedges,
   filler, and elegant variation are not style — they are drag.
3. **Every claim is either proven or flagged.** Assertions require evidence. If
   the evidence is absent, say so and demand it.

## The Process

### Step 1: Extract the logical chain

Before editing a single word, map the argument:

> **Premise A:** [state it]
> **Premise B:** [state it]
> **∴ Conclusion C:** [state it]

Do this even if the original text is disorganized. Force the argument into explicit
if-then structure. This reveals:
- What's actually being claimed
- Which premises do real work
- Which steps are assumed rather than proven
- Whether the conclusion actually follows

If the argument can't be mapped this way, state that plainly: *"This piece does not
have a coherent logical chain. Here is what it needs to establish before it can make
this claim."*

### Step 2: Audit each premise

For every premise, ask:

| Question | If no → |
|----------|---------|
| Is this claim true? | Flag it. Provide counter-evidence if known. |
| Is this claim cited? | Mark it **[UNCITED]** and note what source is needed. |
| Does this premise follow from the prior one? | Mark the gap **[NON SEQUITUR]** and explain the missing step. |
| Is this premise doing real work in the chain? | If not, mark it **[DEAD WEIGHT]** — cut it. |
| Is this stated as precisely as it needs to be? | If not, mark it **[VAGUE]** and demand the precise version. |

Do not be charitable about gaps. A skeptical reader will find them. Better to find
them now.

### Step 3: Cut

Apply the blade to the prose:

- **Remove hedges:** "It could be argued that," "one might suggest," "perhaps,"
  "in some sense" — delete unless the uncertainty is philosophically earned.
- **Remove filler:** "It is worth noting that," "as mentioned above," "in order to,"
  "the fact that" — delete.
- **Remove passive voice** unless the agent is genuinely unknown or the passive
  is doing rhetorical work.
- **Remove elegant variation:** if you said "argument" in sentence one, don't say
  "thesis" in sentence three to avoid repetition. Repetition is clear. Variation
  is confusing.
- **Remove long lead-ins:** If a sentence takes more than 5 words to get to its
  subject, restructure it.
- **Cut any sentence that could be removed without losing a step in the chain.**

### Step 4: Deliver the output

Return three things:

**1. The logical chain** (explicit, numbered, if-then form)

**2. The annotated audit** — the original argument with inline flags:
- `[UNCITED]` — claim needs a source
- `[NON SEQUITUR]` — this doesn't follow from what came before; explain why
- `[DEAD WEIGHT]` — this sentence contributes nothing; mark for cutting
- `[VAGUE]` — state precisely what is being claimed
- `[FALSE PREMISE]` — this claim is wrong or contested; state the problem
- `[ASSUMED]` — this step was smuggled in without being argued

**3. The tightened version** — rewritten prose with cuts made and gaps called out
inline where the argument cannot yet be made because the premise isn't proven.
If the argument cannot be completed honestly, say so. Do not paper over gaps with
better-sounding language.

## Tone and stance

You are not a copy editor. You are a hostile-but-honest reviewer who has read
widely, believes almost nothing without evidence, and is constitutionally incapable
of being impressed by confident language that doesn't cash out. Treat every claim
as guilty until proven innocent.

But do not be gratuitously harsh. The goal is a sharper argument, not a demoralized
writer. When something works — when a premise is tight, a citation is solid, a
sentence is doing exactly what it should — say so. Precision about what's wrong
requires precision about what's right.

## Scope

This skill operates on any unit of written argument: a single paragraph, a memo,
an essay, a pitch, a research note, a policy brief, a tweet thread. The process
scales. A three-sentence argument gets the same logical-chain extraction as a
twenty-page white paper.

If the input is very long (>2,000 words), extract the logical chain from the whole
piece first and audit at the section level before going line-by-line.

## Large Documents (>2,000 words): Mandatory Subagent Dispatch

**Do not audit a large document in a single pass.** Single-pass audits of long documents
produce shallow flags and miss structural problems. Dispatch subagents.

### When to dispatch

- Any document >2,000 words
- Any multi-section report, white paper, or research document
- Any document with distinct regional/topical sections that can be reviewed independently

### How to dispatch

1. **Read the first 150 lines** to understand the document's structure and claimed argument.

2. **Identify natural section boundaries** — regional sections, topical chapters, major argument
   blocks. Each becomes one subagent scope.

3. **Dispatch one subagent per section** using the Task tool. Each subagent gets:
   - The editorial standard to work toward (quote the original if available; describe the
     target voice if not)
   - Explicit scope: which section/region/lines to review
   - The four deliverables: logical chain audit, buzz-saw flags, editorial rewrite of
     the section intro/synthesis, synthesis verdict
   - Any known problems to look for (e.g., "check if LGBTQ+ criminalization is treated
     with false equivalence")

4. **Always dispatch an intro/framing agent** as a separate task. The intro is where
   voice is established and arguments are stated. It fails differently than section content.

5. **Run all agents in parallel** (single message, multiple Task tool calls).

### Synthesizing results

When subagents return:
- Read each audit
- Identify cross-cutting problems (a hedging pattern that appears in every section is
  a systemic issue, not a section issue — name it as systemic)
- Produce a master synthesis: what are the 3-5 highest-leverage fixes for the whole document?
- Write the replacement intro/framing prose (or commission a final agent to do so if the
  intro needs substantial rewriting based on what the section audits revealed)

### Subagent prompt template

```
You are doing a buzz-saw editorial review of [section name].

## THE STANDARD YOU'RE EDITING TOWARD
[Quote or describe the target voice. Be specific — what does the original sound like?
What does it say directly that the current version hedges?]

## YOUR TASK
Read [file path] and focus on [section description with line numbers or headers].

Produce:
1. LOGICAL CHAIN AUDIT — what argument is this section making? If it's a data dump, say so.
2. BUZZ-SAW FLAGS — flag [DEAD WEIGHT], [VAGUE], [UNCITED], [HEDGING], [MISSING VOICE]
3. EDITORIAL REWRITE — 2-3 paragraph replacement intro/synthesis for this section
4. SYNTHESIS VERDICT — one paragraph: what's the actual argument, is it made clearly?
```

## When the argument cannot be saved

Sometimes an argument is broken at the foundation — a false premise, a non sequitur
that cannot be repaired, a conclusion that simply doesn't follow from anything.
In that case, say so directly:

> "This argument cannot be made in its current form because [X]. To make the case
> for [conclusion], you would need to establish [missing premises]. As written,
> the strongest supportable claim is [weaker true version]."

Producing a polished version of a broken argument is worse than useless — it
makes the flaws harder to see.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/srvo/.claude/plugins/synced/21d27081-2e23-4f4c-829b-5f4870dd16f6_915e03b7-ced5-4453-aba6-c97d1f5ae0b0/58da2c13-5ed4-4485-9625-fb87b369e6b4/skills/productivity/writing-for-agents

Reference for writing any document an agent consumes: a skill, an `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, a doc reached by a pointer. The packaging differs; the writing does not: the same levers make each one predictable, since the agent takes the same _process_ every run rather than producing the same output.

When the document you're writing is a skill, read [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md) for frontmatter, invocation choice, and router skills.

## Context pointers

A **context pointer** is a reference held in the agent's context that names some out-of-context material and encodes the condition for reaching it. A skill's description is one; a line in `AGENTS.md` naming a doc is the same object. The pointer's _wording_, not its target, decides when the agent reaches the material, and how reliably. A must-have target behind a weakly worded pointer is a variance bug: sharpen the wording first, and inline the material only if sharpening fails.

A pointer does two jobs: state what the material is, and list the **branches** that should trigger reaching it (a branch is a distinct case the document handles, so different runs take different paths through it). Every word of an always-loaded pointer costs on every turn, so it earns even harder pruning than the body:

- **Front-load the leading word**: the pointer is where it does its triggering work.
- **One trigger per branch.** Synonyms that rename a single branch are one branch written twice; collapse them and keep only genuinely distinct branches.
- **Cut identity the body already carries.**

## The two loads

Every document and pointer you add spends one of two budgets:

- **Context load** is the cost of always-loaded material on the agent's window: an `AGENTS.md` line, a skill description, anything sitting in context every turn, spending tokens and attention whether or not it fires.
- **Cognitive load** is the cost on the human: which documents exist and when to reach for each. The human is the index. Not a cost to minimise: it is the price of human agency; spend it where human judgement matters, remove it where it does not.

Material reached only through a pointer escapes context load at the price of the pointer's own line; material with no pointer at all rides entirely on cognitive load.

## Information hierarchy

A document is built from two content types: **steps** (the ordered actions the agent performs) and **reference** (definitions, rules, facts consulted on demand). The two mix freely: all steps (a recipe), all reference (a review's rules, this skill), or both. The core decision is where each piece sits on the **information hierarchy**, a ladder ranked by how immediately the agent needs the material:

1. **In-file step** is the primary tier: what the agent does, in order.
2. **In-file reference** is consulted on demand. Often a legitimately flat peer-set (every rule of a review on one rung), which is a fine arrangement, not a smell.
3. **Disclosed reference** is pushed out into a separate file, reached by a context pointer, loaded only when the pointer fires. Spans a sibling file in the same folder through fully external reference that lives anywhere and any document can point at.

Push too little down and the top bloats; push too much and you hide material the agent actually needs. That tension is the whole decision.

**Progressive disclosure** is the move down the ladder (out of the main file and behind a pointer) so the top stays legible. Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Branching is the cleanest disclosure test: inline what every branch needs, and push behind a pointer what only some branches reach. When a document has steps, in-file reference that should be disclosed buries them and turns attending to them into a coin-flip: a variance lever, not just a legibility one.

**Co-location** is the within-file companion: where the ladder decides _how far down_ a piece sits, co-location decides _what sits beside it_ once there. Keep a concept's definition, rules, and caveats under one heading rather than scattered, so reading one part brings its neighbours with it. The test: the document should read like documentation written for the agent. Grouped material reads that way; scattered material does not. (Distinct from duplication: that repeats one meaning in two places; scattering fragments one meaning across many.)

**Sprawl** is the failure mode here: a document simply too long, even when every line is live and unique. Attention thins across the excess, and every extra line is one more to keep relevant. The cure is the ladder: disclose reference behind pointers, and split by branch or sequence so each path carries only what it needs.

## Steps and completion criteria

Every step ends on a **completion criterion**, the condition that tells the agent the work is done. Two properties make it a lever:

- **Clarity**: can the agent tell done from not-done? A vague bound ("understanding reached") invites **premature completion**: ending the step before it is genuinely done, attention slipping to _being done_. The visible steps still ahead (the **post-completion steps**) supply the pull; the criterion's clarity is the resistance. Defend in order: **sharpen the bound first** (local and cheap); only if it is irreducibly fuzzy _and_ you observe the rush, hide the later steps by splitting the sequence. Hiding only works across a real context boundary (a hand-off or a subagent dispatch; an inline call leaves the later steps in context and clears nothing).
- **Demand**: how much it requires. "Every modified model accounted for" forces thorough work where "produce a change list" does not. Demand drives **legwork** (the digging the agent does within the work, latent in the wording rather than written as its own step), and it is not step-bound: "every rule applied" binds a body of flat reference just as "every step done" binds a sequence, which is how an all-reference document still carries an exhaustiveness bar.

The strongest criteria are both checkable and exhaustive.

## When to split

Splitting one document into two spends one of the two loads, so split only when the cut earns it:

- **By sequence**: split a run of steps where the post-completion steps tempt the agent to rush the one in front of it. Keeping them out of view drives more legwork on the current task. Beware the reverse: merging sequences exposes each step's later steps to what follows, inviting premature completion.
- **By invocation**, skill-specific: see [`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`](SKILL-MECHANICS.md).

## Leading words

A **leading word** is a compact concept already living in the model's pretraining that the agent thinks with while running the document (_lesson_, _fog of war_, _tracer bullets_). Repeated as a token, never as a sentence, it accumulates a distributed definition and anchors a whole region of behaviour in the fewest tokens, by recruiting priors the model already holds. Coining your own works if you define it clearly, but a made-up word recruits no priors: you pay in definition tokens what a pretrained word gives free; reach for an existing word first.

It anchors twice. In the body, _execution_: the agent reaches for the same behaviour every time the word appears, and inside flat reference it focuses attention on a class of thing to look for. In a pointer, _invocation_: when the same word lives in your prompts, your docs, and your codebase, the agent links that shared language to the material and reaches it more reliably.

Hunt for opportunities to refactor with leading words. A triad spelled out at three sites, a pointer spending a sentence to gesture at one idea. Each is a passage begging to collapse into a single token:

- "fast, deterministic, low-overhead" → _tight_ (a _tight_ loop).
- "a loop you believe in" → _red_, turning a fuzzy gate into a binary observable state (the loop goes _red_ on the bug, or it doesn't).

You win twice: fewer tokens, and a sharper hook for the agent to hang its thinking on. Assume every document is carrying restatements that leading words retire. Go find them.

**Negation** is the failure mode beside this lever: steering by prohibition drags the forbidden behaviour into context and makes it _more_ available, not less. _Don't think of an elephant_, and the elephant is all there is; the negation is a weak modifier the strongly-activated concept overruns, so the ban half-reads as an instruction to do the thing. Prompt the **positive**: state the target behaviour ("write one-line comments") so the banned one is never spoken. A prohibition earns its place only as a hard guardrail you cannot phrase positively; even then, pair it with the positive target so attention lands on what to do.

## Pruning

- Keep each meaning in a **single source of truth**: one authoritative place, so changing the behaviour is a one-place edit. **Duplication** (the same meaning in more than one place) costs maintenance and tokens, and inflates a meaning's prominence on the ladder past its real rank. (The accidental inverse of a leading word, which repeats a token on purpose, never the meaning.)
- The **environment** is a source of truth too (`package.json` scripts, config files, the directory layout, `--help` output), and a document that restates it is a **cache**: a copy of a lookup, earning its load only when the lookup is expensive. Cache what the agent cannot find by looking: the unwritten convention, the reason behind a choice, the gotcha no config confesses. Leave the one-file, one-command lookups to the environment, where they cannot go stale.
- Check every line for **relevance**: does it still bear on what the document does? A line loses relevance by never bearing on the task (mere exposition, or a branch that should be disclosed) or by going stale as the behaviour or world it describes changes. Shorter documents are easier to keep relevant. Without a pruning discipline the default fate is **sediment**: stale layers that settle because adding feels safe and removing feels risky, until you must core down through them to find what is still live.
- Hunt **no-ops** sentence by sentence: an instruction the model already obeys by default pays load to say nothing. The test (does it change behaviour versus the default?) is model-relative, not reader-relative: two people disagreeing about a no-op disagree about the default, and settle it by running the document, not by debate. When a sentence fails, delete the whole sentence rather than trim words from it. The test also grades leading words: a word too weak to beat the default (_be thorough_ when the agent is already thorough-ish) is a no-op, and the fix is a stronger word (_relentless_), not a different technique.

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
  One exception, legend kept: the tall segmented bar (*Figures* in `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`).
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

# Buzz Saw Editor

sharp.

## The Standard

A buzz-saw argument has three properties:

1. **Logical chain.** Each premise follows from the prior one with no gaps assumed.
   If A → B → C → D, every arrow must be earned. Unstated premises are a liability.
2. **No needless words.** Every sentence carries weight or it gets cut. Hedges,
   filler, and elegant variation are not style — they are drag.
3. **Every claim is either proven or flagged.** Assertions require evidence. If
   the evidence is absent, say so and demand it.

### Step 1: Extract the logical chain

Before editing a single word, map the argument:

> **Premise A:** [state it]
> **Premise B:** [state it]
> **∴ Conclusion C:** [state it]

Do this even if the original text is disorganized. Force the argument into explicit
if-then structure. This reveals:
- What's actually being claimed
- Which premises do real work
- Which steps are assumed rather than proven
- Whether the conclusion actually follows

If the argument can't be mapped this way, state that plainly: *"This piece does not
have a coherent logical chain. Here is what it needs to establish before it can make
this claim."*

For every premise, ask:

| Question | If no → |
|----------|---------|
| Is this claim true? | Flag it. Provide counter-evidence if known. |
| Is this claim cited? | Mark it **[UNCITED]** and note what source is needed. |
| Does this premise follow from the prior one? | Mark the gap **[NON SEQUITUR]** and explain the missing step. |
| Is this premise doing real work in the chain? | If not, mark it **[DEAD WEIGHT]** — cut it. |
| Is this stated as precisely as it needs to be? | If not, mark it **[VAGUE]** and demand the precise version. |

Do not be charitable about gaps. A skeptical reader will find them. Better to find
them now.

Apply the blade to the prose:

- **Remove hedges:** "It could be argued that," "one might suggest," "perhaps,"
  "in some sense" — delete unless the uncertainty is philosophically earned.
- **Remove filler:** "It is worth noting that," "as mentioned above," "in order to,"

  is doing rhetorical work.

   - The editorial standard to work toward (quote the original if available; describe the

```
Read [file path] and focus on [section description with line numbers or headers].

Produce:
1. LOGICAL CHAIN AUDIT — what argument is this section making? If it's a data dump, say so.
2. BUZZ-SAW FLAGS — flag [DEAD WEIGHT], [VAGUE], [UNCITED], [HEDGING], [MISSING VOICE]
3. EDITORIAL REWRITE — 2-3 paragraph replacement intro/synthesis for this section
4. SYNTHESIS VERDICT — one paragraph: what's the actual argument, is it made clearly?
```

## When the argument cannot be saved

Sometimes an argument is broken at the foundation — a false premise, a non sequitur
that cannot be repaired, a conclusion that simply doesn't follow from anything.
In that case, say so directly:

> "This argument cannot be made in its current form because [X]. To make the case
> for [conclusion], you would need to establish [missing premises]. As written,
> the strongest supportable claim is [weaker true version]."

Producing a polished version of a broken argument is worse than useless — it
makes the flaws harder to see.


ARGUMENTS: The "Draft opening argument (step 0)" blockquote and the "Draft order" list in /Users/srvo/dev/anthropic-pbc/docs/plan-unified-report.md. Tighten in place; keep every factual claim traceable to docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md and add no new facts or numbers.
